title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
四川鄉試録序
嘉靖丁酉歲當大比巡按四
川監察御史金〔燦〕奉
命而來殫心事事以貢院隘弗稱
乃相地量工屬有司恢拓之
於是垣屋煥然一新比司監
臨秉公貞度用罔弗臧維時
===
巡撫右副都御史張〔翰〕惟文
教是崇士類丕振先是春二
月巡按監察御史陸〔琳〕謀于
藩臬長貳預聘〔珠〕暨教諭劉
〔邦采〕典試事教諭舒〔文明〕坑
〔進良〕胡〔乾〕沈〔良〕呂〔調音〕訓導
鄭〔時暢〕同典試事咸如期至
punctuated:
四川鄉試録序

嘉靖丁酉歲，當大比，巡按四川監察御史金〔燦〕奉命而來，殫心事事。以貢院隘弗稱，乃相地量工，屬有司恢拓之。於是垣屋煥然一新。比司監臨，秉公貞度，用罔弗臧。維時，巡撫右副都御史張〔翰〕惟文教是崇，士類丕振。先是，春二月，巡按監察御史陸〔琳〕謀于藩臬長貳，預聘〔珠〕暨教諭劉〔邦采〕典試事，教諭舒〔文明〕、坑〔進良〕、胡〔乾〕、沈〔良〕、呂〔調音〕、訓導鄭〔時暢〕同典試事，咸如期至。
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Sichuan Provincial Examination

In the dingyou year of Jiajing [1537], when the triennial examination was due, Jin Can, Regional Inspector of Sichuan and Investigating Censor, arrived under imperial orders and devoted himself wholeheartedly to every matter. Finding the examination compound cramped and inadequate, he surveyed the site, assessed the work required, and directed the responsible officials to enlarge it. Its walls and buildings were thus entirely renewed. When he undertook the duties of Supervising Official, he acted impartially and maintained upright standards, so that everything was properly managed. At this time, Zhang Han, Grand Coordinator and Right Vice Censor-in-chief, placed the highest value on literary education, greatly invigorating the scholars.

Earlier, in the second month of spring, Lu Lin, Regional Inspector and Investigating Censor, consulted the chief and deputy officials of the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions. They invited me, Zhu [surname not supplied], and Liu Bangcai, a School Instructor, in advance to serve as Examiners. School Instructors Shu Wenming, Keng Jinliang [surname uncertain: 坑, ?], Hu Qian, Shen Liang, and Lü Tiaoyin [given name uncertain: 調音, ?], together with Assistant Instructor Zheng Shichang, were to serve as Associate Examiners. All arrived as scheduled.

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
逮入院提調則布政使司左
布政使張〔鉞〕右叅政李〔中〕監
試則按察司按察使胡〔宗明〕
僉事李〔淏〕其防範於外則右
布政使林〔豫〕右叅政劉〔勲〕右
叅議李〔瑜〕副使朱〔良〕朱〔紈〕都
〔世家〕歐陽〔必進〕胡〔仲謨〕僉事
===
段〔續〕薛〔甲〕蔣〔信〕都指揮僉事
芮〔恩〕鄧〔斌〕亦罔不旣厥心焉
御史〔爕〕乃誓於衆曰嗟乎茲
舉也多士嚮用之始也而予
與諸司以人事
君之義也予固惕厲厥衷矣諸司
其用勗諸衆曰諸乃合提學
punctuated:
逮入院，提調則布政使司左布政使張〔鉞〕、右叅政李〔中〕；監試則按察司按察使胡〔宗明〕、僉事李〔淏〕。其防範於外，則右布政使林〔豫〕、右叅政劉〔勲〕、右叅議李〔瑜〕、副使朱〔良〕、朱〔紈〕、都〔世家〕、歐陽〔必進〕、胡〔仲謨〕、僉事段〔續〕、薛〔甲〕、蔣〔信〕、都指揮僉事芮〔恩〕、鄧〔斌〕，亦罔不旣厥心焉。
御史〔爕〕乃誓於衆曰：「嗟乎！茲舉也，多士嚮用之始也，而予與諸司以人事君之義也。予固惕厲厥衷矣，諸司其用勗諸！」衆曰：「諸乃合提學
translation_en:
When they entered the examination compound, the Proctors were Zhang Yue, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, and Li Zhong, Right Vice Administration Commissioner. Supervising the examination were Hu Zongming, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner, and Li Hao, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner. Responsible for security outside were Lin Yu, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner; Liu Xun, Right Vice Administration Commissioner; Li Yu, Right Assistant Administration Commissioner; Zhu Liang, Zhu Wan, Du Shijia, Ouyang Bijin, and Hu Zhongmo, Vice Surveillance Commissioners; Duan Xu, Xue Jia, and Jiang Xin, Assistant Surveillance Commissioners; and Rui En and Deng Bin, Assistant Regional Military Commissioners. They too all devoted themselves fully to their duties.
The censor Xie then solemnly charged the assembled officials, saying: “Ah! This examination marks the beginning of these scholars’ advancement toward employment. For me and the officials of the various offices, it also fulfills our duty to serve the sovereign by providing him with worthy men. I have indeed maintained vigilance and rigor in my heart. May you officials likewise exert yourselves!” The assembled officials said: “We then brought together [?] the official supervising education …

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
副使阮〔朝東〕所校士三試之
舉其良錄其文之粹者以
獻
珠當序諸首乃拜手稽首言曰
於乎盛哉嘗聞蜀多文士乃
今見之厥有由矣仰惟
皇上建極錫福禮備樂和是以天
人協應
===
前星炳燿麟趾振振臣工胥慶
而多士用興實百代之景運
也矧是歲蜀以稔稱民用忻
忻然夫百穀用成俊民用章
洪範之休徵也時將鎖院偶
值風雨執事者慮焉至期天
乃開霽三試如之諸士於是
punctuated:
副使阮〔朝東〕所校士，三試之，舉其良，錄其文之粹者以獻。」
珠當序諸首，乃拜手稽首言曰：「於乎，盛哉！嘗聞蜀多文士，乃今見之，厥有由矣。仰惟皇上建極錫福，禮備樂和，是以天人協應，前星炳燿，麟趾振振，臣工胥慶，而多士用興，實百代之景運也。矧是歲蜀以稔稱，民用忻忻然。夫百穀用成，俊民用章，洪範之休徵也。時將鎖院，偶值風雨，執事者慮焉。至期，天乃開霽，三試如之。諸士於是
translation_en:
…the candidates assessed by Vice Commissioner Ruan Chaodong: examine them in three sessions, select the best among them, and transcribe the finest of their compositions for presentation.”
Zhu, charged with placing a preface at the beginning, thereupon bowed with clasped hands, prostrated himself, and said: “Ah, how splendid! I have long heard that Shu abounds in men of literary accomplishment; now I have seen this myself. There is a reason for it. Reverently considering how His Majesty establishes the supreme standard and bestows blessings, with ritual fully observed and music harmonious, Heaven and humanity respond in accord. The Foremost Star shines brightly, and the qilin’s feet signify flourishing imperial offspring. All officials rejoice together, and the many scholars rise to prominence. Truly this is an auspicious age such as comes once in a hundred generations! Moreover, this year Shu is reported to have a plentiful harvest, and the people are filled with joy. That all grains ripen and men of outstanding ability become manifest accords with the favorable signs in the ‘Great Plan’ chapter of the Book of Documents. Just as the examination compound was about to be locked, wind and rain happened to arrive, causing those administering the examination concern. When the appointed time came, however, the sky cleared; it was so for all three sessions. The candidates thereupon …

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
乎馨其所長矣〔珠〕乃作而
嘆曰奇哉得無有名世之士
出乎其間與其惟我
皇上德教之隆明良之會天實相
之而山川亦效靈與固宜其
人文之盛如此也是故吾得
而縱觀之屹屹乎爾矣若岷
===
峨之厚而重也可以知其德
焉洋洋乎爾矣若江漢之沛
而汞也可以知其才焉穆穆
乎爾矣若陸海之宏而廣也
可以知其量焉惟德可以貞
俗惟才可以經國惟量可以
任重具玆美也則人文之所
punctuated: 乎馨其所長矣。〔珠〕乃作而嘆曰：「奇哉！得無有名世之士出乎其間與？其惟我皇上德教之隆，明良之會，天實相之，而山川亦效靈與？固宜其人文之盛如此也。」是故吾得而縱觀之：屹屹乎爾矣，若岷峨之厚而重也，可以知其德焉；洋洋乎爾矣，若江漢之沛而汞也，可以知其才焉；穆穆乎爾矣，若陸海之宏而廣也，可以知其量焉。惟德可以貞俗，惟才可以經國，惟量可以任重。具玆美也，則人文之所
translation_en: … brought forth their strengths [?]. Zhu 〔珠〕 then rose and exclaimed: “How extraordinary! Might there not emerge from among them men renowned in their age? Surely this is owing to the flourishing moral instruction of Our Emperor and the coming together of an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers: Heaven indeed assists them, and the mountains and rivers likewise manifest their numinous power! It is fitting indeed that literary and cultural accomplishment should flourish so greatly.” Thus I have been able to survey them fully. Towering aloft, like the substantial mass and weight of Mount Min and Mount Emei, they reveal their moral virtue. Abundant and expansive, like the surging waters of the Yangzi and Han rivers [?], they reveal their talent. Dignified and harmonious, like the vast breadth of the “land-sea,” the richly productive land, they reveal their capacity. Only virtue can rectify customs; only talent can order the state; only capacity can bear weighty responsibilities. Possessing these excellent qualities, they embody that whereby literary and cultural accomplishment…

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
以盛匪獨以藝而已槩蜀之
先賢若尹吉甫之忠勳范祖
禹之行業張敬夫之理學皆
有聞於世者也諸士其將追
美昔賢矣乎抑進而上之由
賢以希聖乎諸士涵泳
聖化積學以需用固皆有志者也
===
繼今觀
國之光筮仕且有日矣其毋怠
厥志務恒爾德全爾才充爾
量以徽爾文則庶無負於
聖明之教是固邦家之光而舉之
者亦與有光矣諸士其懋之
哉如其行罔顧言則舉匪其
punctuated:
以盛，匪獨以藝而已。槩蜀之先賢，若尹吉甫之忠勳、范祖禹之行業、張敬夫之理學，皆有聞於世者也。諸士其將追美昔賢矣乎？抑進而上之，由賢以希聖乎？諸士涵泳聖化，積學以需用，固皆有志者也。
繼今觀國之光，筮仕且有日矣。其毋怠厥志，務恒爾德，全爾才，充爾量，以徽爾文，則庶無負於聖明之教。是固邦家之光，而舉之者亦與有光矣。諸士其懋之哉！如其行罔顧言，則舉匪其
translation_en:
…through which cultural accomplishment flourishes; it does not rest on literary skill alone. Surveying the former worthies of Shu, we find the loyal service and achievements of Yin Jifu, the conduct and accomplishments of Fan Zuyu, and the learning concerning principle of Zhang Jingfu—all renowned in their time. Will you gentlemen emulate the excellence of those earlier worthies? Or will you advance still higher, proceeding from worthiness to aspire to sagehood? Immersed in the sage sovereign’s transforming influence, you have accumulated learning while awaiting employment; surely you are all men of resolve.
Henceforth you will behold the glory of the realm, and the day of your entry into official service is drawing near. Do not slacken in your resolve. Strive to keep your virtue constant, perfect your abilities, and enlarge your capacity, thereby bringing lustre to your literary accomplishment. Then you may hope not to fail the teachings of our sagely and enlightened sovereign. This will indeed bring glory to the state, and those who selected you will share in that glory. Exert yourselves, gentlemen! But if your conduct takes no account of your words, then those selected will not be the right…

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
人豈惟上負
明時下負主司而於鄉先賢亦有
愧焉也已諸士其慎之哉前
北工部右侍郎潘〔鑑〕歷於
蜀雅意造士工科都給事中
尢〔魯〕巡按監察御史李〔實〕工
部郎中侯〔問〕刑部員外郎楊
===
〔琇〕咸以事至樂觀厥成布政
使司左參議李〔克中〕按察司
僉事蔡〔復元〕張〔好古〕皆先時
入
賀今陞任副使龔〔亨〕右參議鄭
〔重〕僉事毛〔衢〕皆嘗旬宣振揚
克襄文教者也故併書之
punctuated:
人，豈惟上負明時，下負主司，而於鄉先賢亦有愧焉也已。諸士其慎之哉！
前北工部右侍郎潘〔鑑〕歷於蜀，雅意造士；工科都給事中尢〔魯〕、巡按監察御史李〔實〕、工部郎中侯〔問〕、刑部員外郎楊〔琇〕，咸以事至，樂觀厥成。布政使司左參議李〔克中〕、按察司僉事蔡〔復元〕、張〔好古〕，皆先時入賀。今陞任副使龔〔亨〕、右參議鄭〔重〕、僉事毛〔衢〕，皆嘗旬宣振揚，克襄文教者也，故併書之。
translation_en:
…men. Would they only fail the enlightened age above and the presiding examiners below? They would also have cause for shame before the earlier worthies of their native region. You gentlemen must take heed!
Pan Jian 潘鑑, former Right Vice Minister of Works at the northern capital, traveled through Sichuan and was deeply intent on cultivating scholars. You Lu 尢魯 [?], Chief Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for Works; Li Shi 李實, Regional Inspector; Hou Wen 侯問, Director in the Ministry of Works; and Yang Xiu 楊琇, Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice, all arrived on official business and were pleased to see the examination brought to a successful conclusion. Li Kezhong 李克中, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner, and Cai Fuyuan 蔡復元 and Zhang Haogu 張好古, Assistant Surveillance Commissioners, had all previously gone to court to offer congratulations. Gong Heng 龔亨, now promoted to Surveillance Vice Commissioner, Zheng Zhong 鄭重, Right Assistant Administration Commissioner, and Mao Qu 毛衢, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner, had all worked to disseminate imperial instructions and encourage worthy talent, successfully advancing literary education. I therefore record them here together.

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
江西南康府儒學教授黄珠
謹序
punctuated: 江西南康府儒學教授黄珠謹序。
translation_en: Preface respectfully composed by Huang Zhu, Instructor of the Confucian School of Nankang Prefecture, Jiangxi.

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
嘉靖十六年四川鄉試
監臨官
巡按四川監察御史金燦〔敷華浙江嘉興縣人 丙戌進士〕
提調官
四川等處承宣布政使司左布政使張鉞〔文輔江西安仁縣人 戊辰進士〕
四川等處承宣布政使司右參政李中〔子庸湖廣隨州籍江西 吉水縣人甲戌進士〕
監試官
四川等處提刑按察司按察使胡宗明〔汝誠直隸績溪縣人 丁丑進士〕
四川等處提刑按察司僉事李棨〔仲謙湖廣永興縣人 己丑進士〕
===
考試官
江西南康府儒學教授黃球〔琢卿福建莆田縣人 庚午貢士〕
福建建寧府壽寧縣儒學教諭劉邦采〔君亮江西安福縣人 戊子貢士〕
同考試官
湖廣寶慶府新化縣儒學教諭舒文明〔道化廣西賓州人 乙酉貢士〕
山西平陽府解州安邑縣儒學教諭狄進良〔汝率直隸安肅縣人 壬午貢士〕
湖廣武昌府蒲圻縣儒學教諭胡乾〔易知廣西臨桂縣人 辛卯貢士〕
直隸滁州全椒縣儒學教諭沈良〔貞夫福建莆田縣人 乙酉貢士〕
河南彰德府安陽縣儒學教諭呂調音〔宗夔湖廣江夏縣人 辛卯貢士〕
punctuated:
嘉靖十六年四川鄉試。

監臨官：
巡按四川監察御史金燦〔敷華，浙江嘉興縣人，丙戌進士〕。

提調官：
四川等處承宣布政使司左布政使張鉞〔文輔，江西安仁縣人，戊辰進士〕。
四川等處承宣布政使司右參政李中〔子庸，湖廣隨州籍，江西吉水縣人，甲戌進士〕。

監試官：
四川等處提刑按察司按察使胡宗明〔汝誠，直隸績溪縣人，丁丑進士〕。
四川等處提刑按察司僉事李棨〔仲謙，湖廣永興縣人，己丑進士〕。

考試官：
江西南康府儒學教授黃球〔琢卿，福建莆田縣人，庚午貢士〕。
福建建寧府壽寧縣儒學教諭劉邦采〔君亮，江西安福縣人，戊子貢士〕。

同考試官：
湖廣寶慶府新化縣儒學教諭舒文明〔道化，廣西賓州人，乙酉貢士〕。
山西平陽府解州安邑縣儒學教諭狄進良〔汝率，直隸安肅縣人，壬午貢士〕。
湖廣武昌府蒲圻縣儒學教諭胡乾〔易知，廣西臨桂縣人，辛卯貢士〕。
直隸滁州全椒縣儒學教諭沈良〔貞夫，福建莆田縣人，乙酉貢士〕。
河南彰德府安陽縣儒學教諭呂調音〔宗夔，湖廣江夏縣人，辛卯貢士〕。
translation_en:
Sichuan Provincial Examination, the sixteenth year of Jiajing (1537).

Supervising Official:
Jin Can, Regional Inspector of Sichuan and Investigating Censor, courtesy name Fuhua, was a native of Jiaxing County, Zhejiang, and a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the bingxu year.

Proctors:
Zhang Yue, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Sichuan, courtesy name Wenfu, was a native of Anren County, Jiangxi, and a metropolitan graduate of the wuchen year.
Li Zhong, Right Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner of Sichuan, courtesy name Ziyong, was registered in Suizhou, Huguang, and was a native of Jishui County, Jiangxi. He was a metropolitan graduate of the jiaxu year.

Examination Inspectors:
Hu Zongming, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner of Sichuan, courtesy name Rucheng, was a native of Jixi County in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili) and a metropolitan graduate of the dingchou year.
Li Qi, Assistant Provincial Surveillance Commissioner of Sichuan, courtesy name Zhongqian, was a native of Yongxing County, Huguang, and a metropolitan graduate of the jichou year.

Examiners:
Huang Qiu, Professor of the Confucian School of Nankang Prefecture, Jiangxi, courtesy name Zhuoqing, was a native of Putian County, Fujian, and a tribute scholar (gongshi) of the gengwu year.
Liu Bangcai, Instructor of the Confucian School of Shouning County, Jianning Prefecture, Fujian, courtesy name Junliang, was a native of Anfu County, Jiangxi, and a tribute scholar of the wuzi year.

Associate Examiners:
Shu Wenming, Instructor of the Confucian School of Xinhua County, Baoqing Prefecture, Huguang, courtesy name Daohua, was a native of Binzhou, Guangxi, and a tribute scholar of the yiyou year.
Di Jinliang, Instructor of the Confucian School of Anyi County, Jiezhou, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, courtesy name Rushuai, was a native of Ansu County, Zhili, and a tribute scholar of the renwu year.
Hu Qian, Instructor of the Confucian School of Puqi County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang, courtesy name Yizhi, was a native of Lingui County, Guangxi, and a tribute scholar of the xinmao year.
Shen Liang, Instructor of the Confucian School of Quanjiao County, Chuzhou, Zhili, courtesy name Zhenfu, was a native of Putian County, Fujian, and a tribute scholar of the yiyou year.
Lü Tiaoyin, Instructor of the Confucian School of Anyang County, Zhangde Prefecture, Henan, courtesy name Zongkui, was a native of Jiangxia County, Huguang, and a tribute scholar of the xinmao year.

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
江西南昌府進賢縣儒學訓導鄭時暘〔世芬福建閩縣人　乙酉貢士〕

江西南昌府進賢縣儒學訓導鄭時暘〔世芬，福建閩縣人，乙酉貢士〕。

四川布政司理問所理問鄭宏〔子容，江西金谿縣人，監生〕。

成都府同知陳輔〔朝中，浙江餘姚縣人，癸酉貢士〕。

保寧府巴州知州孫雲〔從龍，直隸崑山縣人，己丑進士〕。
邛州知州張紀〔世綱，雲南右衛官籍，壬午貢士〕。
成都府雙流縣知縣吳謨〔汝明，廣西宜山縣人，壬午貢士〕。
夔州府萬縣知縣龍雲〔澤之，雲南趙州人，壬午貢士〕。

彌封官：
保寧府同知王聘〔叔儒，陝西山陽縣籍，咸寧縣人，癸酉貢士〕。
translation_en:
Zheng Shiyang, Assistant Instructor in the Confucian School of Jinxian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, had the courtesy name Shifen. He was from Min County, Fujian, and was a tribute student (gongshi) of the yiyou year.

Officials responsible for printing examination papers:
Zheng Hong, Judicial Officer in the Judicial Office of the Sichuan Provincial Administration Commission, had the courtesy name Zirong. He was from Jinxi County, Jiangxi, and was a student of the Imperial University.
Shi Chang, Clerk in the Registry of the Sichuan Provincial Surveillance Commission, had the courtesy name Yuandao. He was from Hezhou, Shaanxi, and was a student of the Imperial University.

Officials responsible for collecting and keeping examination scripts:
Shao Jingji, Prefect of Chengdu, had the courtesy name Zhongcai. He was from Renhe County, Zhejiang, and was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the bingxu year.
Fu Haoli, Prefect of Chongqing, had the courtesy name Zichao. He was from Huating County in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili), and was a metropolitan graduate of the xinsi year.
Meng Qi, Prefect of Shunqing, had the courtesy name Shichang. He was from Xianning County, Shaanxi, and was a metropolitan graduate of the jiaxu year.

Officials responsible for receiving examination scripts:
Chen Fu, Vice Prefect of Chengdu, had the courtesy name Chaozhong. He was from Yuyao County, Zhejiang, and was a tribute student of the guiyou year.
Li Qi, Vice Prefect of Shunqing, had the courtesy name Wenfu. He was from Nanfeng County, Jiangxi, and was a metropolitan graduate of the jichou year.
Tao Lian, Prefectural Judge of Xuzhou, had the courtesy name Jingfu. He was registered in Qujing, Yunnan, was a native of Dangtu County, Zhili, and was a metropolitan graduate of the jichou year.
Sun Yun, Magistrate of Bazhou in Baoning Prefecture, had the courtesy name Conglong. He was from Kunshan County, Zhili, and was a metropolitan graduate of the jichou year.
Zhang Ji, Magistrate of Qiongzhou, had the courtesy name Shigang. He belonged to an officer household registered in the Yunnan Right Guard and was a tribute student of the renwu year.
Wu Mo, Magistrate of Shuangliu County in Chengdu Prefecture, had the courtesy name Ruming. He was from Yishan County, Guangxi, and was a tribute student of the renwu year.
Long Yun, Magistrate of Wan County in Kuizhou Prefecture, had the courtesy name Zezhi. He was from Zhaozhou, Yunnan, and was a tribute student of the renwu year.

Officials responsible for sealing candidates’ identifying information:
Wang Pin, Vice Prefect of Baoning, had the courtesy name Shuru. He was registered in Shanyang County, Shaanxi, was a native of Xianning County, and was a tribute student of the guiyou year.

punctuated:
順慶府通判沈淵〔時暹，浙江仁和縣人，辛酉貢士，大理衛籍〕。順慶府蓬州知州董毅〔惟遠，湖廣麻城縣人，庚午貢士〕。成都府成都縣知縣羅應兆〔子良，陝西洵陽縣人，壬午貢士〕。成都府漢州德陽縣知縣袁一貫〔道夫，湖廣醴陵縣人，己卯貢士〕。重慶府璧山縣知縣金白〔用晉，廣西臨桂縣人，壬午貢士〕。重慶府長壽縣知縣丁濬〔師禹，湖廣醴陵縣人，丙子貢士〕。

謄錄官：成都府推官徐鏊〔學何，貴州新添衛籍，直隸宣城縣人，丙子貢士〕。嘉定州知州高登〔應明，貴州威清衛籍，直隸儀真縣人，乙酉貢士〕。成都府綿州知州朱光霽〔克明，雲南蒙化衛官籍，直隸滁州人，癸酉貢士〕。重慶府巴縣知縣王瑞〔符賢，湖廣江夏縣人，壬午貢士〕。潼川州射洪縣知縣滕廷賓〔憑衡，湖廣邵陽縣人，丙子貢士〕。敘州府珙縣知縣何貫〔本一，江西德化縣人，乙酉貢士〕。成都府內江縣知縣李允簡〔可大，廣西融縣人，壬午貢士〕。

對讀官：敘州府同知王尚用〔賢卿，江西安福縣人，丙子貢士〕。成都府通判吳穩〔定之，江西安仁縣人，監生〕。重慶府涪州知州余光〔緝之，江西龍泉縣人，壬午貢士〕。
translation_en:
Shen Yuan, Assistant Prefect of Shunqing Prefecture, had the courtesy name Shixian and was a native of Renhe County, Zhejiang. He was a tribute scholar (gongshi) of the xinyou cycle and was registered in Dali Guard.

Dong Yi, Magistrate of Peng Department in Shunqing Prefecture, had the courtesy name Weiyuan and was a native of Macheng County, Huguang. He was a tribute scholar of the gengwu cycle.

Luo Yingzhao, Magistrate of Chengdu County in Chengdu Prefecture, had the courtesy name Ziliang and was a native of Xunyang County, Shaanxi. He was a tribute scholar of the renwu cycle.

Yuan Yiguan, Magistrate of Deyang County in Han Department, Chengdu Prefecture, had the courtesy name Daofu and was a native of Liling County, Huguang. He was a tribute scholar of the jimao cycle.

Jin Bai, Magistrate of Bishan County in Chongqing Prefecture, had the courtesy name Yongjin and was a native of Lingui County, Guangxi. He was a tribute scholar of the renwu cycle.

Ding Jun, Magistrate of Changshou County in Chongqing Prefecture, had the courtesy name Shiyu and was a native of Liling County, Huguang. He was a tribute scholar of the bingzi cycle.

Transcription Officials:

Xu Ao, Prefectural Judge of Chengdu Prefecture, had the courtesy name Xuehe. He was registered in Xintian Guard, Guizhou, was a native of Xuancheng County in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a tribute scholar of the bingzi cycle.

Gao Deng, Magistrate of Jiading Department, had the courtesy name Yingming. He was registered in Weiqing Guard, Guizhou, was a native of Yizhen County in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a tribute scholar of the yiyou cycle.

Zhu Guangji, Magistrate of Mian Department in Chengdu Prefecture, had the courtesy name Keming. He belonged to an officer household registered in Menghua Guard, Yunnan, was a native of Chu Department in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a tribute scholar of the guiyou cycle.

Wang Rui, Magistrate of Ba County in Chongqing Prefecture, had the courtesy name Fuxian and was a native of Jiangxia County, Huguang. He was a tribute scholar of the renwu cycle.

Teng Tingbin, Magistrate of Shehong County in Tongchuan Department, had the courtesy name Pingheng and was a native of Shaoyang County, Huguang. He was a tribute scholar of the bingzi cycle.

He Guan, Magistrate of Gong County in Xuzhou Prefecture, had the courtesy name Benyi and was a native of Dehua County, Jiangxi. He was a tribute scholar of the yiyou cycle.

Li Yunjian, Magistrate of Neijiang County in Chengdu Prefecture, had the courtesy name Keda and was a native of Rong County, Guangxi. He was a tribute scholar of the renwu cycle.

Collation Officials:

Wang Shangyong, Vice Prefect of Xuzhou Prefecture, had the courtesy name Xianqing and was a native of Anfu County, Jiangxi. He was a tribute scholar of the bingzi cycle.

Wu Wen, Assistant Prefect of Chengdu Prefecture, had the courtesy name Dingzhi and was a native of Anren County, Jiangxi. He was a student of the Directorate of Education (jiansheng).

Yu Guang, Magistrate of Fu Department in Chongqing Prefecture, had the courtesy name Jizhi and was a native of Longquan County, Jiangxi. He was a tribute scholar of the renwu cycle.

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
所謂立之斯立道之斯行綏之斯來動之
斯和
是故君子戒慎乎其所不睹恐懼乎其所
不聞
欲貴者人之同心也人人有貴於己者弗
思耳
易
天地以順動故日月不過而四時不忒聖
人以順動則刑罰清而民服豫之時義
===
大矣哉
貞吉升階大得志也
夫易聖人所以崇德而廣業也知崇禮卑
崇效天卑法地
日往則月來月往則日來日月相推而明
生焉寒往則暑來暑往則寒來寒暑相
推而歲成焉往者屈也來者信也屈信
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

所謂立之斯立，道之斯行，綏之斯來，動之斯和。

是故君子戒慎乎其所不睹，恐懼乎其所不聞。

欲貴者，人之同心也。人人有貴於己者，弗思耳。

易

天地以順動，故日月不過而四時不忒；聖人以順動，則刑罰清而民服。豫之時義大矣哉！

貞吉，升階，大得志也。

夫易，聖人所以崇德而廣業也。知崇禮卑，崇效天，卑法地。

日往則月來，月往則日來，日月相推而明生焉；寒往則暑來，暑往則寒來，寒暑相推而歲成焉。往者屈也，來者信也。屈信
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

As the saying goes: when he establishes them, they stand firm; when he guides them, they proceed; when he gives them peace, they come to him; when he stirs them, they become harmonious.

Therefore the gentleman is watchful and cautious about what he does not see, and apprehensive about what he does not hear.

The desire for honor is common to all people. Everyone possesses within himself something worthy of honor; they simply do not reflect upon it.

Book of Changes (Yi)

Heaven and earth move in accordance with what is fitting; thus the sun and moon do not stray from their courses, and the four seasons do not err. When the sage moves in accordance with what is fitting, punishments are just and clear, and the people submit. Great indeed is the significance of the time of Enthusiasm (Yu)!

“Perseverance brings good fortune; ascending the steps”: this means greatly fulfilling one's aspirations.

The Changes is that by which the sages exalt their virtue and broaden their undertakings. Knowledge is lofty; ritual propriety is lowly. The lofty emulates heaven; the lowly follows earth.

When the sun departs, the moon comes; when the moon departs, the sun comes. Sun and moon impel each other, and light is thereby produced. When cold departs, heat comes; when heat departs, cold comes. Cold and heat impel each other, and the year is thereby completed. Departing is contraction; coming is extension. Contraction and extension…

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄

相感而利生焉
書
乃聖乃神乃武乃文
惟皇上帝降衷于下民若有恒性克綏厥
猷惟后
建官惟賢位事惟能
弘敷五典式和民則爾身克正罔敢弗正
民心罔中惟爾之中
詩
===
匪東方則明月出之光
苾芬孝祀神嗜飲食卜爾百福如幾如式
既齊既稷既匡既敕永錫爾極時萬時
億
伴奐爾游矣優游爾休矣
時邁其邦昊天其子之實右序有周薄言
震之莫不震疊懷柔百神及河喬嶽允
王維后明昭有周式序在位載戢干戈
載櫜弓矢我求懿德肆于時夏允王保
punctuated:
相感而利生焉。

書
乃聖乃神，乃武乃文。
惟皇上帝降衷于下民，若有恒性；克綏厥猷，惟后。
建官惟賢，位事惟能。
弘敷五典，式和民則。爾身克正，罔敢弗正；民心罔中，惟爾之中。

詩
匪東方則明，月出之光。
苾芬孝祀，神嗜飲食。卜爾百福，如幾如式。既齊既稷，既匡既敕。永錫爾極，時萬時億。
伴奐爾游矣，優游爾休矣。
時邁其邦，昊天其子之。實右序有周，薄言震之，莫不震疊。懷柔百神，及河喬嶽。允王維后。明昭有周，式序在位。載戢干戈，載櫜弓矢。我求懿德，肆于時夏。允王保
translation_en:
…Their contraction and expansion act upon one another, and benefit arises from this.

Book of Documents

He was sagely and divinely perceptive, both martial and cultivated.

August Heaven on High bestows moral goodness upon the people below, who thereby possess a constant nature. It is the sovereign who can guide them securely along its proper course.

In establishing offices, choose only the worthy; in assigning duties, choose only the capable.

Widely disseminate the five teachings, thereby bringing the people's standards of conduct into harmony. If your own person is upright, none will dare to be otherwise. When the people's hearts lack the mean, they will take your mean as their guide.

Book of Odes

It is not the east growing light; it is the radiance of the rising moon.

Fragrant are the offerings made in filial sacrifice; the spirits relish the drink and food. They foretell a hundred blessings for you, just as you hope and according to the proper pattern. You are reverent and prompt, upright and diligent. May they forever bestow upon you the utmost blessing, in tens of thousands and hundreds of millions.

At ease and unhurried you roam; leisurely and contented you rest.

He makes his seasonal progress through his states; may Vast Heaven treat him as its son. Truly Heaven assists and sustains Zhou. He brings his awe to bear, and none fail to tremble. He conciliates the hundred spirits, including those of the Yellow River and the lofty mountains. Truly the king is sovereign. Brightly illustrious is Zhou, duly ordering those who hold office. Shields and dagger-axes are put away; bows and arrows are stored in their cases. We seek excellent virtue, to spread throughout these lands of Xia. Truly the king preserves…

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
小邾人于黃父〔昭公二十有五年〕
禮記
言父子君臣長幼之道合德音之致禮之
大者也
饗禘有樂而食嘗無樂陰陽之義也凡飲
養陽氣也凡食養陰氣也故春禘而秋
嘗春饗孤子秋食耆老其義一也而食
嘗無樂飲養陽氣也故有樂食養陰氣
也故無聲凡聲陽也
故天子之爲樂也以賞諸侯之有德者也
德盛而教尊五穀時熟然後賞之以樂
福者備也備者百順之名也無所不順者
之謂備言內盡於己而外順於道也
===
第貳場
論
誠者聖人之本
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢水旱責躬詔〔後元元年〕
punctuated:
小邾人于黃父。〔昭公二十有五年〕

禮記

言父子、君臣、長幼之道，合德音之致，禮之大者也。

饗禘有樂，而食嘗無樂，陰陽之義也。凡飲，養陽氣也；凡食，養陰氣也。故春禘而秋嘗，春饗孤子，秋食耆老，其義一也。而食嘗無樂，飲養陽氣也，故有樂；食養陰氣也，故無聲。凡聲，陽也。

故天子之爲樂也，以賞諸侯之有德者也。德盛而教尊，五穀時熟，然後賞之以樂。

福者，備也。備者，百順之名也。無所不順者之謂備，言內盡於己而外順於道也。

第貳場

論

誠者，聖人之本。

詔誥表〔內科一道〕

擬漢水旱責躬詔〔後元元年〕
translation_en:
…and men of Lesser Zhu, at Huangfu. 〔Twenty-fifth year of Duke Zhao.〕

Record of Rites (Liji)

To articulate the proper relations between father and son, ruler and minister, elder and younger, and to accord with the purport of the sounds of virtue: these are the great essentials of ritual.

That there is music at ceremonial drinking entertainments and the di sacrifice, but none at ceremonial meals and the chang sacrifice, expresses the principle of yin and yang. All drinking nourishes yang energy; all eating nourishes yin energy. Thus the di sacrifice is held in spring and the chang sacrifice in autumn; orphaned sons are entertained with drink in spring, and the aged are served meals in autumn. The principle is the same. Yet ceremonial meals and the chang sacrifice have no music. Drinking nourishes yang energy, and therefore has music; eating nourishes yin energy, and therefore has no sound. All sound belongs to yang.

Thus, when the Son of Heaven institutes music, he does so to reward those among the feudal lords who possess virtue. Only when their virtue flourishes, their moral instruction is honored, and the five grains ripen in their proper seasons does he reward them with music.

Blessing means completeness. Completeness is the term for accordance in every respect. To be in accordance in all things is called completeness. This means inwardly fulfilling one's own responsibilities and outwardly according with the Way.

Second Session

Discourse

Sincerity is the foundation of the sage.

Imperial Edicts, Proclamations, and Memorials 〔One question from among these [?].〕

Compose, in the voice of a Han emperor, an edict taking personal blame for floods and drought. 〔First year of Houyuan.〕

擬唐以馬周爲監察御史誥貞觀三年
擬宋以范仲淹參知政事富弼爲樞密副
使謝表慶暦三年
判語〔五條〕
出使不復命
市司評物價
不操練軍士
畧人畧賣人
造作不如法
===
第叁場
策五道
問郊社所以祀上帝禘嘗所以祀先國之
大禮也成周備矣是故祀各有其所有
其時有其儀不數不疏不混而無別者
其義何與後世若漢若唐若宋乃罔克
師古郊祀合祭于屋下廟制異室而同
堂則混焉且或疏焉或數焉不經甚矣
間有慕古之君議禮之臣又病於費□
punctuated:
擬唐以馬周爲監察御史誥，貞觀三年。
擬宋以范仲淹參知政事、富弼爲樞密副使謝表，慶暦三年。
判語〔五條〕
出使不復命。
市司評物價。
不操練軍士。
畧人、畧賣人。
造作不如法。

第叁場
策五道
問：郊社所以祀上帝，禘嘗所以祀先，國之大禮也，成周備矣。是故祀各有其所、有其時、有其儀，不數不疏，不混而無別者，其義何與？後世若漢、若唐、若宋，乃罔克師古，郊祀合祭于屋下，廟制異室而同堂，則混焉，且或疏焉，或數焉，不經甚矣。間有慕古之君、議禮之臣，又病於費□
translation_en:
Compose a proclamation in the manner of the Tang appointing Ma Zhou as Investigating Censor, dated the third year of Zhenguan (629).
Compose a memorial of thanks in the manner of the Song for the appointment of Fan Zhongyan as Vice Grand Councilor and Fu Bi as Military Affairs Vice Commissioner, dated the third year of Qingli (1043).

Legal judgments〔five items〕
Failure to report back upon completion of an official mission.
Assessment of commodity prices by the market office.
Failure to drill soldiers.
Abducting persons; abducting and selling persons.
Manufacturing or construction not in accordance with regulations.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions

Question: The suburban and soil-altar sacrifices serve to worship the Lord on High, and the di and chang sacrifices serve to worship the ancestors. These are the great rites of the state, and they were fully established under the Zhou. Thus each sacrifice had its own place, time, and ceremonial forms; they were neither too frequent nor too infrequent, nor were they conflated so that distinctions disappeared. What principles underlay this?

Later dynasties—the Han, Tang, and Song—failed to take antiquity as their model. They combined the suburban sacrifices under one roof, while their ancestral temples had separate chambers within a single hall. Thus distinctions were confused; moreover, some sacrifices were too infrequent and others too frequent. These practices departed greatly from the canonical norms. From time to time there were rulers who admired antiquity and ministers who deliberated on ritual, but they too were hampered by expense [?]…

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
不合竟莫能裁定惟因陋就簡而已可
慨也豈禮樂必有待而後行與洪惟我

而兩見者與

聖心所自得之妙與諸生佩服
punctuated:
不合，竟莫能裁定，惟因陋就簡而已，可慨也！豈禮樂必有待而後行與？洪惟我皇上，天縱聖學，履中正以建民極，心法之妙，直與文武周公曠世同符。所以饗帝饗親者，本旣懋矣，而於禮制每惓惓焉。於是乎首建圜丘、方澤以祀天地，續創昭穆群廟以祀先，嚴其所，酌其時，辨其儀，用以致敬致孝焉。是誠至明至備之制，其追配成周，亘古今而兩見者與？
大祀旣成，乃用敷言于天下。伏讀明詔，有曰：「郊所以祀天，廟所以祀先，其道一而已矣，未有不相關者也。」大哉言乎！其聖心所自得之妙與？諸生佩服
translation_en:
…they failed to agree, and in the end no one could reach a definitive settlement. They merely perpetuated inadequate arrangements and settled for simplicity. How lamentable! Must rites and music await the right circumstances before they can be put into practice? We reverently reflect that our Emperor, endowed by Heaven with sagely learning, follows the mean and uprightness to establish the highest standard for the people. The subtlety of his method of cultivating the mind accords directly with that of Kings Wen and Wu and the Duke of Zhou, despite the ages separating them. The foundation for his offerings to the Supreme Lord and his ancestors was already amply developed, yet he remained constantly attentive to ritual institutions. Thus he first established the Circular Mound and the Square Marsh to sacrifice to Heaven and Earth, and subsequently founded the ancestral temples arranged in zhao and mu order to sacrifice to his forebears. He strictly defined their locations, weighed their proper times, and distinguished their ceremonies, thereby expressing reverence and filial devotion. These are truly institutions of the utmost clarity and completeness. Do they not rival those of the Zhou at its height, constituting only the second such achievement in all history?
Once the great sacrificial arrangements were completed, he proclaimed his words throughout the realm. Reverently reading his illustrious edict, we find it says: “The suburban sacrifice serves to worship Heaven; the ancestral temple serves to worship one's forebears. Their Way is one and the same. They have never been unrelated.” How great these words are! Do they not express the subtle understanding that his sagely mind has attained for itself? You students have respectfully embraced…

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
彞章有日矣其亦知此禮相關之精義否與
其於
聖製之至明至備者亦能揄揚其萬一與其欲
陳之毋讓
問嘗聞天之立君本為民也古者人君之
治天下生養之地教斯存焉教之有素
舉之有時善治乃成周禮者周公致大
平之書措置規模徧布精密姑以一二
言之周制內有六鄉之法外有六遂之
===
法大司徒以鄉三物教萬民而賓興之
鄉大夫三年則大比攷其德行道藝而
興賢者能者鄉老及鄉大夫帥其吏與
其衆寡以禮禮賓之厥明鄉老及鄉大
夫群吏獻賢能之書于王王拜受之登
于天府內史貳之紫陽朱子曰比閭族
黨之法正周公建太平之基本其詳可
得聞與我
朝稽古定制酌用六典於天下州縣每百一
punctuated:
彞章有日矣，其亦知此禮相關之精義否與？其於聖製之至明至備者，亦能揄揚其萬一與？其欲陳之，毋讓。

問：嘗聞天之立君，本為民也。古者人君之治天下，生養之地，教斯存焉。教之有素，舉之有時，善治乃成。《周禮》者，周公致大平之書，措置規模，徧布精密。姑以一二言之：周制內有六鄉之法，外有六遂之法。大司徒以鄉三物教萬民，而賓興之。鄉大夫三年則大比，攷其德行道藝，而興賢者能者。鄉老及鄉大夫帥其吏與其衆寡，以禮禮賓之。厥明，鄉老及鄉大夫、群吏獻賢能之書于王，王拜受之，登于天府，內史貳之。紫陽朱子曰：「比閭族黨之法，正周公建太平之基本。」其詳可得聞與？我朝稽古定制，酌用六典，於天下州縣，每百一
translation_en:
…you have long been steeped in these established ordinances. Do you also understand the profound principle linking these rites? Can you extol even a ten-thousandth part of the supreme clarity and completeness of the institutions established by His Majesty? Set forth what you wish to say without holding back.

Question: We have heard that Heaven establishes rulers fundamentally for the sake of the people. When rulers in antiquity governed the realm, wherever the people lived and were nourished, instruction was also present. Instruction was provided consistently, and worthy men were recommended at appointed times; thus good government was achieved. The Rites of Zhou is the book in which the Duke of Zhou set out how to bring about great peace. Its arrangements and institutional framework are comprehensive, detailed, and precise. To mention just one or two examples: under the Zhou system, the inner territory was governed by the institutions of the six townships, and the outer territory by those of the six rural districts. The Grand Minister of Education instructed all the people in the three categories of township teaching and promoted worthy men by honoring them as guests. Every three years, the township grand masters conducted a grand evaluation, examining the people's virtue, conduct, learning, and skills, and recommended the worthy and capable. The township elders and township grand masters led their subordinate officers and the assembled people in ceremonially honoring those recommended as guests. The following morning, the township elders, township grand masters, and assembled officers presented the register of the worthy and capable to the king. The king bowed as he received it and deposited it in the Celestial Treasury; the Interior Scribe retained a duplicate. Master Zhu of Ziyang said: “The system of neighborhood units—the bi, lü, zu, and dang—was precisely the foundation upon which the Duke of Zhou established great peace.” May we hear its details? Our dynasty has consulted antiquity in establishing its institutions and selectively adopted the six administrative codes. Throughout the subprefectures and counties of the realm, for every hundred and …

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
十户爲一里十户爲一甲每甲有長又
製木鐸訓詞以警衆設學校之教以明
倫凡三年大比以興賢能其於周制果
相一與易曰易窮則變變則通通則久
時之義大矣哉諸生其悉言之以觀經
世之學
問古者一道德以同俗學術一也後世或
以質之所近爲學門户則衆矣宋明道
先生嘗言于朝曰方今人執私見家爲
===
異說支離經訓無復統一程夫子兄弟
倡道當時而士習猶有未一可見學之
不講聖人之憂也孔門之學萬世之統
一也列聖之傳至于吾夫子直指仁以
教人先儒云仁自夫子發之夫子贊易
發仁體矣孟氏得之而言之親切焉至
于有宋眞儒特起以繼往聖開來學爲
已任有謂仁者與物同體義禮知信皆
仁也又曰萬物之生意最可觀此元者
punctuated:
十户爲一里，十户爲一甲，每甲有長。又製木鐸訓詞以警衆，設學校之教以明倫。凡三年大比，以興賢能。其於周制果相一與？易曰：「易窮則變，變則通，通則久。」時之義大矣哉！諸生其悉言之，以觀經世之學。
問：古者一道德以同俗，學術一也。後世或以質之所近爲學，門户則衆矣。宋明道先生嘗言于朝曰：「方今人執私見，家爲異說，支離經訓，無復統一。」程夫子兄弟倡道當時，而士習猶有未一，可見學之不講，聖人之憂也。孔門之學，萬世之統一也。列聖之傳至于吾夫子，直指仁以教人。先儒云：「仁自夫子發之。」夫子贊易，發仁體矣；孟氏得之，而言之親切焉。至于有宋，眞儒特起，以繼往聖、開來學爲已任。有謂：「仁者與物同體，義禮知信皆仁也。」又曰：「萬物之生意最可觀，此元者
translation_en:
…[one hundred and] ten households constitute one li, and ten households constitute one jia, each jia having a head. Admonitory texts were also composed for proclamation with the wooden clapper to alert the populace, and instruction in schools was established to elucidate human relationships. Every three years a great examination is held to advance the worthy and capable. Does this indeed accord with the institutions of Zhou? The Book of Changes says: “When change reaches its limit, it transforms; through transformation it finds passage; through passage it endures.” Great indeed is the significance of timeliness! Let you students explain this fully, so that we may assess your learning in ordering the world.
Question: In antiquity, the Way and virtue were unified to bring customs into agreement: learning was one. In later ages, some pursued learning according to the inclinations of their natural dispositions, and schools of thought proliferated. Master Mingdao of the Song once addressed the court, saying: “Today each person clings to private views, and each school produces divergent doctrines. They fragment the teachings of the classics, and unity is no more.” The Cheng brothers, those masters, championed the Way in their day, yet scholars’ practices still lacked unity. This shows why failure to cultivate learning was a source of concern for the Sage. The learning of Confucius’s school provides unity for all ages. When the transmission of the successive sages reached our Master, he pointed directly to benevolence in teaching others. An earlier Confucian said: “It was the Master who brought benevolence to light.” In his elucidation of the Book of Changes, the Master revealed the essential nature of benevolence; Mengzi grasped it and spoke of it with intimate precision. With the advent of the Song, true Confucians arose preeminently, taking as their own responsibility the continuation of the sages of the past and the opening of learning for those to come. One said: “The benevolent form one body with all things; righteousness, ritual propriety, wisdom, and trustworthiness are all benevolence.” He also said: “The impulse toward life in the myriad things is most worthy of contemplation. This is what is meant by ‘the primal’…

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
善之長也有謂偏言則一事專言則包
四者又曰仁者天下之公善之本也有
謂禮儀三百威儀三千無一物而非仁
也有謂天地生生之理這箇動意未嘗
止息仁一也其所言不同如此可得聞
其旨與聖功之要自列聖以至孔門敬
之一字未之有改也孟氏則曰勿忘勿
助宋儒有以無欲爲學其於敬何如有
以循理爲敬有以主一爲敬有以畏爲
===
敬敬一也其所論不一如此可得聞其
說與夫仁人心也南軒張子曰惻隱之
心仁之端也於此求之則不差矣其於
諸儒之見何如南軒蜀產也爲孔門之
學也諸士子豈無興起者乎
問人君之職惟在於論相相得其人則君
心繇正國是繇定百工繇飭百度繇貞
宗社尊安夷狄賓服相之責重矣哉古
者惟其人而行其道不可尚矣有漢之
punctuated:
善之長也。有謂偏言則一事，專言則包四者；又曰仁者天下之公，善之本也。有謂禮儀三百，威儀三千，無一物而非仁也。有謂天地生生之理，這箇動意未嘗止息。仁一也，其所言不同如此，可得聞其旨與？聖功之要，自列聖以至孔門，敬之一字未之有改也。孟氏則曰勿忘勿助。宋儒有以無欲爲學，其於敬何如？有以循理爲敬，有以主一爲敬，有以畏爲敬。敬一也，其所論不一如此，可得聞其說與？夫仁，人心也。南軒張子曰：「惻隱之心，仁之端也。於此求之，則不差矣。」其於諸儒之見何如？南軒蜀產也，爲孔門之學也，諸士子豈無興起者乎？
問：人君之職，惟在於論相。相得其人，則君心繇正，國是繇定，百工繇飭，百度繇貞，宗社尊安，夷狄賓服。相之責重矣哉！古者惟其人而行其道，不可尚矣。有漢之
translation_en:
…the foremost of the virtues. One said that, spoken of in a restricted sense, benevolence is one particular thing, but spoken of comprehensively, it embraces all four virtues. He also said: “Benevolence is the impartiality of all under Heaven and the root of goodness.” One said: “Among the three hundred rules of ritual and the three thousand rules of deportment, there is nothing that is not benevolence.” One said: “It is the principle by which Heaven and Earth ceaselessly generate life; this impulse to activity never rests.” Benevolence is one, yet their statements differ in these ways. May we hear their purport? As for the essentials of attaining sagehood, from the succession of sages down to the school of Confucius, the single word ‘reverence’ has remained unchanged. Mengzi, however, said: “Neither forget nor help it along.” Among the Song Confucians, some made freedom from desire the basis of learning: how does this relate to reverence? Some defined reverence as following principle, some as concentrating on unity, and some as apprehensiveness. Reverence is one, yet their discussions differ in these ways. May we hear an explanation? Benevolence is the human heart. Master Zhang of Nanxuan said: “The heart of compassion is the beginning of benevolence. Seek it here, and you will not go astray.” How does this compare with the views of the other Confucian scholars? Nanxuan was a native of Shu and pursued the learning of Confucius’s school. Can there be none among you candidates who are inspired to follow him?
Question: The ruler’s duty lies solely in assessing and selecting his chief minister. If the right man is appointed, the ruler’s heart is thereby rectified, the guiding policies of the state settled, the officials brought into order, and all institutions set right; the ancestral temples and altars of state are honored and secure, and the Yi and Di submit as subjects. How weighty is the chief minister’s responsibility! In antiquity, the right men carried out the proper Way; their achievement could not be surpassed. As for those of the Han…

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
相史氏以蕭曹丙魏並稱或者又謂丙
非魏可並也有唐之相史氏以房杜姚
宋並稱或者又謂宋非姚可並也若夫
有宋之興時則有若曰韓曰范曰富曰
歐先後柄用天下同稱其功烈抑有優
劣否與劉元城謂最得宰相大體者惟
李沆與漢之魏相必有所指也外此豈
無可稱者與韓魏公論近世宰相獨許
裴晉公本朝惟師服王沂公必有所見
===
也外此豈無可數者與當司馬君實未
用之時天下屬望說者以爲才備規模
小歉後氏自擇相司馬以天下爲己任
遂以經綸大猷斯時澤被萬民遠服戎
狄旋乾轉坤之功真不誣也豈知人果
難耶抑亦有所未盡耶學者論其世擬
諸道可不知所以求其極則矣乎先儒
有云學必以聖人爲至志在天下必以
宰相事業自期降此寧足道乎
punctuated: 相，史氏以蕭、曹、丙、魏並稱，或者又謂丙非魏可並也。有唐之相，史氏以房、杜、姚、宋並稱，或者又謂宋非姚可並也。若夫有宋之興，時則有若曰韓、曰范、曰富、曰歐，先後柄用，天下同稱其功烈，抑有優劣否與？劉元城謂最得宰相大體者，惟李沆與漢之魏相，必有所指也。外此豈無可稱者與？韓魏公論近世宰相，獨許裴晉公，本朝惟師服王沂公，必有所見也。外此豈無可數者與？當司馬君實未用之時，天下屬望，說者以爲才備，規模小歉。後氏自擇相司馬，以天下爲己任，遂以經綸大猷。斯時澤被萬民，遠服戎狄，旋乾轉坤之功，真不誣也。豈知人果難耶？抑亦有所未盡耶？學者論其世，擬諸道，可不知所以求其極則矣乎？先儒有云：「學必以聖人爲至，志在天下，必以宰相事業自期。」降此寧足道乎？
translation_en:
…chancellors, historians name Xiao He, Cao Shen, Bing Ji, and Wei Xiang together, yet some maintain that Bing Ji cannot be ranked alongside Wei Xiang. Among the Tang chancellors, historians name Fang Xuanling, Du Ruhui, Yao Chong, and Song Jing together, yet some maintain that Song Jing cannot be ranked alongside Yao Chong. With the rise of the Song, there were such men as Han Qi, Fan Zhongyan, Fu Bi, and Ouyang Xiu, who successively wielded power. All under Heaven alike acclaimed their achievements; nevertheless, were there differences in their merits? Liu Yuancheng said that only Li Hang and Wei Xiang of the Han best grasped the essential principles of the chancellorship. He must have had something particular in mind. Yet were there none besides these worthy of praise? In discussing chancellors of more recent times, Han Qi, Duke of Wei, approved only of Pei Du, Duke of Jin; among those of his own dynasty, he revered only Wang Zeng, Duke of Yi, as his model. He must have had grounds for this judgment. Yet were there none besides these worthy of mention?

Before Sima Junshi was employed in office, all under Heaven placed their hopes in him. Commentators considered him fully endowed with ability, but somewhat deficient in the scope of his vision. The empress [?] personally selected Sima as chancellor. Taking responsibility for all under Heaven upon himself, he thereupon ordered affairs according to a grand plan. At that time his beneficence reached the myriad people, and distant Rong and Di peoples submitted. His achievement in turning Heaven and Earth around was truly no empty claim. Is discerning men’s worth really so difficult? Or was there something those judgments failed to encompass? When scholars discuss the age in which these men lived and assess them against the Way, can they fail to understand how to seek the highest standard?

An earlier Confucian scholar said: “In learning, one must take the sage as the ultimate attainment; when one’s ambition embraces all under Heaven, one must aspire to the accomplishments of a chancellor.” Is anything below this even worthy of discussion?

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
問箕子陳武王八政八曰師周公告成王
立政有曰其克詰爾戎兵聖人告君不
忘乎兵之訓者天理之當然也蓋坎下
坤上爲師除殘去暴保邦衛民不得已
也前古能以衆正王者之師不可及矣
若夫後世以來郭子儀將兵以寬而兵
無不練李光弼將兵以嚴而兵亦無不
練何與蕭倪殷文昌減省兵而致軍士
爲盜禍及於國文彥博龐籍減省兵而
===
致軍士精强邊儲稍蘇何與古良將云
陣而后戰兵法之常運用之妙存乎一
心是果得將兵之要乎有所謂攻討之
兵有所謂鎮守之兵今日西蜀邊陲戎
夷出没備邊之策莫有過於鎮守之兵
也鎮守之兵陸宣公備言之矣說者謂
曲盡古今屯戍防邊之利害其詳可得
聞與先儒有云後世郡縣古之諸侯也
委之以土地人民而不與以兵是以匹
punctuated: 問：箕子陳武王八政，八曰師。周公告成王《立政》，有曰：「其克詰爾戎兵。」聖人告君不忘乎兵之訓者，天理之當然也。蓋坎下坤上爲師，除殘去暴，保邦衛民，不得已也。前古能以衆正，王者之師不可及矣。若夫後世以來，郭子儀將兵以寬，而兵無不練；李光弼將兵以嚴，而兵亦無不練，何與？蕭倪、殷文昌減省兵，而致軍士爲盜，禍及於國；文彥博、龐籍減省兵，而致軍士精强，邊儲稍蘇，何與？古良將云：「陣而后戰，兵法之常；運用之妙，存乎一心。」是果得將兵之要乎？有所謂攻討之兵，有所謂鎮守之兵。今日西蜀邊陲，戎夷出没，備邊之策，莫有過於鎮守之兵也。鎮守之兵，陸宣公備言之矣。說者謂曲盡古今屯戍防邊之利害，其詳可得聞與？先儒有云：「後世郡縣，古之諸侯也。委之以土地人民，而不與以兵，是以匹
translation_en:
Question: When Jizi set forth the eight matters of government for King Wu, the eighth was the army. In “Establishing Government,” the Duke of Zhou admonished King Cheng, saying: “Be able to put your military forces in order.” That the sages, when admonishing rulers, did not forget instruction concerning military affairs accords with heavenly principle. With Kan below and Kun above, the hexagram is The Army: eliminating the cruel and violent, protecting the state, and defending the people are measures undertaken only out of necessity. In high antiquity, rulers could bring the multitude to righteousness; the armies of true kings were beyond compare.

In later ages, Guo Ziyi commanded troops with leniency, yet all his troops were well trained; Li Guangbi commanded troops with severity, yet his troops too were all well trained. Why was this? Xiao Ni and Yin Wenchang [?] reduced troop numbers, causing soldiers to become bandits and bringing disaster upon the state; Wen Yanbo and Pang Ji reduced troop numbers, making their soldiers skilled and strong and somewhat replenishing frontier reserves. Why was this? A worthy general of old said: “To form ranks before fighting is the regular rule of military methods; the subtlety of their application rests in a single mind.” Does this indeed capture the essentials of commanding troops?

There are troops for offensive campaigns and troops for garrison defense. Today, Rong and Yi peoples appear and disappear along the frontiers of western Shu. Among strategies for frontier defense, none surpasses the use of garrison troops. Duke Xuan of Lu discussed garrison troops fully. Commentators say that he exhaustively explained the advantages and disadvantages of stationing troops and defending the frontiers, past and present. May we hear the details?

An earlier Confucian scholar said: “The prefectures and counties of later ages correspond to the feudal lords of antiquity. To entrust them with territory and people without giving them troops is to employ a common…

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
夫而守一州也今日民兵似亦烏重僃
之策之遺意與天下州縣守令因其舊
設民兵選驍勇於常役之中行訓練於
子牧之餘庶乎有備無患外重而內不
輕矣天下行之果無弊否耶諸子存心
當世必明當世之務其直述以對毋畧
punctuated: 夫而守一州也。今日民兵，似亦烏重僃之策之遺意與？天下州縣守令，因其舊設民兵，選驍勇於常役之中，行訓練於子牧之餘，庶乎有備無患，外重而內不輕矣。天下行之，果無弊否耶？諸子存心當世，必明當世之務，其直述以對，毋畧。
translation_en: …a commoner to defend an entire prefecture. Does the militia of today likewise seem to preserve something of the intent of Wu Chongbei’s 烏重僃 [?] policy? If prefects and county magistrates throughout the realm established militias following existing arrangements, selected brave and vigorous men from among those performing regular service, and conducted training in the time remaining from tending the people, then perhaps preparedness would avert danger: the outer regions would be strong without weakening the center. If this were implemented throughout the realm, would it truly be free of abuses? You gentlemen devote your attention to the present age and must understand its affairs. State your views directly in your answers, omitting nothing.

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
所謂立之斯立道之斯行綏之斯來動之
斯和
周建邦
同考試官教諭舒　批〔聖人俄頃之化惟於斯字見之是篇〕
〔曲盡其妙矣錄之〕
考試官教諭劉　批〔於斯字意不放過見學力〕
考試官教授黃　批〔形容神化殆盡從亦知聖人者〕
===
賢者極言聖人之神化以見其不可及也夫有
感斯應則神化與天地同流矣非天下之至聖
其孰能與於斯昔子貢曉子禽如此蓋謂欲知
夫子之不可及也盍自其得邦家者而觀之乎
夫民未易立也夫子有政以立之吾知培植之
餘自爾帖然安堵仰焉而足以事也俯焉而足
以畜也無復顛躋者矣立之斯立其不行而至
者乎夫民未易行也夫子有教以道之吾知倡
導之下自爾翕然向風言焉而以爲則也行焉
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

所謂「立之斯立，道之斯行，綏之斯來，動之斯和」。

周建邦

同考試官教諭舒，批〔聖人俄頃之化，惟於斯字見之。是篇〕〔曲盡其妙矣，錄之。〕
考試官教諭劉，批〔於斯字意不放過，見學力。〕
考試官教授黃，批〔形容神化殆盡，從亦知聖人者。〕

賢者極言聖人之神化，以見其不可及也。夫有感斯應，則神化與天地同流矣。非天下之至聖，其孰能與於斯？昔子貢曉子禽如此，蓋謂欲知夫子之不可及也，盍自其得邦家者而觀之乎？夫民未易立也，夫子有政以立之，吾知培植之餘，自爾帖然安堵，仰焉而足以事也，俯焉而足以畜也，無復顛躋者矣。立之斯立，其不行而至者乎？夫民未易行也，夫子有教以道之，吾知倡導之下，自爾翕然向風，言焉而以爲則也，行焉
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The passage: “When he establishes them, they stand firm; when he guides them, they proceed; when he comforts them, they come to him; when he stirs them, they become harmonious.”

Zhou Jianbang

Associate Examiner Shu, Instructor, comments: 〔The sage’s transformation of the people in an instant is revealed solely in the word si (‘thereupon’). This essay〕〔fully captures its subtlety. Include it.〕
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: 〔He neglects none of the meaning of the word si, demonstrating the strength of his learning.〕
Examiner Huang, Professor, comments: 〔The description of the sage’s wondrous transforming influence is nearly exhaustive; he too understands the sage [?].〕

The worthy speaks in the strongest terms of the sage’s wondrous transforming influence to show that he cannot be equaled. Whenever there is an impulse, a response immediately follows: thus his wondrous transforming influence flows together with Heaven and Earth. Who but the utmost sage of the world could participate in this? This was how Zigong once enlightened Ziqin. His meaning was surely this: if one wishes to understand why the Master cannot be equaled, why not consider what would happen if he obtained a state or a noble house to govern?

The people are not easily established. Yet the Master has policies with which to establish them. I know that, once nurtured, they would naturally settle peacefully in their homes, possessing sufficient means to serve their parents above and support their dependents below. No longer would any fall into distress. “When he establishes them, they stand firm”: is this not arriving without traveling?

The people are not easily set upon the right course. Yet the Master has teachings with which to guide them. I know that, under his leadership, they would naturally turn toward his influence with one accord. When he spoke, they would take his words as their standard; when he acted …

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
而以爲法也無復寘頳者矣道之斯行其不疾
而速者乎至若懷保以盡仁夫子之所以綏之
者固不期民之來也然至仁漸被其將焉往近
者以説遠者以來而庶民其歸附矣所謂綏之
斯來者蓋如此鼓舞以盡神夫子之所以動之
者固不期民之和也然至神默運罔不咸和會
其有極歸其有極而黎民其敏德矣所謂動之
斯和者蓋如此夫立之道之綏之來之聖人之
感也斯立斯行斯來斯和天下之應也其感應
===
之妙神速如此夫豈人之所可及哉抑子貢此
言亦可謂知聖人者矣惜乎夫子終窮弗究其
用而綏來動和之化乃托之空言也已雖然删
述六經垂憲萬世則又神化無窮守我所謂賢
於堯舜者也子貢他日論禮樂可知德政而亦
曰自生民以來未有夫子也斯言盡矣謂二子
智足以知聖人其以此也夫
是故君子戒愼乎其所不睹恐懼乎其所
不聞
punctuated:
而以爲法也，無復寘頳者矣。道之斯行，其不疾而速者乎？至若懷保以盡仁，夫子之所以綏之者，固不期民之來也；然至仁漸被，其將焉往？近者以説，遠者以來，而庶民其歸附矣。所謂綏之斯來者，蓋如此。鼓舞以盡神，夫子之所以動之者，固不期民之和也；然至神默運，罔不咸和，會其有極，歸其有極，而黎民其敏德矣。所謂動之斯和者，蓋如此。夫立之、道之、綏之、來之，聖人之感也；斯立、斯行、斯來、斯和，天下之應也。其感應之妙，神速如此，夫豈人之所可及哉？抑子貢此言，亦可謂知聖人者矣。惜乎夫子終窮，弗究其用，而綏來動和之化，乃托之空言也已。雖然，删述六經，垂憲萬世，則又神化無窮，守我所謂賢於堯舜者也。子貢他日論禮樂可知德政，而亦曰：「自生民以來，未有夫子也。」斯言盡矣。謂二子智足以知聖人，其以此也夫！

是故君子戒愼乎其所不睹，恐懼乎其所不聞。
translation_en:
…and take his conduct as their model; none would any longer falter [?]. When he guides them, they proceed: is this not swiftness without haste? As for cherishing and protecting them to fulfill benevolence, the Master's purpose in bringing them peace is certainly not to make the people come to him. Yet, as his utmost benevolence gradually reaches them, where else would they go? Those nearby rejoice, those afar come, and the common people give him their allegiance. Such is what is meant by “When he brings them peace, they come.” By inspiring and encouraging them, he gives full expression to his spiritual efficacy. The Master's purpose in stirring them is certainly not to make the people harmonious. Yet, as his utmost spiritual efficacy works silently, all become harmonious: they assemble around the supreme standard and return to it, and the common people diligently cultivate virtue. Such is what is meant by “When he stirs them, they become harmonious.” Establishing them, guiding them, bringing them peace, and bringing them to him [?] constitute the sage's influence; their becoming established, proceeding, coming, and becoming harmonious constitute the response of all under Heaven. So wondrous and spiritually swift is this interaction of influence and response—how could others possibly equal it?

Indeed, these words of Zigong show that he may be called one who understood the sage. Alas, the Master remained thwarted to the end and never fully put his abilities into practice; the transforming influence by which he would bring people peace and draw them to him, stir them and make them harmonious, thus found expression only in words. Nevertheless, by editing and transmitting the Six Classics and bequeathing models for ten thousand generations, he exercised a spiritual transforming influence without end. This is what I mean by his being worthier than Yao and Shun [?]. On another occasion, Zigong discussed how ritual and music reveal virtue and government, and also said: “Since human beings first existed, there has never been anyone like the Master.” These words say it all. Surely this is why it is said that the two men's wisdom sufficed to understand the sage!

“Therefore the gentleman is watchful and cautious concerning what he does not see, and fearful and apprehensive concerning what he does not hear.”

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
何一舉
同考試官教諭坑　批〔戒愼恐懼只是一敬字作者文雖〕
〔之遠矣此篇體認明白可録〕
同考試官教諭呂　批〔발〕
考試官教諭劉　批〔識得靜體〕
考試官教授黃　批〔邃於理學者〕
論君子之體道惟敬以直內焉夫聖學莫要於
存養也君子敬以直內則其爲己之功密矣中
庸首章子思子之意以爲天體物而不遺道無
===
時而可離君子體道之功果何如耶是故一念
未起而目不交物廓然其無端矣苟無以主之
知離道何君子於此戒愼乎其所不睹焉惟瞬
有養庸何思也惟息有存庸何慮也夫目無所
見雖曰寂然不動也主一於不識不知之天以
全靜中有動之妙體道之功其密也爲何如百
慮未萌而耳不交物洞然其無體矣苟無以主
之知離道何君子於此恐懼乎其所不聞焉惺
惺不昧自無忘也翼翼不已自無間也夫耳無
punctuated:
何一舉

同考試官教諭坑，批〔戒愼恐懼，只是一敬字。作者文雖〕〔之遠矣，此篇體認明白，可録。〕
同考試官教諭呂，批〔발〕
考試官教諭劉，批〔識得靜體。〕
考試官教授黃，批〔邃於理學者。〕

論君子之體道，惟敬以直內焉。夫聖學莫要於存養也。君子敬以直內，則其爲己之功密矣。《中庸》首章，子思子之意，以爲天體物而不遺，道無時而可離。君子體道之功，果何如耶？是故一念未起，而目不交物，廓然其無端矣。苟無以主之，知離道何？君子於此戒愼乎其所不睹焉。惟瞬有養，庸何思也？惟息有存，庸何慮也？夫目無所見，雖曰寂然不動也，主一於不識不知之天，以全靜中有動之妙，體道之功，其密也爲何如？百慮未萌，而耳不交物，洞然其無體矣。苟無以主之，知離道何？君子於此恐懼乎其所不聞焉。惺惺不昧，自無忘也；翼翼不已，自無間也。夫耳無
translation_en:
He Yiju

Associate Examiner Keng [?], Instructor, comments: 〔“Being watchful and cautious, apprehensive and fearful” amounts simply to the single word “reverence.” Although the author’s writing…〕〔…far removed [?], this essay shows clear understanding and may be selected.〕
Associate Examiner Lü, Instructor, comments: 〔[Illegible or garbled comment: 발.]〕
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: 〔He understands the substance of stillness.〕
Examiner Huang, Professor, comments: 〔One deeply versed in the Learning of Principle.〕

In discussing how the gentleman embodies the Way, it is through reverence alone that he makes his inner life upright. Nothing is more essential to the learning of the sages than preserving and nourishing the mind. When the gentleman makes his inner life upright through reverence, his efforts to cultivate himself are thorough indeed. In the opening chapter of the Doctrine of the Mean, Master Zisi’s meaning is that Heaven embodies all things without leaving anything out, and that the Way cannot be departed from for even a moment. What, then, is the gentleman’s work of embodying the Way actually like?

Thus, before a single thought has arisen, when the eyes have not engaged with things, there is a vast openness without any beginning. If there were nothing to govern it, who could know how far one might depart from the Way [?]? Here the gentleman is watchful and cautious concerning what he does not see. With nourishment at every instant, what need is there for deliberate thought? With preservation at every breath, what need is there for deliberation? When the eyes see nothing, this may be called being quiescent and unmoving. Yet by maintaining singleness of mind in Heaven’s state of unknowing and unawareness, he preserves fully the subtlety of movement within stillness. How thorough is his work of embodying the Way!

Before the hundred concerns have sprouted, when the ears have not engaged with things, there is a clear openness without form. If there were nothing to govern it, who could know how far one might depart from the Way [?]? Here the gentleman is apprehensive and fearful concerning what he does not hear. Alert and unclouded, he naturally never forgets; unceasingly attentive, he naturally allows no interruption. Now, when the ears have no…

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
所聞雖曰至靜無感也惟一於無思無爲之境
以全靜而無靜之眞體道之功其密也又何如
夫然則存養之無間天理之本體全矣聖學之
功豈有要於此哉大抵一動一靜天命之流行
道之原也君子於其靜也立本動也審幾一敬
而已矣何有一髮之間哉故曰敬以直內義以
方外子思子於中庸揭聖功也首章先靜而後
動孝章先動而後靜者動靜一理者道也動靜
無間者功也然動靜無端陰陽無始知道者默
===
而觀之可也
欲貴者人之同心也人人有貴於己者弗
思耳
吳崇德
同考試官教諭沈　批〔詞意得孟子慨世之旨可以占所養〕
矣
考試官教諭劉　批〔親切發明〕
考試官教授黃　批〔得伸此抑彼意〕
大賢言人皆欲貴而不察貴之在我也夫天爵
punctuated:
所聞，雖曰至靜無感也，惟一於無思無爲之境，以全靜而無靜之眞，體道之功，其密也又何如？夫然則存養之無間，天理之本體全矣。聖學之功，豈有要於此哉？大抵一動一靜，天命之流行，道之原也。君子於其靜也立本，動也審幾，一敬而已矣，何有一髮之間哉？故曰：「敬以直內，義以方外。」子思子於《中庸》揭聖功也，首章先靜而後動，孝章先動而後靜者，動靜一理者道也，動靜無間者功也。然動靜無端，陰陽無始，知道者默而觀之可也。
欲貴者，人之同心也。人人有貴於己者，弗思耳。
吳崇德
同考試官教諭沈，批〔詞意得孟子慨世之旨，可以占所養〕矣。
考試官教諭劉，批〔親切發明〕。
考試官教授黃，批〔得伸此抑彼意〕。
大賢言人皆欲貴，而不察貴之在我也。夫天爵
translation_en:
…hears nothing: although this may be called utmost stillness, untouched by external stimuli, one remains single-minded in the realm of neither thought nor action, thereby preserving the truth of stillness that is yet not mere stillness. How thorough, then, is the work of embodying the Way! When preservation and nurture thus proceed without interruption, the fundamental substance of Heaven’s principle is complete. Could anything be more essential to the work of learning to become a sage? In general, movement and stillness are the flowing operation of Heaven’s mandate, the source of the Way. In stillness the gentleman establishes the foundation; in movement he scrutinizes the incipient stirrings. It is simply a matter of reverent attentiveness throughout: how could there be even a hair’s breadth of interruption? Hence it is said: “Through reverent attentiveness, straighten the inner self; through righteousness, square outward conduct.” When Master Zisi sets forth the work of sagehood in the Doctrine of the Mean, the opening chapter places stillness before movement, while the chapter on filial piety [?] places movement before stillness. This is because movement and stillness sharing one principle constitute the Way, while allowing no interruption between movement and stillness constitutes the work of cultivation. Yet movement and stillness have no starting point, and yin and yang have no beginning. Those who understand the Way may contemplate this in silence.
The desire for honor is common to all people. Everyone has something honorable within himself; he simply does not reflect upon it.
Wu Chongde
Associate Examiner Shen, Instructor, comments: “The language and meaning capture Mencius’s concern over the state of the world; from this one can discern the writer’s self-cultivation.”
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “An intimate and pertinent elucidation.”
Examiner Huang, Professor, comments: “It captures the intention of elevating the one and subordinating the other.”
The great worthy says that all people desire honor, yet fail to recognize that honor resides within themselves. Now, Heaven-conferred nobility…

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
在我何貴如之人顧舍此而外求其亦不思之
甚與昔孟子因人求人爵而棄其天爵故示以
爲己之學如此彼貴如公卿而有服在大僚人
情於此孰不慶明揚之有會而思所以致其身
者乎貴如大夫而迪簡在王庭人情於此孰不
願進取之有階而思所以行其志者乎夫人爵
之求人心所同如此而亦豈知天爵之無俟於
求耶是故人孰不有仁乎則天命之重我其受
之矣充之而彌光赫赫乎其有令名不位而自
===
尊何待於外也人孰不有義乎則天德之良我
其守之矣廓之而彌盛休休乎其有餘樂不爵
而自榮何假於人也夫人人有貴於己而非自
外至則固宜人人自脩於己而不胥外求矣顧
乃徇人之欲勝而以天爵爲虛名逐物之意多
而以仁義爲外物蓋亦不求諸心而未之思耳
誠思之則知所貴在我亦何暇求之人哉噫自
有着而自棄之可哀已抑論古之人君設爵以
待天下之士而古之士亦惟脩身以俟之固無
punctuated: 在我，何貴如之？人顧舍此而外求，其亦不思之甚與！昔孟子因人求人爵而棄其天爵，故示以爲己之學如此。彼貴如公卿，而有服在大僚，人情於此，孰不慶明揚之有會，而思所以致其身者乎？貴如大夫，而迪簡在王庭，人情於此，孰不願進取之有階，而思所以行其志者乎？夫人爵之求，人心所同如此，而亦豈知天爵之無俟於求耶？是故人孰不有仁乎？則天命之重，我其受之矣。充之而彌光，赫赫乎其有令名，不位而自尊，何待於外也？人孰不有義乎？則天德之良，我其守之矣。廓之而彌盛，休休乎其有餘樂，不爵而自榮，何假於人也？夫人人有貴於己，而非自外至，則固宜人人自脩於己，而不胥外求矣。顧乃徇人之欲勝，而以天爵爲虛名；逐物之意多，而以仁義爲外物。蓋亦不求諸心，而未之思耳。誠思之，則知所貴在我，亦何暇求之人哉！噫！自有着而自棄之，可哀已！抑論古之人君設爵以待天下之士，而古之士亦惟脩身以俟之，固無
translation_en:
…lies within oneself: what nobility can equal it? Yet people abandon this and seek outside themselves. Is this not thoughtlessness in the extreme? In former times, because people sought human rank and abandoned their heavenly nobility, Mengzi thus showed them the learning undertaken for one’s own moral cultivation. When someone attains the eminence of a duke or minister and serves in high office, who would not rejoice at the opportunity to be recognized and promoted for his worth, and consider how to devote himself to service? When someone attains the eminence of a grand master and is selected for service at the royal court, who would not wish for a means of advancement and consider how to carry out his aspirations? Such is the universal desire for human rank; yet how could people know that heavenly nobility requires no seeking?

Who, then, does not possess benevolence? The weighty charge conferred by Heaven is something I have received. Develop it fully, and it shines ever brighter; resplendent is the good name it brings. One is honorable even without an official position: why depend on anything external? Who does not possess righteousness? The goodness of Heaven’s virtue is something I must preserve. Extend it, and it flourishes ever more fully; expansive is the abundant joy it brings. One has glory even without rank: why borrow it from others? Since everyone possesses nobility within himself, and it does not come from outside, everyone should surely cultivate himself, rather than seek it outside himself. Yet the urge to gratify human desires prevails, and people regard heavenly nobility as an empty name; their minds are much occupied with pursuing external things, and they regard benevolence and righteousness as things external to themselves. This is simply because they do not seek within their own hearts and have not reflected upon it. If they truly reflected, they would know that what is noble lies within themselves. What leisure would they then have to seek it from others? Alas! To possess it oneself and yet cast it aside—how lamentable!

Furthermore, the rulers of antiquity established ranks to await the worthy men of the realm, while the worthy men of antiquity merely cultivated themselves and awaited appointment. There certainly were none who…

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
自售以干進者降及後世道德日喪功利日開
無復有仁義之談人才至是壞矣可慨也孟子
目擊當時士習卑陋故反覆於人爵天爵之辨
蓋欲挽人心而復之古也士之有志者盍亦以
古人自期
易
天地以順動故日月不過而四時不忒聖
人以順動則刑罰清而民服豫之時義
大矣哉
===
同考試官教諭舒　批〔題本正大平易場中作者不於順動上文雖則於時義中紛繞認理精而措詞潔無踰此篇〕
考試官教諭劉　批〔時義意當如此〕
考試官教授黃　批〔理融氣順予其得豫之旨矣〕
周建邦
彖傳舉天地聖人之豫而極贊之也夫天地聖
人之道大矣而皆不外乎豫焉其斯以爲大乎
聖人傳豫之彖意若曰豫順以動豈惟建侯行
師爲然哉雖天地聖人則亦有然者自天地言
punctuated:
自售以干進者。降及後世，道德日喪，功利日開，無復有仁義之談，人才至是壞矣，可慨也！孟子目擊當時士習卑陋，故反覆於人爵天爵之辨，蓋欲挽人心而復之古也。士之有志者，盍亦以古人自期？

易

天地以順動，故日月不過而四時不忒；聖人以順動，則刑罰清而民服。豫之時義大矣哉！

考試官教諭劉，批〔時義意當如此。〕
考試官教授黃，批〔理融氣順，予其得豫之旨矣。〕

周建邦

彖傳舉天地聖人之豫而極贊之也。夫天地聖人之道大矣，而皆不外乎豫焉，其斯以爲大乎？聖人傳豫之彖，意若曰：豫，順以動，豈惟建侯行師爲然哉？雖天地聖人，則亦有然者。自天地言
translation_en:
…any who offered themselves for sale to seek advancement. In later ages, moral virtue declined daily, while the pursuit of achievement and profit spread daily. There was no longer any talk of benevolence and righteousness; the worth of men of talent had by then been corrupted. How lamentable! Mencius personally witnessed the debased habits of the scholars of his time. He therefore repeatedly distinguished between honors bestowed by men and honors bestowed by Heaven, seeking to turn people’s hearts back toward antiquity. Should not scholars with aspirations likewise take the ancients as their standard?

Book of Changes

“Heaven and Earth act in accordance with what is fitting; thus the sun and moon do not stray from their courses, and the four seasons do not err. The sage acts in accordance with what is fitting; thus punishments are justly administered and the people submit. Great indeed is the significance of the time of Joy (Yu)!”

Associate Examiner Shu, an Instructor, comments: 〔The topic is inherently upright, grand, plain, and accessible. Candidates in the examination hall did not develop their writing around ‘acting in accordance with what is fitting,’ but became entangled in the ‘significance of the time’ [?]. In precise understanding of principle and concise expression, no essay surpasses this one.〕
Examiner Liu, an Instructor, comments: 〔This is how the meaning of ‘the significance of the time’ should be understood.〕
Examiner Huang, a Professor, comments: 〔Its principles are thoroughly integrated and its flow of expression is smooth. I credit it with grasping the purport of Joy.〕

Zhou Jianbang

The Commentary on the Judgments adduces the Joy of Heaven and Earth and of the sage, and praises it to the utmost. The Way of Heaven and Earth and of the sage is great, yet none of it falls outside Joy. Is this why Joy is deemed great? In commenting on the judgment of Joy, the sage’s meaning is as though he said: Joy means acting in accordance with what is fitting. Does this apply only to establishing feudal lords and mobilizing armies? Even Heaven and Earth and the sage exemplify it. Speaking from the standpoint of Heaven and Earth…

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
之於穆不已妙大化闔闢之機冲漠無朕運一
元通復之理惟以順動也故日月相推而明生
無過差矣寒暑相推而歲成無愆忒矣而化以
成焉天地之豫如此自聖人言之以道爲體施
之萬事而無情與時偕行達之天下而不悖亦
以順動也則大觀有不戒之孚而人皆寡過刑
罰清矣至德有自然之應而罔不率俾萬民服
矣而治以成焉聖人之豫又如此夫莫大乎天
地不能外豫而爲之化則豫遍於天地矣莫大
===
乎聖人不能外豫而爲之治則豫盡於聖人矣
豫之時義其極大而無以加乎夫子舉而賛之
淵乎旨矣抑論之天地聖人順動一也然天地
無心而成化也所以賛天地之化者聖人也是
故撫五辰齊七政而極地平天成焉聖人裁成
輔相之功不容已也天地非聖人則其化亦過
矣然則聖人其成天地之能乎嗚呼天人之際
未易言也
夫易聖人所以崇德而廣業也知崇禮卑
punctuated:
之，於穆不已，妙大化闔闢之機；冲漠無朕，運一元通復之理，惟以順動也。故日月相推而明生，無過差矣；寒暑相推而歲成，無愆忒矣，而化以成焉。天地之豫如此。自聖人言之，以道爲體，施之萬事而無情；與時偕行，達之天下而不悖，亦以順動也。則大觀有不戒之孚，而人皆寡過，刑罰清矣；至德有自然之應，而罔不率俾，萬民服矣，而治以成焉。聖人之豫又如此。夫莫大乎天地，不能外豫而爲之化，則豫遍於天地矣；莫大乎聖人，不能外豫而爲之治，則豫盡於聖人矣。豫之時義，其極大而無以加乎！夫子舉而賛之，淵乎旨矣！抑論之，天地聖人，順動一也。然天地無心而成化也，所以賛天地之化者，聖人也。是故撫五辰，齊七政，而極地平天成焉。聖人裁成輔相之功，不容已也。天地非聖人，則其化亦過矣。然則聖人其成天地之能乎！嗚呼！天人之際，未易言也。

夫易，聖人所以崇德而廣業也。知崇禮卑。
translation_en:
…As for Heaven and Earth: august and unceasing, they wondrously effect the opening and closing through which the great transformation proceeds; empty, still, and without perceptible trace, they set in motion the principle by which the primal unity circulates and returns. This is solely because their movement accords with the proper order. Thus the sun and moon succeed one another and light arises, without deviation or error; cold and heat succeed one another and the year is completed, without irregularity or lapse. Transformation is thereby accomplished. Such is the Harmony (Yu) of Heaven and Earth. Speaking of the sage, he takes the Way as his substance and applies it to the myriad affairs without partial feeling; he moves together with the times and extends his influence throughout the world without contravening the proper order. This too is because his movement accords with that order. Through his majestic example, he inspires trust without admonition, so that people seldom err and punishments fall into disuse. His consummate virtue elicits a spontaneous response, so that none fail to follow and obey, and all the people submit. Good government is thereby accomplished. Such, in turn, is the sage’s Harmony.

Nothing is greater than Heaven and Earth; yet they cannot accomplish their transformations apart from Harmony. Harmony therefore pervades Heaven and Earth. None is greater than the sage; yet he cannot accomplish good government apart from Harmony. Harmony therefore finds its fullest expression in the sage. How supremely great, beyond anything that could be added, is the significance of the time of Harmony! The Master brings it forward and praises it: how profound his meaning! Yet let us consider this further. Heaven and Earth and the sage are alike in moving in accordance with the proper order. Heaven and Earth, however, accomplish transformation without conscious intention; it is the sage who assists their transforming work. Thus he orders the five celestial markers and harmonizes the seven celestial regulators, bringing to full realization order on earth and accomplishment in Heaven. The sage’s work of regulating and completing, assisting and sustaining, cannot cease. Without the sage, the transformations of Heaven and Earth would also go to excess. Does the sage, then, bring the capacities of Heaven and Earth to fulfillment? Ah! The relationship between Heaven and humanity is not easily spoken of.

The Changes is that by which the sage exalts his virtue and enlarges his undertakings. Knowledge is lofty; ritual propriety is lowly.…

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
崇效天卑法地
程尚儒
同考試官教諭舒　批〔崇德廣業知禮效法須是實見得方　得辭達此作亦庶幾乎錄之〕
考試官教諭劉　批〔知崇禮卑得傳意〕
考試官教授黃　批〔聖人所以崇德廣業者發明殆盡〕
大傳論易聖人因之以爲學焉夫學至聖人而
極也而必因乎易焉易不至矣乎大傳之意若
曰天下無易外之道聖人無易外之學何則聖
===
人有日新之德德則盛矣然其巍乎莫及者易
崇之也卦爻之法象皆其心德之流通聖人有
富有之業業則大矣然其浩乎無疆者易廣之
也變通之推遷皆其事功之充擴何者崇德莫
大於知聖人明天道察民故而理無不窮則睿
智所照會之吾心者無餘理知何崇也廣業莫
要於禮聖人觀會通行典禮而理無不循則躬
行所及措之天下者有實用禮何卑也夫莫高
匪天聖人效之知之崇者天之高也德不於是
punctuated:
崇效天，卑法地。

程尚儒

同考試官教諭舒　批〔崇德廣業，知禮效法，須是實見得，方　得辭達。此作亦庶幾乎，錄之。〕

考試官教諭劉　批〔知崇禮卑，得傳意。〕

考試官教授黃　批〔聖人所以崇德廣業者，發明殆盡。〕

大傳論易，聖人因之以爲學焉。夫學至聖人而極也，而必因乎易焉，易不至矣乎？大傳之意若曰：天下無易外之道，聖人無易外之學。何則？聖人有日新之德，德則盛矣；然其巍乎莫及者，易崇之也。卦爻之法象，皆其心德之流通。聖人有富有之業，業則大矣；然其浩乎無疆者，易廣之也。變通之推遷，皆其事功之充擴。何者？崇德莫大於知，聖人明天道，察民故，而理無不窮，則睿智所照，會之吾心者無餘理，知何崇也！廣業莫要於禮，聖人觀會通，行典禮，而理無不循，則躬行所及，措之天下者有實用，禮何卑也！夫莫高匪天，聖人效之，知之崇者，天之高也。德不於是
translation_en:
…In its loftiness, it emulates Heaven; in its lowliness, it models itself on Earth.

Cheng Shangru

Associate Examiner Shu, Instructor, comments: 〔Elevating virtue and broadening achievement, knowledge and ritual propriety, emulating and taking as a model—one must truly grasp these before one can express them adequately. This composition comes close; include it.〕

Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: 〔On the loftiness of knowledge and the lowliness of ritual propriety, this captures the meaning of the Commentary.〕

Examiner Huang, Professor, comments: 〔The means by which the sages elevate virtue and broaden achievement are elucidated almost exhaustively.〕

The Great Commentary discusses the Changes, upon which the sages base their learning. Learning reaches its pinnacle in the sages, yet even they must base it upon the Changes. Does this not show that the Changes is supremely perfect? The meaning of the Great Commentary is as though it said: there is no Way under Heaven outside the Changes, and the sages have no learning outside the Changes. Why is this? The sages possess virtue that is renewed daily, and their virtue is indeed abundant. Yet it is the Changes that elevates it to an unsurpassable height. The models and images of the hexagrams and their lines are all the flowing expression of the virtue within their hearts. The sages possess achievements of great richness, and their achievements are indeed vast. Yet it is the Changes that broadens them to boundless scope. The successive movements of transformation and adaptation are all extensions of their practical accomplishments.

Why is this so? Nothing is more important for elevating virtue than knowledge. The sages illuminate the Way of Heaven and investigate the circumstances of the people, leaving no principle unexplored. Thus, of the principles illuminated by their sagely wisdom, none remains ungathered within the heart. How lofty is knowledge! Nothing is more essential for broadening achievement than ritual propriety. The sages observe how things converge and interconnect, and carry out the established rites, leaving no principle unfollowed. Thus, wherever their personal practice extends, what they put into effect throughout the world has practical use. How lowly is ritual propriety!

Nothing is higher than Heaven, and the sages emulate it: the loftiness of knowledge is the height of Heaven. Is it not thereby that virtue…

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
而崇乎莫卑匪地聖人法之禮之卑者地之卑
也業不於是而廣乎噫茲聖人之學也易之所
以爲至也抑易孰作之聖人作之孰能至之聖
人至之聖人至之而奚聖人用之蓋洗心退藏
神明齋戒聖人有心易焉聖人用易用之此心
焉耳豈心之外復有易而德業之外復有心哉
不然夫子讀易奚爲而韋編之三絶也亦有契
於此心而已矣
書
===
乃聖乃神乃武乃文
吳崇德

考試官教諭劉　批〔善形容帝堯之德〕
考試官教授黃　批〔變化不測處善發明〕
大臣稱聖君之德必隨其變化而名之也蓋聖
神文武帝德變化之不測也大臣舉而稱之其
責難於舜之意大矣昔伯益因舜以克艱歸堯
punctuated:
而崇乎？莫卑匪地，聖人法之；禮之卑者，地之卑也，業不於是而廣乎？噫！茲聖人之學也，易之所以爲至也。抑易孰作之？聖人作之。孰能至之？聖人至之。聖人至之而奚？聖人用之。蓋洗心退藏，神明齋戒，聖人有心易焉。聖人用易，用之此心焉耳。豈心之外復有易，而德業之外復有心哉？不然，夫子讀易，奚爲而韋編之三絶也？亦有契於此心而已矣。

translation_en:
…and thereby be exalted? Nothing is lower than the earth, and the sage takes it as his model. The lowliness of ritual propriety is the lowliness of the earth: does not his work thereby become extensive? Ah! This is the learning of the sage, and this is why the Changes reaches the utmost perfection. Yet who made the Changes? The sages made it. Who can bring it to perfection? The sages bring it to perfection. And when the sages bring it to perfection, what then [?]? They put it to use. Cleansing their hearts and withdrawing into concealment, attaining spiritual clarity through purification and abstinence, the sages possess the Changes within their hearts. When they use the Changes, they use it in this heart alone. Could there be a Changes apart from the heart, or a heart apart from virtue and achievement? If this were not so, why did the Master, in reading the Changes, wear through its leather binding straps three times? It was simply that he found accord with this heart.

Book of Documents

“Now sagely, now spiritually marvelous, now martial, now cultured”

Wu Chongde

Comment by Associate Examiner Shen, Instructor: “The word ‘now’ in the topic particularly rewards reflection. This essay aptly names and describes the transformations of sagely virtue, while its ideas and language are precise. This is the only essay I have seen that achieves this.”

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: “It aptly portrays Emperor Yao’s virtue.”

Comment by Examiner Huang, Professor: “It ably elucidates the unfathomable aspects of these transformations.”

When a great minister praises a sage ruler’s virtue, he must name it according to its transformations. Sageliness, spiritual marvel, culture, and martial prowess are the unfathomable transformations of imperial virtue. In enumerating and praising them, the great minister had a profound intention to demand difficult achievements of Shun. Long ago, when Shun credited Yao with the ability to master difficulties, Bo Yi took this occasion…

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
而遂美堯之德以勸之其意以爲大哉堯之爲
君也盡乎克艱之道本乎聖人之德其德不可
名而其所可名者變化也以言乎其聖也理與
心一淵乎無形迹之可求是不思不勉從容中
道大而化之之謂聖矣以言乎其神也聖之至
妙渾乎非心思之可測是不疾而速不行而至
聖而不可知之之謂神矣曰聖曰神帝德變化
之妙也豈言語所能形容耶有所謂武者恭己
臨下儼然不怒之威剛主於內聖武日昭毅乎
===
大畏於四海焉有所謂文者大觀在上炳然英
華之發美在其中文章日著煥乎大顯於天下
焉曰武曰文帝德變化之妙也豈議擬所能彷
彿耶夫以帝堯之德如此此其所以君天子之
大位而盡克艱之道也與伯益述之其勸勉帝
舜之意不亦可見乎抑孟氏曰堯舜性之也帝
堯之大德固性之也嘗聞堯之兢兢舜之業業
其然乎曰然堯與首之以欽聖功之要也舜之
爲君伯益告之以無怠無荒皐陶告之以無教
punctuated:
而遂美堯之德以勸之。其意以爲：大哉，堯之爲君也！盡乎克艱之道，本乎聖人之德。其德不可名，而其所可名者，變化也。以言乎其聖也，理與心一，淵乎無形迹之可求，是不思不勉，從容中道，「大而化之之謂聖」矣。以言乎其神也，聖之至妙，渾乎非心思之可測，是不疾而速，不行而至，「聖而不可知之之謂神」矣。曰聖曰神，帝德變化之妙也，豈言語所能形容耶？有所謂武者，恭己臨下，儼然不怒之威；剛主於內，聖武日昭，毅乎大畏於四海焉。有所謂文者，大觀在上，炳然英華之發；美在其中，文章日著，煥乎大顯於天下焉。曰武曰文，帝德變化之妙也，豈議擬所能彷彿耶？夫以帝堯之德如此，此其所以君天子之大位而盡克艱之道也與！伯益述之，其勸勉帝舜之意，不亦可見乎？

translation_en:
…and thus praised Yao’s virtue to exhort him. His meaning was this: How great was Yao as a ruler! He fully realized the way of meeting the difficulties of rulership, grounding himself in the virtue of a sage. His virtue cannot be named; what can be named are its transformations. To speak of his sageliness: principle and mind were one, so profound that no outward trace could be sought. Without deliberation or effort, he naturally accorded with the proper way: this is what is meant by “Greatness that transforms is called sageliness.” To speak of his spiritual potency: this was sageliness at its utmost subtlety, an integral whole beyond the reach of thought. Swift without haste, arriving without travelling: this is what is meant by “Sageliness that cannot be fathomed is called spiritual potency.” “Sagely” and “spiritually potent” name the wondrous transformations of the emperor’s virtue. How could words describe them?

There was also what is called his martial quality: reverent in his own person as he presided over those below, he possessed an imposing authority without anger. Firmness governed within; his sagely martial power shone forth daily, resolute and greatly feared throughout the Four Seas. There was also what is called his civil refinement: an exalted exemplar stood above, brilliantly displaying its excellence. Beauty lay within him; its patterned expression grew daily more manifest, shining resplendently throughout the world. “Martial” and “civil” name the wondrous transformations of the emperor’s virtue. How could conjecture or comparison even approximate them? Such was Emperor Yao’s virtue. Surely this explains how he occupied the exalted position of Son of Heaven and fully realized the way of meeting the difficulties of rulership! In Boyi’s account of this, is his intention to exhort Emperor Shun not also evident?

Moreover, Master Meng said, “Yao and Shun possessed it by nature.” Emperor Yao’s great virtue was indeed his by nature. Yet we have heard of Yao’s anxious vigilance and Shun’s cautious attentiveness. Was this so? The reply is: Yes. As for Yao [?], reverence was placed first: this is the essential point of the work of becoming a sage. When Shun was ruler, Boyi admonished him, “Be neither idle nor negligent,” and Gao Yao admonished him, “Do not teach …

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
逸欲有邦大禹告之無若丹朱傲惟慢遊是好
聖人性之而當時聖臣陳告如此可以見性之
者之有事於學也蓋天人之際間不容髮聖學
之極恒純乎天程子曰鼓萬物而不與聖人同
憂聖人人也故不能無憂於此黙識而有得焉
可以知聖人之學矣故曰聖希天
弘敷五典式和民則爾身克正罔敢弗正
民心罔中惟爾之中
夏泗
===

賢王於大臣必命以司徒之教而示以教之本
焉蓋教化國家之先務也使不本諸身焉其何

其意若謂司徒掌邦教固以教民爲職矣然所
以教之者當何如哉彼父子之親君臣之義天
punctuated:
逸欲有邦。大禹告之：「無若丹朱傲，惟慢遊是好。」聖人性之，而當時聖臣陳告如此，可以見性之者之有事於學也。蓋天人之際，間不容髮；聖學之極，恒純乎天。程子曰：「鼓萬物而不與聖人同憂。」聖人，人也，故不能無憂。於此黙識而有得焉，可以知聖人之學矣。故曰：「聖希天。」
