title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
下之常道也必大而布之性分之固有昭揭於
四海焉夫婦之別長幼之序朋友之信天下之
達道也必弘而敷之職分之當爲開示於萬方
焉惟寅以和民則誘掖獎勸納斯民於親義之
歸使其天性呈露有不能已也惟翼以和厥衷
勞來匡直納斯民於序別信之域使其良心感
發有不容遏也此司徒之教也然其本則在君
牙之身使本不立焉則推之有不準動之有不
化其可乎蓋爾之一身下民觀法之所在也果
===
能動必以正而自處乎無偏無黨之地則身之
倡乎人也必從乎爾之正焉將見民日遷善有
不約而同之風孰敢有不正者乎爾之一心下
民趨向之所係也如民心罔念不免乎作好作
惡之思猶不可求之民也必率以爾之中焉務
使爾心所存有不令而從之機孰敢有罔中者
乎吁穆王之告君牙如此教民之道可謂盡矣
抑天佑下民作之君作之師故教養者人君奉
若天道也司徒掌邦教周制也觀穆王命君牙
punctuated:
下之常道也，必大而布之，性分之固有昭揭於四海焉。夫婦之別、長幼之序、朋友之信，天下之達道也，必弘而敷之，職分之當爲開示於萬方焉。惟寅以和民，則誘掖獎勸，納斯民於親義之歸，使其天性呈露，有不能已也。惟翼以和厥衷，勞來匡直，納斯民於序別信之域，使其良心感發，有不容遏也。此司徒之教也，然其本則在君牙之身。使本不立焉，則推之有不準，動之有不化，其可乎？蓋爾之一身，下民觀法之所在也。果能動必以正，而自處乎無偏無黨之地，則身之倡乎人也，必從乎爾之正焉。將見民日遷善，有不約而同之風，孰敢有不正者乎？爾之一心，下民趨向之所係也。如民心罔念，不免乎作好作惡之思，猶不可求之民也。必率以爾之中焉，務使爾心所存，有不令而從之機，孰敢有罔中者乎？吁！穆王之告君牙如此，教民之道可謂盡矣。
抑天佑下民，作之君，作之師，故教養者，人君奉若天道也。司徒掌邦教，周制也。觀穆王命君牙
translation_en:
…are the constant ways of all under Heaven. They must be spread far and wide, so that what is inherent in human nature is clearly displayed throughout the Four Seas. Distinction between husband and wife, precedence between elder and younger, and trustworthiness between friends are universally binding ways of all under Heaven. They must be broadly disseminated, so that the duties proper to each person’s station are made known in every region. Through reverence, bring the people into harmony: guide and assist them, encourage and exhort them, bringing them to affection and righteousness, so that their innate nature reveals itself in an irrepressible outpouring. Through watchful care, harmonize their inmost dispositions: comfort and encourage them, correct and set them straight, bringing them into the realm of precedence, distinction, and trustworthiness, so that their innate moral sense is stirred and awakened beyond restraint. Such is the teaching of the Minister of Education. Its foundation, however, lies in Jun Ya’s own person. If that foundation is not established, what he extends to others will lack a standard, and his efforts to stir them will fail to transform them. Could this be acceptable?
Your own person is what the common people look to as their model. If you can ensure that every action is upright and place yourself where there is neither partiality nor faction, then, when you lead others by personal example, they will surely follow your uprightness. You will see the people advance daily toward goodness, sharing a common disposition without prior agreement. Who would dare to be otherwise than upright? Your own heart determines the direction in which the common people turn. If you give no thought to the people’s hearts [?] and cannot escape thoughts of indulging personal likes and dislikes, you still cannot demand this of the people. You must lead them through your own centeredness, taking care that what you hold in your heart has the power to make them follow without being commanded. Who would dare to fail to hold to the center? Ah! King Mu’s admonition to Jun Ya was such that it may be said to have fully expounded the way of teaching the people.
Moreover, Heaven protects the common people, establishing rulers and teachers for them. Thus, in teaching and sustaining them, the ruler reverently follows the Way of Heaven. That the Minister of Education should administer the state’s teaching was an institution of the Zhou. When we consider King Mu’s charge to Jun Ya…

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
以司徒之教而下章又以養民之道告之可見
司徒之官兼教養之職也穆王之訓殆亦不忘
文武之訓而守有周之家法與夫子錄之其以
此與抑亦以示萬世君天下者之王道也
詩
苾芬孝祀神嗜飲食卜爾百福如幾如式
既齊既稷既匡既勑永錫爾極時萬時
億
何一舉
===
同考試官教諭坑　批　〔題本明白作者率多繁冗是篇整潔不浮何以加矣〕
同考試官教諭呂　批　〔文氣冲融得嘏詞意〕
考試官教諭劉　批　〔簡古含蓄〕
考試官教授黃　批　〔深得祝嘏之旨〕
神於公卿之祭隨其事而報之也夫禮物之盡
祀事之明也神之報之能不以其類哉昔公卿
有田祿者力於農事以奉宗廟之祭此則祝致
神意以嘏主人也蓋曰萃道在假於有廟祭義
punctuated:
以司徒之教，而下章又以養民之道告之，可見司徒之官兼教養之職也。穆王之訓，殆亦不忘文武之訓而守有周之家法與？夫子錄之，其以此與？抑亦以示萬世君天下者之王道也。
詩
苾芬孝祀，神嗜飲食。卜爾百福，如幾如式。既齊既稷，既匡既勑，永錫爾極，時萬時億。
何一舉
同考試官教諭坑批〔題本明白，作者率多繁冗，是篇整潔不浮，何以加矣！〕
同考試官教諭呂批〔文氣冲融，得嘏詞意。〕
考試官教諭劉批〔簡古含蓄。〕
考試官教授黃批〔深得祝嘏之旨。〕
神於公卿之祭，隨其事而報之也。夫禮物之盡，祀事之明也，神之報之，能不以其類哉？昔公卿有田祿者，力於農事，以奉宗廟之祭。此則祝致神意，以嘏主人也。蓋曰：萃道在假於有廟，祭義
translation_en:
…with the teaching entrusted to the Minister of Education, while in the following section he also instructs him in the way of nourishing the people. This shows that the office of Minister of Education combined responsibility for teaching and nourishing them. In giving these instructions, was King Mu perhaps also mindful of the instructions of Kings Wen and Wu, preserving the ancestral rules of the Zhou house? Was this why Confucius recorded them? Or was it also to show the kingly Way to those who would rule all under Heaven for ten thousand generations?

Book of Odes

“Fragrant are the filial sacrifices;
The spirits relish the drink and food.
They foretell a hundred blessings for you,
In accordance with your expectations and the prescribed forms.
Reverent and prompt,
Upright and diligent,
You shall forever be granted the utmost blessing,
In tens of thousands and hundreds of millions.”

He Yiju

Associate Examiner Keng [?], Instructor, comments: “The topic is inherently clear, yet writers mostly make it lengthy and cumbersome. This piece is orderly and concise, without superficiality. How could it be improved?”

Associate Examiner Lü, Instructor, comments: “The flow of the prose is harmonious and unforced; it captures the meaning of the words conveying the spirits’ blessings.”

Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “Concise, antique in style, and rich in implicit meaning.”

Examiner Huang, Professor, comments: “It deeply grasps the purport of the blessings pronounced by the invocator.”

At the sacrifices offered by dukes and high ministers, the spirits reward them in accordance with their service. When the ritual offerings are complete and the sacrificial service is illustrious, how could the spirits fail to reward them in kind? In former times, dukes and high ministers who held lands and emoluments devoted their efforts to agriculture so as to supply the sacrifices in the ancestral temples. Here the invocator conveys the spirits’ intentions, pronouncing blessings upon the host. In substance, he says: “The Way of Gathering Together lies in approaching the ancestral temple; the meaning of sacrifice…”

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
惟備於仁賢公卿今日之祭不有當於神意者
乎是故祭莫先於盡物也今爾陳飲食于孝祀
之時牲醴則既備也粢盛則既潔也苾苾芬芬
足以昭一心之明信神既嗜之而罔厭矣由是
感通之下將與爾以百福之隆自身而家休徵
爲之疊應由家而國瑞慶爲之駢臻受祿于天
其來如期也宜稼于田其多如法也夫豈有限
量乎哉其爲飲食之報也如此祭莫要於盡禮
也今爾肅禮容於享獻之際既整而且疾也既
===
正而且戒也濟濟蹌蹌足以占一心之恭敬神
固歆之而罔恫矣由是昭鑒之餘來錫爾以衆
善之極思若啓之約之于大中之矩行若翼之
躋之于亨嘉之會時有萬焉罄無不宜也時有
億焉動罔弗臧也夫豈有窮盡乎哉其爲禮容
之報也如此是則感之有道報之非私也幽明
類應之理詎不信夫抑聞書以明德惟馨易以
禴祭爲尚祭固不專於物也今以禮物並言者
何哉蓋祭物以力農而備先成民而後致力於
punctuated: 惟備於仁賢。公卿今日之祭，不有當於神意者乎？是故祭莫先於盡物也。今爾陳飲食于孝祀之時，牲醴則既備也，粢盛則既潔也，苾苾芬芬，足以昭一心之明信，神既嗜之而罔厭矣。由是感通之下，將與爾以百福之隆：自身而家，休徵爲之疊應；由家而國，瑞慶爲之駢臻。受祿于天，其來如期也；宜稼于田，其多如法也。夫豈有限量乎哉？其爲飲食之報也如此。祭莫要於盡禮也。今爾肅禮容於享獻之際，既整而且疾也，既正而且戒也，濟濟蹌蹌，足以占一心之恭敬，神固歆之而罔恫矣。由是昭鑒之餘，來錫爾以衆善之極：思若啓之，約之于大中之矩；行若翼之，躋之于亨嘉之會。時有萬焉，罄無不宜也；時有億焉，動罔弗臧也。夫豈有窮盡乎哉？其爲禮容之報也如此。是則感之有道，報之非私也。幽明類應之理，詎不信夫？抑聞《書》以明德惟馨，《易》以禴祭爲尚，祭固不專於物也。今以禮物並言者何哉？蓋祭物以力農而備，先成民而後致力於
translation_en:
…is fully realized only in the humane and worthy. Does not the sacrifice offered today by the dukes and ministers accord with the spirits’ intentions? Thus, in sacrifice nothing takes precedence over providing the offerings in full. Now, as you set out food and drink for this filial sacrifice, the sacrificial animals and sweet liquor are fully prepared, and the grain offerings are pure. Their rich fragrance suffices to manifest the clarity and sincerity of your undivided heart. The spirits have savored them without satiety. Through this communion, they will grant you the abundance of a hundred blessings. From your person to your household, auspicious signs will answer one after another; from your household to the state, felicitous portents and blessings will arrive together. You receive bounty from Heaven, arriving at its appointed time; your crops flourish in the fields, their abundance following the proper pattern. How could there be any limit to this? Such is the recompense for your offerings of food and drink.

In sacrifice nothing is more essential than fulfilling the rites. Now, as you maintain solemn ritual deportment while presenting your offerings, you are orderly and swift, upright and circumspect. Your dignified bearing and measured steps suffice to reveal the reverence of your undivided heart. The spirits indeed delight in this and feel no distress. Having clearly perceived it, they come to bestow upon you the utmost of every good. They seem to enlighten your thoughts, bringing them within the standards of the great mean; they seem to assist your conduct, raising you into a confluence of prosperity and excellence. Here are blessings by the ten thousand, with nothing whatsoever unfitting; here are blessings by the hundred million, with no action that is not good. How could these ever be exhausted? Such is the recompense for your ritual deportment.

Thus there is a proper way to move the spirits, and their recompense is no act of partiality. Is not the principle by which the unseen and visible realms respond to one another according to kind truly reliable? Yet I have heard that the Book of Documents holds that only illustrious virtue is fragrant, while the Book of Changes esteems the modest yue sacrifice. Sacrifice assuredly does not depend solely upon material offerings. Why, then, speak here of ritual and offerings together? It is because sacrificial offerings are made ready through diligent farming: first bring the people to fulfillment, and only afterward devote effort to…

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
神此其所以爲美也春秋奉物以祀先而曰民
力之普存者亦此意歟噫公卿德盛政修感神
固有素矣福善之報豈偶然哉彼不務民義而
諂瀆鬼神者烏足以知此
伴奐爾游矣優游爾休矣
劉世魁
同考試官教諭坑　批〔游休二字作者率多牽連一律惟此作分析明白豁人心目宜録之以式來學〕
同考試官教諭呂　批〔文詞簡當得康公規美之意是亦可愛者〕
===
考試官教諭劉　批〔說王者治安之福甚盡〕
考試官教授黃　批〔游休字分析明白〕
大臣於賢君兩舉其自得之樂焉夫樂而自得
福莫大焉者也大臣舉以爲賢君告其進戒之
意微矣哉此詩爲召公從成王游歌卷阿而作
也及此蓋謂吾王守成業而享盛治夫何爲哉
今日之福固有可言者矣夫莫不游也然游非
伴奐則游不足以言樂非福也吾王何如其游
耶極大觀於俯仰胸次悠然與天地同流託餘
punctuated:
神，此其所以爲美也。春秋奉物以祀先，而曰民力之普存者，亦此意歟？噫！公卿德盛政修，感神固有素矣，福善之報豈偶然哉？彼不務民義而諂瀆鬼神者，烏足以知此？

伴奐爾游矣，優游爾休矣。
劉世魁
同考試官教諭坑，批〔游休二字，作者率多牽連一律，惟此作分析明白，豁人心目，宜録之以式來學。〕
同考試官教諭呂，批〔文詞簡當，得康公規美之意，是亦可愛者。〕
考試官教諭劉，批〔說王者治安之福甚盡。〕
考試官教授黃，批〔游休字分析明白。〕

大臣於賢君，兩舉其自得之樂焉。夫樂而自得，福莫大焉者也。大臣舉以爲賢君告，其進戒之意微矣哉！此詩爲召公從成王游，歌卷阿而作也。及此，蓋謂吾王守成業而享盛治，夫何爲哉？今日之福，固有可言者矣。夫莫不游也，然游非伴奐，則游不足以言樂，非福也。吾王何如其游耶？極大觀於俯仰，胸次悠然，與天地同流；託餘
translation_en:
…the spirits: this is what makes it admirable. When offerings are presented in spring and autumn to sacrifice to the ancestors, and it is said that the people's labor is fully represented in them, does this not express the same idea? Ah! When dukes and ministers possess abundant virtue and well-ordered government, they have long had the means to move the spirits. How could the blessing that rewards goodness be accidental? How could those who neglect their obligations toward the people and instead flatter and profane the ghosts and spirits understand this?

“Freely and at ease you roam; leisurely and contentedly you rest.”
Liu Shikui.
Associate Examiner Keng [?], Instructor, comments: 〔Writers mostly conflate the two words “roam” and “rest,” treating them alike. This composition alone distinguishes them clearly, opening the reader's mind and eyes. It should be recorded as a model for future students.〕
Associate Examiner Lü, Instructor, comments: 〔The language is concise and apt, capturing Duke Kang's intent to admonish through praise. This too deserves appreciation.〕
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: 〔It explains most fully the blessings a king enjoys when his realm is well governed and at peace.〕
Examiner Huang, Professor, comments: 〔The words “roam” and “rest” are clearly distinguished.〕

A great minister addresses a worthy ruler, citing in two ways the pleasure of his contentment. To find pleasure and contentment—no blessing is greater. In citing these to address his worthy ruler, how subtle is the minister's intention to offer admonition! This poem was composed when the Duke of Shao accompanied King Cheng on an excursion and sang “The Winding Hill” (Juan a). At this point, he means that our king preserves the achievements handed down to him and enjoys flourishing government: what need has he to exert himself? There is indeed much to say about the blessings he enjoys today. Everyone may roam; yet unless one roams freely and at ease, such roaming cannot be called pleasure and is no blessing. How does our king roam? Looking upward and downward, he takes in the grandest vistas; his heart is tranquil, moving in harmony with Heaven and Earth. He gives expression to his lingering…

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
興於咏歌神思𤋮然與景象俱泰秉輿所至如
在風塵之表其孰得而我拘也吾王之游其伴
奐有如此者游之爲樂也何至哉夫莫不休也
然休非優游則休不足以言樂非福也吾王何
如其休耶機務息而動履從容陟降有安和之
慶臨御畢而身心清暇寢興無宵旰之勞王心
𢡟寧如脫形骸之外其孰得而我累也吾王之
休其優游有如此者休之爲樂也何至哉夫無
往非樂則無往非福召公進戒之意有在矣爲
===
成王者盍思所以致此者哉大抵否泰之機恒
相倚伏忠臣愛君必防其漸故召公進戒必先
歆以至治而繼以得賢輔治告焉蓋與周公無
逸之戒同一安不忘危之意也厥後成王爲守
成令主固其學力之到二公夾輔之功亦不可
誣也故萬世之下誦成王之德而稱二公之功
不衰
春秋
冬楚人陳侯蔡侯鄭伯許男圍宋 十有
punctuated:
興於咏歌，神思𤋮然，與景象俱泰。秉輿所至，如在風塵之表，其孰得而我拘也？吾王之游，其伴奐有如此者，游之爲樂也何至哉！夫莫不休也，然休非優游，則休不足以言樂，非福也。吾王何如其休耶？機務息而動履從容，陟降有安和之慶；臨御畢而身心清暇，寢興無宵旰之勞。王心𢡟寧，如脫形骸之外，其孰得而我累也？吾王之休，其優游有如此者，休之爲樂也何至哉！夫無往非樂，則無往非福。召公進戒之意有在矣。爲成王者，盍思所以致此者哉？大抵否泰之機，恒相倚伏。忠臣愛君，必防其漸，故召公進戒，必先歆以至治，而繼以得賢輔治告焉。蓋與周公《無逸》之戒，同一安不忘危之意也。厥後成王爲守成令主，固其學力之到，二公夾輔之功亦不可誣也。故萬世之下，誦成王之德，而稱二公之功不衰。

春秋

冬，楚人、陳侯、蔡侯、鄭伯、許男圍宋。十有
translation_en:
…his inspiration in song, his thoughts radiant and as harmonious as the surrounding scene. Wherever his carriage takes him, he seems to be beyond the dust and turmoil of the world. Who could constrain him? Such is the carefree ease of our king’s excursions: how consummate the pleasure he takes in them! Everyone rests, but unless rest brings unhurried ease, it cannot be called pleasure and is no blessing. What, then, is our king’s rest like? When urgent affairs cease, his movements are composed, and in ascending and descending he enjoys peace and harmony. When his duties as ruler are finished, body and mind are clear and at leisure; in sleeping and rising, he is free from the toil of working before dawn and late into the evening. The king’s heart is deeply tranquil [?], as though released from the confines of his bodily form. Who could burden him? Such is the unhurried ease of our king’s rest: how consummate the pleasure he takes in it!

If there is pleasure wherever he goes, there is blessing wherever he goes. Herein lies the Duke of Shao’s purpose in offering admonition. Should not King Cheng reflect on what has brought this about? Generally, the forces of adversity and prosperity always depend upon one another and lie concealed within one another. A loyal minister who loves his ruler must guard against the first signs of danger. Thus, in offering admonition, the Duke of Shao first stirred the king’s desire for perfect government, then advised him to obtain worthy men to assist in governing. This shares with the Duke of Zhou’s admonition in “Against Idleness” (Wu yi) the same purpose: never to forget danger amid security. That King Cheng subsequently became an excellent ruler who preserved his inheritance was certainly the achievement of his learning; yet the contribution of the two dukes, who supported him together, cannot be denied. Thus, through countless generations, people have celebrated King Cheng’s virtue and continued without diminution to praise the achievements of the two dukes.

Spring and Autumn Annals

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
二月甲戌公會諸侯盟于宋〔俱僖公二十有七年〕
王詢
同考試官訓導鄭　批〔傳意甚明作者多補叙宋與盟之非殊失體認惟此卷說得發明擬純為合可以式矣故録〕
考試官教諭劉　批〔足破羣疑〕
考試官教授黄　批〔得謹嚴旨〕
國以結夷春秋亦著其罪此楚與諸侯之圍宋
外夷合諸侯以軍大春秋均著其罪内君即大
===
會之盟楚而其罪皆不容掩有以見春秋謹華
夷之辨也嘗聞之詩曰蠢爾蠻荆大邦爲讎則
楚之暴横由來漸矣至是復偕陳蔡鄭許而有
宋之圍焉夫宋公先代之後作賓王家未聞有
可討之罪藏於諸侯之策者楚果何詞以圍之
耶圍既出於無名矣况復摟諸侯以同事耶諸
侯於宋皆友邦也楚方有事簒我中華禽獸逼
人之憂固宜有動於中不能却之援之乃舉兵
而同會焉獨不惡傷其類乎噫宋鮑負遊楚鄭
punctuated:
二月甲戌，公會諸侯盟于宋。〔俱僖公二十有七年〕
王詢
同考試官訓導鄭批〔傳意甚明，作者多補叙宋與盟之非，殊失體認。惟此卷說得發明，擬純為合，可以式矣，故録。〕
考試官教諭劉批〔足破羣疑。〕
考試官教授黄批〔得謹嚴旨。〕
國以結夷，春秋亦著其罪。此楚與諸侯之圍宋，外夷合諸侯以軍大，春秋均著其罪；内君即大會之盟楚，而其罪皆不容掩，有以見春秋謹華夷之辨也。嘗聞之，《詩》曰：「蠢爾蠻荆，大邦爲讎。」則楚之暴横，由來漸矣。至是復偕陳、蔡、鄭、許而有宋之圍焉。夫宋公，先代之後，作賓王家，未聞有可討之罪藏於諸侯之策者，楚果何詞以圍之耶？圍既出於無名矣，况復摟諸侯以同事耶？諸侯於宋，皆友邦也。楚方有事簒我中華，禽獸逼人之憂，固宜有動於中。不能却之、援之，乃舉兵而同會焉，獨不惡傷其類乎？噫！宋鮑負遊楚鄭
translation_en:
…On the jiaxu day of the twelfth month, the duke met the regional lords and made a covenant at Song. 〔Both passages belong to the twenty-seventh year of Duke Xi.〕
Wang Xun 王詢
Associate Examiner Zheng, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔The meaning of the commentary is very clearly conveyed. Most writers add an account of the wrongfulness of Song’s participation in the covenant, badly misunderstanding the passage. This essay alone brings out its meaning; its treatment is wholly fitting [?] and may serve as a model. Hence its inclusion.〕
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: 〔Sufficient to dispel the many doubts.〕
Examiner Huang, Professor, comments: 〔Captures the purport of scrupulous rigor.〕
When states ally with the barbarians, the Spring and Autumn Annals also makes their guilt manifest. Here, in the siege of Song by Chu and the regional lords, an external barbarian power joined the regional lords in military action against a great state [?], and the Spring and Autumn Annals records their guilt alike. The ruler of an inner state attended the great gathering to covenant with Chu [?], and none of their guilt could be concealed. This shows how carefully the Spring and Autumn Annals maintains the distinction between the Chinese and the barbarians.
I have heard these words from the Book of Odes: “You restless Man of Jing, foes of the great states!” Thus Chu’s violence and arrogance had long been developing. Now it again joined Chen, Cai, Zheng, and Xu in laying siege to Song. The duke of Song was a descendant of a former dynasty and held the status of guest of the royal house. We have never heard of any offense warranting punitive action being recorded against him in the annals of the regional lords. What grounds, then, could Chu possibly offer for besieging him? The siege already lacked a legitimate justification; how much worse to drag the regional lords into the same undertaking!
The regional lords were all rulers of states friendly to Song. As Chu undertook to usurp our central realm, alarm at beasts pressing upon human beings surely ought to have stirred within them. Unable to repel Chu and aid Song, they instead raised troops and joined the gathering. Did they alone feel no abhorrence at harming their own kind? Alas! Bao of Song, bearing or relying upon something, traveled to Chu and Zheng [?] …

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
侯之君子猶以其亟病中國不之與也今日之
役果何名乎經於楚子貶而稱人以例其餘而
諸侯之罪見矣又聞之詩曰戎狄是膺荊舒是
懲是魯之攘楚固其宜矣于時魯因與楚結好
乃有宋之盟焉夫魯僖周公之裔人望攸屬方
謂有紓難之圖以光前人之烈者果何所取而
與會耶會既比之匪人矣況復即宋地而與之
盟耶魯之於宋亦友邦也宋方被圍民朝夕急
中國冠裳之禍亦已親擊於目不能攘之恤之
===
又與會而同盟焉獨能無慊於心乎噫楚莊伐
陳陳鄭盟之君子固以其從義討賊不之罪也
今日之舉果何義乎經書盟于宋謂宋方見圍
無慊與盟而魯之罪亦著矣由是觀之則知夷
狄之於中國與中國之所以處夷狄固有大界
限而不可易者矣此春秋所以爲謹嚴之書也
歟抑又論之世入春秋王迹既熄伯圖遂啓彼
宋者中國之樞紐也楚成窺伯故於宋獨致力
焉其後楚莊繼之亦復圍宋盟宋知今日矣所
punctuated:
侯之，君子猶以其亟病中國，不之與也。今日之役，果何名乎？經於楚子貶而稱人，以例其餘，而諸侯之罪見矣。又聞之，《詩》曰：「戎狄是膺，荊舒是懲。」是魯之攘楚，固其宜矣。于時魯因與楚結好，乃有宋之盟焉。夫魯僖，周公之裔，人望攸屬，方謂有紓難之圖，以光前人之烈者，果何所取而與會耶？會既比之匪人矣，況復即宋地而與之盟耶？魯之於宋，亦友邦也。宋方被圍，民朝夕急，中國冠裳之禍，亦已親擊於目，不能攘之恤之，又與會而同盟焉，獨能無慊於心乎？噫！楚莊伐陳，陳鄭盟之，君子固以其從義討賊，不之罪也。今日之舉，果何義乎？經書「盟于宋」，謂宋方見圍，無慊與盟，而魯之罪亦著矣。由是觀之，則知夷狄之於中國，與中國之所以處夷狄，固有大界限而不可易者矣。此《春秋》所以爲謹嚴之書也歟！

抑又論之，世入春秋，王迹既熄，伯圖遂啓。彼宋者，中國之樞紐也。楚成窺伯，故於宋獨致力焉。其後楚莊繼之，亦復圍宋、盟宋，知今日矣。所
translation_en:
…the lord [?]; the gentleman nevertheless withheld approval because he repeatedly afflicted the Central States. What legitimate grounds, then, were there for the present campaign? The Classic degrades the Viscount of Chu by calling him simply a “man,” thereby setting the judgment for the others; thus the guilt of the feudal lords becomes apparent.

I have also heard these words from the Book of Odes: “The Rong and Di were repelled; Jing and Shu were chastised.” It was therefore certainly fitting for Lu to repel Chu. At this time, however, Lu cultivated friendly relations with Chu, and consequently there was the covenant at Song. Duke Xi of Lu was a descendant of the Duke of Zhou, upon whom people’s hopes rested. Just when one expected him to devise a plan to relieve the crisis and thereby illuminate his ancestor’s achievements, what could he possibly have found commendable that led him to attend this meeting? By attending, he had already allied himself with unworthy men; how much worse, then, to go onto Song’s own territory and covenant with them! Lu, too, was a friendly state to Song. Song was under siege, and its people faced urgent peril morning and evening. The calamity threatening the capped and robed civilization of the Central States was already striking directly before his eyes [?]. Unable to repel the attackers or succor the afflicted, he nevertheless attended the meeting and joined the covenant. Could he alone feel no misgivings in his heart?

Alas! When King Zhuang of Chu attacked Chen, Chen and Zheng entered into a covenant with him. The gentleman did not condemn this, since it accorded with righteousness and punished a malefactor. But what righteousness was there in the present undertaking? The Classic records “made a covenant at Song,” indicating that Song was then under siege and “had no misgivings about joining the covenant” [?]; thus Lu’s guilt, too, becomes manifest. Viewed in this light, the relations of the Yi and Di with the Central States, and the way the Central States should deal with the Yi and Di, clearly involve a fundamental boundary that cannot be altered. Is this not why the Spring and Autumn Annals is a book of such scrupulous rigor?

Let us consider the matter further. As the age entered the Spring and Autumn period, the traces of kingly rule had faded, and designs for hegemony consequently arose. Song was the pivotal state among the Central States. King Cheng of Chu coveted hegemony and therefore directed particular effort against Song. Later, King Zhuang of Chu followed him, again besieging Song and making a covenant at Song—“knowing this day” [?]. What …

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
幸晉文晉悼相繼而興皆能以救宋却楚成功
故晉人有言曰成霸安彊自宋始矣然則茲役
也固夷夏盛衰之一幾歟
蔡公子履出奔楚　陳侯之弟黃出奔楚
〔襄公二十年〕
張瑶
同考試官訓導鄭　批〔責臣與君士子類能言之至於發明義端本之意僅見此篇且詞充理到是用録出〕
考試官教諭劉　批〔録以正大倫〕
===
考試官教授黃　批〔簡嚴〕
春秋於貴戚之去國有明義以責其臣者有端
本以責其君者此可見履之奔其失在已黃之
奔其失在君也春秋各致意於書法有以哉且
履者蔡之公子也何爲而出奔于楚耶有兄曰
燮者見殺于蔡乃歸楚以免禍也而春秋罪及
其身者誠以貴爲公子社稷之鎮在焉進退從
違之義不可苟也彼燮者非蔡之公子耶身雖
被殺其棄楚從晉之謀無亦求利於社稷出於
punctuated:
幸晉文、晉悼相繼而興，皆能以救宋却楚成功。故晉人有言曰：「成霸安彊，自宋始矣。」然則茲役也，固夷夏盛衰之一幾歟？
蔡公子履出奔楚。陳侯之弟黃出奔楚。〔襄公二十年〕
張瑶
同考試官訓導鄭批〔責臣與君，士子類能言之。至於發明義端本之意，僅見此篇。且詞充理到，是用録出。〕
考試官教諭劉批〔録以正大倫。〕
考試官教授黃批〔簡嚴。〕
春秋於貴戚之去國，有明義以責其臣者，有端本以責其君者。此可見履之奔，其失在已；黃之奔，其失在君也。春秋各致意於書法，有以哉！且履者，蔡之公子也，何爲而出奔于楚耶？有兄曰燮者，見殺于蔡，乃歸楚以免禍也。而春秋罪及其身者，誠以貴爲公子，社稷之鎮在焉，進退從違之義不可苟也。彼燮者，非蔡之公子耶？身雖被殺，其棄楚從晉之謀，無亦求利於社稷，出於
translation_en:
…Fortunately, Duke Wen and Duke Dao of Jin arose in succession, and both achieved success by rescuing Song and repelling Chu. Thus the men of Jin had a saying: “Achieving hegemony and securing strength began with Song.” Was this campaign, then, not a pivotal moment in the rise and decline of the barbarians and the Chinese states?
Prince Lü of Cai fled to Chu. Huang, younger brother of the Marquis of Chen, fled to Chu. 〔Twentieth year of Duke Xiang.〕
Zhang Yao.
Associate Examiner Zheng, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔Candidates generally know how to discuss holding ministers and rulers accountable. But only this essay elucidates the intention of making duty clear and rectifying the source. Moreover, its language is full and its reasoning thorough; hence its selection.〕
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: 〔Selected to set the cardinal human relationships right.〕
Examiner Huang, Professor, comments: 〔Concise and rigorous.〕
When recording the departure of noble royal kinsmen from their states, the Spring and Autumn Annals sometimes makes duty clear in order to hold a minister accountable, and sometimes rectifies the source in order to hold his ruler accountable. Here we can see that in Lü’s flight, the fault lay with himself; in Huang’s flight, the fault lay with his ruler. There is good reason for the distinct intentions conveyed by the Annals’ wording in each case! Now Lü was a prince of Cai: why did he flee to Chu? He had an elder brother named Xie who was killed in Cai, so he went over to Chu to escape disaster. Yet the Annals assigns blame to Lü himself precisely because, with his noble standing as a prince, he bore responsibility for safeguarding the altars of soil and grain. The duties governing whether to advance or withdraw, to comply or resist, could not be treated casually. Was Xie not also a prince of Cai? Although he was killed, was not his plan to abandon Chu and follow Jin intended to benefit the state—to emerge from …

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
幽谷遷於喬木事之合義無可易者覆其母弟
何獨愲耶進而事君既不能明義以正國退而
自處又不能居正以遠害惴惴焉懼禍之及謀
其不免至於出奔而歸楚焉噫楚果何人也夷
狄也禽獸也兄固棄之弟固歸之賢不肖之相
去何如耶經書于策者曰是蔡之公子也而奔
楚也而覆之罪見矣若黃者陳侯之弟也亦何
爲而出奔于楚耶有臣曰慶寅慶虎者譖之于
楚乃赴楚以求勝也而春秋譏歸陳侯者誠以
===
貴爲諸侯一國之利勢在焉生殺予奪之柄不
可移也彼二慶者非陳之臣子耶爲人臣子而
敢爲暴君去親之謀固已自干於國典惟辟作
威惟辟作福事之在我初無難者哀爲國君何
獨懵耶以尊榮之身而不能遠其暴蔑之辱有
親愛之弟而不能保其富貴之常唯唯然聽其
愬楚無能與辨至黃之因楚而後克焉噫楚果
何人也非君之尊非父之親臣固愬之弟復因
之倫謂國有君乎經以弟書若曰是陳侯之弟
punctuated: 幽谷，遷於喬木，事之合義，無可易者。覆其母弟，何獨愲耶？進而事君，既不能明義以正國；退而自處，又不能居正以遠害。惴惴焉懼禍之及，謀其不免，至於出奔而歸楚焉。噫！楚果何人也？夷狄也，禽獸也。兄固棄之，弟固歸之，賢不肖之相去何如耶？經書于策者曰：是蔡之公子也，而奔楚也。而覆之罪見矣。若黃者，陳侯之弟也，亦何爲而出奔于楚耶？有臣曰慶寅、慶虎者，譖之于楚，乃赴楚以求勝也。而春秋譏歸陳侯者，誠以貴爲諸侯，一國之利勢在焉，生殺予奪之柄不可移也。彼二慶者，非陳之臣子耶？爲人臣子，而敢爲暴君去親之謀，固已自干於國典。惟辟作威，惟辟作福，事之在我，初無難者。哀爲國君，何獨懵耶？以尊榮之身，而不能遠其暴蔑之辱；有親愛之弟，而不能保其富貴之常。唯唯然聽其愬楚，無能與辨，至黃之因楚而後克焉。噫！楚果何人也？非君之尊，非父之親，臣固愬之，弟復因之，倫謂國有君乎？經以弟書，若曰：是陳侯之弟
translation_en:
…from a secluded valley and ascending to a lofty tree: his action accorded with righteousness, and there was nothing in it to alter. Yet Lü [?], his younger brother by the same mother, why was he alone so bewildered [?]? In coming forward to serve his ruler, he could not make righteousness clear and thereby set the state right; in withdrawing to conduct his own affairs, he could not abide in rectitude and thereby keep harm at a distance. Trembling with fear that disaster would reach him, he reckoned that he could not escape it, and ultimately fled the state and went over to Chu. Alas! What sort of people are those of Chu? They are barbarians, birds and beasts. The elder brother rejected them, while the younger brother went over to them: how great was the distance between the worthy and the unworthy! What the Classic records on its tablets says, in effect: this man was a ducal son of Cai, yet he fled to Chu. Thus Lü’s [?] guilt becomes apparent.

As for Huang, he was the younger brother of the Marquis of Chen. Why, then, did he too flee to Chu? There were ministers named Qing Yin and Qing Hu who slandered him before Chu, so he went to Chu to seek to prevail over them. Yet the Spring and Autumn Annals directs its censure at the Marquis of Chen. This is precisely because, in his exalted position as a regional lord, he held the resources and power of an entire state; the authority to grant life or death, to bestow or take away, could not be transferred to others. Were those two Qings not subjects of Chen? As subjects, they dared to plot to oppress their ruler and remove his kinsman, thereby already making themselves liable to the laws of the state. Only the sovereign may wield punitive power; only the sovereign may confer blessings. These matters lay in his own hands and presented no inherent difficulty. Why, then, was Ai, the ruler of the state, alone so benighted? Despite his exalted and honored position, he could not avert the humiliation of their violence and contempt; though he had a beloved younger brother, he could not preserve that brother’s wealth and rank. Meekly assenting, he allowed them to lodge their accusations in Chu, unable to contest their case, until Huang prevailed only by relying on Chu. Alas! What sort of people are those of Chu? They possess neither a ruler’s august authority nor a father’s familial bond. His ministers lodged accusations there, and his younger brother in turn relied upon it. Can one still [?] say that the state had a ruler? By recording him as ‘younger brother,’ the Classic seems to say: this was the younger brother of the Marquis of Chen…

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
也而使之奔楚也而陳哀之罪昭矣吁貶蔡侯
則爲臣者知明義以事君而臣道盡譏陳侯則
爲君者知正法以馭臣而君道盡謂春秋爲經
世之書信夫雖然侯可罪矣殺謀臣以說夷狄
在蔡景也何心哀可罪矣因夷狄以誅國臣在
陳黃也何義噫子展與晉蕭魚結盟季友去魯
落姑請復然則陳蔡之君臣其罪豈獨在於侯
與哀侯哉
禮記
故天子之爲樂也以賞諸侯之有德者也
德盛而教尊五穀時熟然後賞之以樂
曾士爻
同考試官教諭胡　批〔發揮作樂命德之意明盡蓋黨究樂〕
〔而有得者〕
考試官教諭劉　批〔典雅〕〔足式〕
考試官教授黃　批〔沖〕〔澹〕
記者論人君作樂以命德而必徵其實也蓋樂
非無因而作也而君之命德以之則樂豈可易
punctuated:
也，而使之奔楚也，而陳哀之罪昭矣。吁！貶蔡侯，則爲臣者知明義以事君，而臣道盡；譏陳侯，則爲君者知正法以馭臣，而君道盡。謂春秋爲經世之書，信夫！雖然，侯可罪矣，殺謀臣以說夷狄，在蔡景也何心？哀可罪矣，因夷狄以誅國臣，在陳黃也何義？噫！子展與晉蕭魚結盟，季友去魯落姑請復，然則陳蔡之君臣，其罪豈獨在於侯與哀侯哉？

禮記
故天子之爲樂也，以賞諸侯之有德者也。德盛而教尊，五穀時熟，然後賞之以樂。
曾士爻
同考試官教諭胡　批〔發揮作樂命德之意明盡，蓋黨究樂〕〔而有得者。〕
考試官教諭劉　批〔典雅〕〔足式。〕
考試官教授黃　批〔沖〕〔澹。〕

記者論人君作樂以命德，而必徵其實也。蓋樂非無因而作也，而君之命德以之，則樂豈可易
translation_en:
…yet he was made to flee to Chu; thus Duke Ai of Chen’s guilt becomes manifest. Ah! By censuring the lord of Cai, the text teaches ministers to understand righteousness in serving their rulers, thereby fulfilling the way of the minister. By criticizing the lord of Chen, it teaches rulers to uphold proper laws in governing their ministers, thereby fulfilling the way of the ruler. How true it is to call the Spring and Autumn Annals a book for ordering the world! Nevertheless, though the lord deserved blame, what intentions did Duke Jing of Cai have in killing a minister who had devised a plan, to please the barbarians? Though Duke Ai deserved blame, what righteousness was there in Huang of Chen’s relying on the barbarians to execute his state’s ministers? Ah! Zizhan concluded a covenant with Jin at Xiaoyu; Jiyou left Lu, and at Luogu his return was requested. Thus, among the rulers and ministers of Chen and Cai, could the guilt rest solely with the lord of Cai and Duke Ai [?]?

Record of Rites
“Thus the Son of Heaven makes music to reward those feudal lords who possess virtue. When their virtue flourishes, their teaching is honored, and the five grains ripen in season, only then does he reward them with music.”
Zeng Shiyao
Associate Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: “The meaning of making music to honor virtue is expounded clearly and fully. Evidently one who has studied music [?] and gained insight into it.”
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “Classical and elegant; worthy to serve as a model.”
Examiner Huang, Professor, comments: “Serene and restrained.”

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
視乎哉昔者天子以一身而建中和之極以一
心而凝聲氣之元固嘗取諸豫以作樂矣然樂
何爲而作也蓋諸侯之有德也不可無襃嘉之
典而樂之設也正以昭錫與之具焉耳故夫爲
諸侯者奮謀猷於亮寀而疏附之績隆懋忠貞
於藩屏而保乂之道著由是本諸身而徵諸民
也下觀而化自樹乎民極之尊道德一而風俗
同五典其克從矣感之人而應之天也和氣所
召自臻乎大有之徵陰陽和而風雨時百穀其
===
用乂矣夫惟其有是德也於焉隨其分而賞其
樂昭品秩於器數之間庶使聞其樂而知其德
彰激勸於旌别之下此則君臣之交胥悅之義
而樂之所由作也吁樂以賞德則錫之者非濫
與德賞於樂則受之者不虛君非有道之世其
孰能之大抵崇功報德人君馭下之微權効力
攄忠人臣事君之大節故蹇著匪躬之義而晋
隆錫馬之恩此篤棐明保姬旦所以委質於成
王而彤弓秬鬯平王所以錫德於文侯也雖然
punctuated: 視乎哉？昔者，天子以一身而建中和之極，以一心而凝聲氣之元，固嘗取諸豫以作樂矣。然樂何爲而作也？蓋諸侯之有德也，不可無襃嘉之典，而樂之設也，正以昭錫與之具焉耳。故夫爲諸侯者，奮謀猷於亮寀，而疏附之績隆；懋忠貞於藩屏，而保乂之道著。由是本諸身而徵諸民也，下觀而化，自樹乎民極之尊；道德一而風俗同，五典其克從矣。感之人而應之天也，和氣所召，自臻乎大有之徵；陰陽和而風雨時，百穀其用乂矣。夫惟其有是德也，於焉隨其分而賞其樂，昭品秩於器數之間，庶使聞其樂而知其德，彰激勸於旌别之下。此則君臣之交胥悅之義，而樂之所由作也。吁！樂以賞德，則錫之者非濫與；德賞於樂，則受之者不虛君。非有道之世，其孰能之？大抵崇功報德，人君馭下之微權；効力攄忠，人臣事君之大節。故蹇著匪躬之義，而晋隆錫馬之恩。此篤棐明保，姬旦所以委質於成王；而彤弓秬鬯，平王所以錫德於文侯也。雖然，
translation_en:
…be regarded lightly? In ancient times, the Son of Heaven, through his own person, established the supreme standard of equilibrium and harmony, and through his single heart concentrated the primal source of sound and vital energy. He indeed drew upon the hexagram Yu (Enthusiasm) in making music. Yet for what purpose was music made? When the feudal lords possessed virtue, there had to be rites to commend and honor them; the establishment of music served precisely to make manifest the means of bestowing such rewards. Thus those who were feudal lords exerted their talents in counsel as fellow assistants to the ruler, achieving distinction in drawing others into allegiance; they cultivated loyalty and constancy as bulwarks of the realm, making manifest their ability to protect and govern.

Their virtue was rooted in themselves and verified among the people. Those below observed them and were transformed, and they thereby established themselves as exalted standards for the people. Moral principles became one and customs became uniform, so that the five cardinal teachings could be followed. Their influence moved people and elicited a response from Heaven. The harmonious vital energy they summoned naturally brought signs of great abundance: yin and yang were in accord, wind and rain came in their seasons, and all grains flourished.

Precisely because they possessed such virtue, they were rewarded with music appropriate to their allotted standing. Their grades and ranks were made manifest in the instruments and their prescribed numbers, so that those hearing their music might recognize their virtue, and the encouragement offered by these marks of distinction would be evident. This is the meaning of ruler and ministers taking mutual delight in their dealings, and the reason music was made. Ah! When music rewards virtue, those who bestow it do not give indiscriminately; when virtue is rewarded with music, those who receive it do not fail their ruler. Who could accomplish this except in an age governed according to the Way?

In general, honoring achievement and recompensing virtue are the subtle means by which a ruler directs his subordinates; exerting oneself and giving full expression to loyalty are the great obligations of a minister serving his ruler. Thus the hexagram Jian (Obstruction) makes clear the principle of disregarding oneself, while Jin (Advance) magnifies the favor of horses bestowed as gifts. Such devoted assistance and enlightened protection explain why Ji Dan pledged his service to King Cheng; the red bow and black-millet sacrificial wine explain how King Ping rewarded the virtue of the Marquis of Wen. Nevertheless…

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
八佾之賜後世譏之雍歌之徹君子憾焉然則
僭也濫也爲君臣者其亦致嚴於斯
福者備也備者百順之名也無所不順者
之謂備言內盡於己而外順於道也
陳勛
同考試官教諭胡　批〔備順二字其旨合含畜于盡己順道發出作者〕
〔類失之支蔓是篇體認真切特錄之〕
考試官教諭劉　批〔意完詞確〕
考試官教授黃　批〔敷暢〕
===
記者推福之義亦惟悉有衆善而已夫福未易
致也萃衆善而歸之身其爲福也孰盛焉此固
祭之所與而賢者之所獨受也今夫致祭雖無
徼福之心而盡義自有獲福之理人知賢者之
有福也而不知福也者備之謂也夫苟得此而
遺彼則身之所利者恒少而其所不足者恒多
謂之福不可也人知備之爲福也而不知備也
者百順之謂也夫茍舉百而廢一則行之所咈
者雖微而其所順者尚虧謂之備不可也夫順
punctuated:
八佾之賜，後世譏之；雍歌之徹，君子憾焉。然則僭也、濫也，爲君臣者其亦致嚴於斯。

福者，備也；備者，百順之名也。無所不順者之謂備，言內盡於己而外順於道也。

陳勛

同考試官教諭胡批〔備順二字，其旨合含畜于盡己順道發出，作者〕〔類失之支蔓，是篇體認真切，特錄之。〕
考試官教諭劉批〔意完詞確。〕
考試官教授黃批〔敷暢。〕

記者推福之義，亦惟悉有衆善而已。夫福未易致也，萃衆善而歸之身，其爲福也孰盛焉？此固祭之所與，而賢者之所獨受也。今夫致祭，雖無徼福之心，而盡義自有獲福之理。人知賢者之有福也，而不知福也者備之謂也。夫苟得此而遺彼，則身之所利者恒少，而其所不足者恒多，謂之福不可也。人知備之爲福也，而不知備也者百順之謂也。夫茍舉百而廢一，則行之所咈者雖微，而其所順者尚虧，謂之備不可也。夫順
translation_en:
…Later generations criticized the grant of eight ranks of dancers; the gentleman deplored the singing of the Yong hymn at the removal of the sacrificial offerings. Thus, concerning usurpation of ritual privileges and their indiscriminate bestowal, rulers and ministers alike must exercise strict care.

“Blessing means completeness; completeness is the name for compliance in every respect. To comply in all things is what is meant by completeness: inwardly fulfilling one’s own duties and outwardly complying with the Way.”

Chen Xun 陳勛

Associate Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: 〔The purport of the two words ‘completeness’ and ‘compliance’ should be held together implicitly and brought out through ‘fulfilling one’s own duties and complying with the Way’ [?]. Writers〕〔generally err by rambling into digressions. This essay grasps the meaning truly and precisely, and has therefore been specially selected for inclusion.〕
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: 〔The meaning is complete and the wording precise.〕
Examiner Huang, Professor, comments: 〔Ample and fluent in exposition.〕

In elucidating the meaning of blessing, the recorder means simply possessing all forms of goodness in their entirety. Blessing is not easily attained. To gather every form of goodness into oneself—what blessing could be greater? This is indeed what sacrifice confers and what the worthy alone receive. Now, although one offers sacrifice without any intention of soliciting blessings, fulfilling one’s obligations naturally carries within it the principle by which blessings are obtained. People know that the worthy possess blessings, but do not know that blessing means completeness. If one obtains this but leaves out that, the benefits accruing to oneself will always be few, while one’s deficiencies will always be many. This cannot be called blessing. People know that completeness constitutes blessing, but do not know that completeness means compliance in every respect. If one attends to a hundred things but neglects one, then, although the departure from right conduct may be slight, one’s compliance remains deficient. This cannot be called completeness. Now, compliance…

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
而至于百則亦無所不順而備其至矣然其義
何如以言乎其內也忠信以立其本無有一念
之欺內省不疚而洗心之密已精自反而縮而
屋漏之誠無忝是內無不盡矣以言乎其外也
集義以顯其仁無有一事之苟素履無咎考祥
妙元吉之旋中行獨復慎動有攸往之利是外
無不順矣是則無內也無外也而皆無所不順
則夫百順也者其斯之謂與吁備者順之積也
福者備之徵也君子亦惟求之自我而已舍是
則世俗之求而非君子之所謂福也抑論世之
求福者不曰富貴利澤則曰祿壽康寧而盡已
順道之謂未之前聞也是不然鬼神之道存乎
吉凶吉凶之道存乎我苟其身有未順則愧怍
之地皆悔吝之途也故箕子之演五福必曰攸
好德而夫子之所自求者亦曰丘之禱久矣然
則善求福者其亦求之吾心之天斯可矣
第貳場
論
punctuated:
而至于百，則亦無所不順，而備其至矣。然其義何如？以言乎其內也，忠信以立其本，無有一念之欺；內省不疚，而洗心之密已精；自反而縮，而屋漏之誠無忝：是內無不盡矣。以言乎其外也，集義以顯其仁，無有一事之苟；素履無咎，考祥妙元吉之旋；中行獨復，慎動有攸往之利：是外無不順矣。是則無內也，無外也，而皆無所不順，則夫百順也者，其斯之謂與？吁！備者，順之積也；福者，備之徵也。君子亦惟求之自我而已，舍是則世俗之求，而非君子之所謂福也。抑論世之求福者，不曰富貴利澤，則曰祿壽康寧，而盡已順道之謂，未之前聞也。是不然！鬼神之道存乎吉凶，吉凶之道存乎我。苟其身有未順，則愧怍之地，皆悔吝之途也。故箕子之演五福，必曰攸好德；而夫子之所自求者，亦曰：「丘之禱久矣。」然則善求福者，其亦求之吾心之天，斯可矣。

第貳場

論
translation_en:
…and when this compliance extends to all hundred aspects, there is nothing in which one fails to comply, and completeness reaches its utmost. But what does this mean? Speaking of the inner self, one establishes its foundation through loyalty and trustworthiness, without a single deceitful thought. Inward examination reveals no cause for remorse, and the meticulous work of cleansing the heart has already become refined. Turning back upon oneself, one finds oneself upright, and one’s sincerity even in the seclusion of one’s chamber is without shame. Thus nothing within is left unfulfilled. Speaking of outward conduct, one accumulates righteous deeds to manifest one’s benevolence, without carelessness in a single undertaking. In plain and unadorned conduct there is no blame; examining the auspices, one marvelously attains the return of supreme good fortune [?]. Walking amid others, one alone returns to the right path; acting cautiously, one finds advantage in having somewhere to proceed. Thus nothing outward fails to accord with the right. Whether inward or outward, then, there is nothing that does not accord with it. Is this not what is meant by compliance in all hundred aspects?

Ah! Completeness is the accumulation of such compliance; blessing is the evidence of completeness. The gentleman seeks it only within himself. To abandon this is to pursue what the vulgar seek, rather than what the gentleman calls blessing. Now, those in the world who seek blessings speak either of wealth, rank, profit, and benefits, or of emoluments, longevity, health, and peace. Yet one has never heard them speak of fully exerting oneself [?] and following the Way. This is mistaken! The operation of ghosts and spirits lies in good and ill fortune; the source of good and ill fortune lies in oneself. If there is anything in one’s conduct that does not accord with the right, every occasion for shame is a path to remorse and humiliation. Thus, when Jizi expounded the five blessings, he necessarily included ‘a love of virtue.’ And concerning what the Master sought for himself, he too said: ‘I, Qiu, have long been praying.’ Those who know how to seek blessings should therefore seek them in the Heaven within their own hearts. That will suffice.

Second Session

Discourse

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
誠者聖人之本
何一舉
同考試官教諭坑　批〔聖人盡性之學未易語也此作精密　無一剩語可與語誠矣〕
同考試官教諭呂　批〔聖人所以爲聖人全乎太極而已此　周子之旨也塲中作者率多補綴浮泛僅見此篇〕
考試官教諭劉　批〔論無斧鑿痕是識誠者〕
考試官教授黄　批〔充邑宏深可與語易通者〕
論曰誠者道之會也聖人所以聖者亦本諸此
===
而已矣道奚會於誠也道在天下散於萬而歸
於一非誠非也故誠者道之會也而心者誠之
管也心外無誠誠外無道人皆有之其初一也
而存焉者寡惟聖人爲能至誠盡性而不失乎
其初是故道崇而德盛化神而業廣人見其然
也而遂以爲絕德孤行望而震焉孰知夫聖人
之於民亦類也誠者人心之所同而全之者聖
人也大哉誠乎聖人以成其聖學者以成其學
舍乎此則異端而已矣而豈可以語道也哉周
punctuated:
誠者聖人之本
何一舉
同考試官教諭坑，批〔聖人盡性之學，未易語也。此作精密，無一剩語，可與語誠矣。〕
同考試官教諭呂，批〔聖人所以爲聖人，全乎太極而已，此周子之旨也。塲中作者率多補綴浮泛，僅見此篇。〕
考試官教諭劉，批〔論無斧鑿痕，是識誠者。〕
考試官教授黄，批〔充邑宏深，可與語易通者。〕
論曰：誠者，道之會也。聖人所以聖者，亦本諸此而已矣。道奚會於誠也？道在天下，散於萬而歸於一，非誠非也。故誠者，道之會也；而心者，誠之管也。心外無誠，誠外無道。人皆有之，其初一也，而存焉者寡。惟聖人爲能至誠盡性，而不失乎其初。是故道崇而德盛，化神而業廣。人見其然也，而遂以爲絕德孤行，望而震焉。孰知夫聖人之於民，亦類也？誠者，人心之所同，而全之者聖人也。大哉，誠乎！聖人以成其聖，學者以成其學。舍乎此，則異端而已矣，而豈可以語道也哉！周
translation_en:
Sincerity Is the Foundation of the Sage

He Yiju

Associate Examiner Keng [?], Instructor, comments: 〔The sage’s learning, through which he fully realizes his nature, is not easily discussed. This composition is precise and meticulous, without a single superfluous phrase. Its author is someone with whom one can discuss sincerity.〕

Associate Examiner Lü, Instructor, comments: 〔What makes a sage a sage is simply his complete realization of the Supreme Ultimate. This is Master Zhou’s meaning. Compositions in the examination hall are mostly patchwork, superficial and vague; this essay alone stands out.〕

Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: 〔The discourse bears no marks of axe or chisel. Its author understands sincerity.〕

Examiner Huang, Professor, comments: 〔Full [?], expansive, and profound: its author is someone with whom one can discuss the Book of Changes and the Penetrating the Book of Changes (Tongshu) [?].〕

The discourse states: Sincerity is where the Way converges. What makes a sage a sage likewise has its foundation in this alone. Why does the Way converge in sincerity? In all under Heaven, the Way disperses among the myriad things and returns to unity; without sincerity, this is not so [?]. Thus sincerity is where the Way converges, and the mind is the conduit of sincerity. Outside the mind there is no sincerity; outside sincerity there is no Way. Everyone possesses it, and at the beginning all are alike, yet few preserve it. Only the sage can attain perfect sincerity and fully realize his nature without losing what he originally possessed. Thus his Way is exalted and his virtue abundant; his transforming influence is wondrous and his accomplishments extensive. People see that he is so and consequently suppose his virtue to be beyond reach and his conduct without equal; they gaze upon him in awe. Who realizes that the sage belongs to the same kind as ordinary people? Sincerity is common to all human minds, but the sage realizes it completely. Great indeed is sincerity! Through it the sage fulfills his sagehood, and the learner fulfills his learning. To abandon it is merely to follow heterodox teachings. How, then, could one speak of the Way? Zhou…

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
子書曰誠者聖人之本懼聖學之不明而示之
以其的也且誠者何也誠無僞無僞則實誠無
息無息則久誠無雜無雜則一包五常統百行
是誠之所以命也嘗觀夫道之始也天地未凝
人物未生而誠之理未嘗息也所謂太極也理
秉氣機相盪相摩夫然後兩儀生焉兩儀既生
運化乃行其通也元而亨也其復也利而貞也
故曰天下雷行物與無妄無妄誠也又曰維天
之命於穆不已惟誠也故不已也是故萬物並
===
育性命各正誠道顯洩無餘蘊矣惟人也得其
秀靈形既生而性亦具焉元而爲仁也亨而爲
禮也利而爲義也貞而爲智也皆實理也而會
於心人孰無是心則亦孰無是誠雖聖人與塗
人無以異也而不能以不異者氣質也是故五
性感動善惡雜揉欲動情勝利害相攻則天命
之性於是乎始鑿而與天地不類是恒人之情
然也夫惟聖人又得其秀之秀者其氣清其質
粹是以其性不鑿而所謂誠者不學而知也不
punctuated:
子書曰：「誠者，聖人之本。」懼聖學之不明，而示之以其的也。且誠者何也？誠無僞，無僞則實；誠無息，無息則久；誠無雜，無雜則一。包五常，統百行，是誠之所以命也。嘗觀夫道之始也，天地未凝，人物未生，而誠之理未嘗息也，所謂太極也。理秉氣機，相盪相摩，夫然後兩儀生焉。兩儀既生，運化乃行。其通也，元而亨也；其復也，利而貞也。故曰：「天下雷行，物與無妄。」無妄，誠也。又曰：「維天之命，於穆不已。」惟誠也，故不已也。是故萬物並育，性命各正，誠道顯洩，無餘蘊矣。
惟人也，得其秀靈，形既生而性亦具焉。元而爲仁也，亨而爲禮也，利而爲義也，貞而爲智也，皆實理也，而會於心。人孰無是心，則亦孰無是誠？雖聖人與塗人，無以異也。而不能以不異者，氣質也。是故五性感動，善惡雜揉，欲動情勝，利害相攻，則天命之性於是乎始鑿，而與天地不類，是恒人之情然也。夫惟聖人，又得其秀之秀者，其氣清，其質粹，是以其性不鑿，而所謂誠者，不學而知也，不
translation_en:
…Master Zhou’s book says: “Sincerity is the foundation of the sage.” Fearing that the learning of the sages would not be understood, he showed learners its target. What, then, is sincerity? Sincerity contains no falsity; without falsity, it is real. Sincerity never ceases; without cessation, it endures. Sincerity contains no admixture; without admixture, it is one. It embraces the Five Constant Virtues and unifies the hundred forms of conduct: this is why it is called sincerity. I have considered the beginning of the Way: before Heaven and Earth had coalesced, before human beings and other things had been born, the principle of sincerity had never ceased. This is what is called the Supreme Ultimate. Principle governs the workings of vital force; through mutual agitation and friction, the Two Modes—yin and yang—then arise. Once the Two Modes have arisen, transformation proceeds. In its unfolding, there are origination and flourishing; in its return, there are benefit and constancy. Thus it is said: “Thunder moves beneath Heaven; all things partake of freedom from falsity.” Freedom from falsity is sincerity. It is also said: “The mandate of Heaven—ah, how profound and unceasing!” It is precisely because it is sincere that it does not cease. Thus the myriad things are nurtured together, each with its nature and allotted existence rightly established; the Way of sincerity manifests itself fully, with nothing left concealed.
Human beings alone receive its finest and most numinous essence. Once their bodily form comes into being, their nature is also complete within them. Origination becomes benevolence; flourishing becomes ritual propriety; benefit becomes righteousness; constancy becomes wisdom. These are all real principles, and they converge in the heart-mind. Who among human beings lacks this heart-mind, and thus who lacks this sincerity? Even the sage and the ordinary person on the road do not differ in this respect. What prevents them from remaining alike is their endowment of vital force and physical constitution. Thus, when the five aspects of human nature are stirred by external things, good and evil become intermingled. Desires arise, emotions prevail, and considerations of benefit and harm contend with one another. The nature bestowed by Heaven then begins to be damaged and ceases to resemble Heaven and Earth. Such is the condition of ordinary people. The sage alone receives the finest of this fine essence: his vital force is clear and his constitution pure. Consequently, his nature remains undamaged, and what is called sincerity he knows without learning, without …

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
強而能也寂然不動者誠潛而貞也感而遂通
者誠應而明也聖人一心葢純於天德而太極
在我矣由是而暢於四肢則聲爲律也身爲度
也誠之形也由是而發於事業則仁以長人非
姑息也禮以嘉會非強世也義以利物非立峻
也知以貞幹非用察也經紀張布物采昭明凡
聖人所爲皆因其機之所不容息而勢之所不
容已者所謂範圍天地之化而不過曲成萬物
而不遺誠之流衍無窮也是故盛德以極大業
===
以成天地以位萬物以育而參賛之功畢矣昔
在上世河圖洛書天不愛道矣二帝三王人不
乏聖矣其所以闡道經世者皆本於實理載在
經籍俱可考見周公而下仲尼爲盛觀其設教
葢莫先於忠信之主而其徒相與講明斯道亦
拳拳於誠意誠身之論則聖賢之意可知也秦
漢以降宗旨堙微異端並出學道者岐於他門
論治者淪於末軌矯僞日滋忠信日薄誠教不
明而其害有不可勝言者周子嗣續道樞再闢
punctuated:
強而能也。寂然不動者，誠潛而貞也；感而遂通者，誠應而明也。聖人一心，葢純於天德，而太極在我矣。由是而暢於四肢，則聲爲律也，身爲度也，誠之形也。由是而發於事業，則仁以長人，非姑息也；禮以嘉會，非強世也；義以利物，非立峻也；知以貞幹，非用察也。經紀張布，物采昭明。凡聖人所爲，皆因其機之所不容息，而勢之所不容已者。所謂範圍天地之化而不過，曲成萬物而不遺，誠之流衍無窮也。是故盛德以極，大業以成，天地以位，萬物以育，而參賛之功畢矣。
昔在上世，河圖洛書，天不愛道矣；二帝三王，人不乏聖矣。其所以闡道經世者，皆本於實理，載在經籍，俱可考見。周公而下，仲尼爲盛。觀其設教，葢莫先於忠信之主，而其徒相與講明斯道，亦拳拳於誠意誠身之論，則聖賢之意可知也。秦漢以降，宗旨堙微，異端並出。學道者岐於他門，論治者淪於末軌。矯僞日滋，忠信日薄，誠教不明，而其害有不可勝言者。周子嗣續道樞，再闢
translation_en:
…is capable without exertion. In stillness, without movement, sincerity is latent and steadfast; in responding and thereby penetrating all things, sincerity is responsive and illuminating. The sage’s single heart is wholly pure in Heaven’s virtue, and the Supreme Ultimate is present within him. When this flows freely through his four limbs, his voice becomes a musical standard and his person a measure: these are sincerity’s outward manifestations. When it issues in undertakings, he leads others through benevolence, without indulgence; brings people together harmoniously through ritual propriety, without coercing the world; benefits things through righteousness, without imposing severity; and provides a steadfast foundation through wisdom, without resorting to intrusive scrutiny. The guiding order is spread abroad, and the patterned splendor of things shines forth. Everything the sage does follows incipient movements that cannot pause and circumstances that cannot permit cessation. This is what is meant by encompassing the transformations of Heaven and Earth without overstepping them, and bringing the myriad things to completion in all their particularity without overlooking any. It is sincerity flowing forth without end. Thus abundant virtue reaches its utmost, great undertakings are accomplished, Heaven and Earth take their proper places, and the myriad things are nourished. The work of participating in and assisting their transforming activity is thereby complete.
In high antiquity, with the River Chart and the Luo Writing, Heaven did not withhold the Way; with the Two Emperors and Three Kings, humanity did not lack sages. The means by which they elucidated the Way and ordered the world were all rooted in true principle. Recorded in the canonical writings, these can all be examined and understood. After the Duke of Zhou, Zhongni was foremost. Looking at how he established his teaching, nothing took precedence over making dutifulness and trustworthiness its guiding principles. His disciples, in jointly discussing and clarifying this Way, likewise devoted themselves earnestly to discussions of making the intentions sincere and making oneself sincere. From this we can understand the intentions of the sages and worthies. From the Qin and Han onward, the essential teaching became obscured and faint, and heterodox doctrines arose together. Those studying the Way strayed into other schools, while those discussing government sank into approaches concerned with peripheral matters. Artifice and falsehood increased daily; dutifulness and trustworthiness diminished daily. The teaching of sincerity was no longer clear, and the resulting harm was beyond description. Master Zhou carried on the central teaching of the Way and opened anew…

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
渾淪是故稱人以聖爲宗稱道以誠爲本盖所
以羽翼孔氏而遺萬世之的也大造學者信其
然矣雖然聖不可遽及也可學而至誠不可徑
造也可思而入未至者主敬以基之寡欲以存
之學問以聚之致曲以充之優而游之使自得
之則能有誠矣能誠而聖可及矣故曰誠者天
之道也誠之者人之道也
表
擬宋以范仲淹參知政事富弼爲樞密副
===
使謝表〔慶曆三年〕
劉世魁
同考試官教諭坑　批〔古人愛君之意宛然可見〕
同考試官教諭呂　批〔善寫范富忠貞之心於百世之下匪〕
〔直麗則可取〕
考試官教諭劉　批〔典則〕
考試官教授黃　批〔說出范富忠愛之意〕
慶曆三年某月某日具官臣范仲淹臣富
弼伏蒙
punctuated:
渾淪。是故稱人以聖爲宗，稱道以誠爲本，盖所以羽翼孔氏而遺萬世之的也。大造學者，信其然矣。雖然，聖不可遽及也，可學而至；誠不可徑造也，可思而入。未至者，主敬以基之，寡欲以存之，學問以聚之，致曲以充之，優而游之，使自得之，則能有誠矣。能誠而聖可及矣。故曰：「誠者，天之道也；誠之者，人之道也。」

表
擬宋以范仲淹參知政事、富弼爲樞密副使謝表〔慶曆三年〕
劉世魁
同考試官教諭坑，批〔古人愛君之意，宛然可見。〕
同考試官教諭呂，批〔善寫范富忠貞之心於百世之下，匪〕〔直麗則可取。〕
考試官教諭劉，批〔典則。〕
考試官教授黃，批〔說出范富忠愛之意。〕

慶曆三年某月某日，具官臣范仲淹、臣富弼，伏蒙
translation_en:
…the undifferentiated whole. Thus, in speaking of human beings, he took sagehood as the highest aim; in speaking of the Way, he took sincerity as its foundation. This was how he supported the teachings of Confucius and bequeathed a standard to ten thousand generations. That he greatly benefited learners is indeed beyond doubt. Nevertheless, sagehood cannot be attained suddenly, but one can reach it through learning; sincerity cannot be achieved directly, but one can enter into it through reflection. Those who have not yet attained it should establish its foundation by maintaining reverence, preserve it by limiting desires, accumulate it through study and inquiry, and bring it to fullness by fully developing even partial stirrings of goodness. They should dwell in it at ease, allowing themselves to grasp it for themselves; then they can possess sincerity. Once they can be sincere, sagehood becomes attainable. Thus it is said: “Sincerity is the Way of Heaven; making oneself sincere is the way of humanity.”

Memorial
A memorial of thanks composed as if under the Song, upon the appointment of Fan Zhongyan as Assistant Administrator and Fu Bi as Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs. 〔Third year of Qingli, 1043.〕
By Liu Shikui.

Associate Examiner, Instructor Lü, comments: 〔It skillfully portrays the loyal and steadfast hearts of Fan and Fu a hundred generations later; it is not〕〔merely its elegant and disciplined writing that deserves appreciation.〕
Examiner, Instructor Liu, comments: 〔Classical and well regulated.〕
Examiner, Professor Huang, comments: 〔It expresses Fan and Fu’s loyalty and love for their sovereign.〕

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
聖恩以〔臣仲淹參知政事臣弼爲樞密副使〕
白麻焜燿文武竝用於
清朝
赤日瞻依衣冠同拜於
丹闕職分兩府
恩出一時揣分難堪抱慚共切臣等誠惶誠
恐稽首頓首上言伏以
槐閣尊崇品秩應三台之象鹿轓嚴重樞
機運萬里之籌
===
國有股肱係大安危王之爪牙在於制御一
日二日萬幾與聞於廟堂三軍六軍九伐仰
成於樽俎故虞有百揆之命帝載惟熙而周
重司馬之藿戎兵式詰姬公呂望同德懋
覇商之功曲逆絳侯結好著安劉之績茲
國家之首務實臣隣之重司已有專官允分
貳職所以賡同寅之用非止爲伴食之員
矧政曰參知蓋分藿於宰相而樞有副使
均制變於邊陲舊名雖沿李唐深意實由
punctuated: 聖恩，以〔臣仲淹參知政事臣弼爲樞密副使〕。白麻焜燿，文武竝用於清朝；赤日瞻依，衣冠同拜於丹闕。職分兩府，恩出一時。揣分難堪，抱慚共切。臣等誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首上言。伏以槐閣尊崇，品秩應三台之象；鹿轓嚴重，樞機運萬里之籌。國有股肱，係大安危；王之爪牙，在於制御。一日二日萬幾，與聞於廟堂；三軍六軍九伐，仰成於樽俎。故虞有百揆之命，帝載惟熙；而周重司馬之藿，戎兵式詰。姬公呂望同德，懋覇商之功；曲逆絳侯結好，著安劉之績。茲國家之首務，實臣隣之重司。已有專官，允分貳職，所以賡同寅之用，非止爲伴食之員。矧政曰參知，蓋分藿於宰相；而樞有副使，均制變於邊陲。舊名雖沿李唐，深意實由
translation_en:
…imperial favor, appointing 〔your servant Zhongyan as Vice Grand Councilor and your servant Bi as Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs〕. The edicts on white hemp paper shine resplendently: civil and military talents are employed together at your enlightened court. Looking reverently toward the crimson sun of Your Majesty, we officials in caps and robes bow together before the vermilion palace gates. Our duties are divided between the two councils; your favor comes to us at the same moment. Measuring our capacities, we find ourselves unequal to these appointments; both of us feel profound shame. Your servants, in fear and trembling, bow our heads to the ground and submit this memorial.

We humbly consider that the grand council chamber is exalted, its ranks corresponding to the celestial Three Terraces; the deer-adorned carriage signifies solemn authority, while the military council devises plans reaching ten thousand li. The state's ministers are its limbs, upon whom its security or peril depends; the king's fighting men are his claws and teeth, whose effectiveness depends upon direction and control. Each day brings countless affairs, in which the court's counselors share; the campaigns of the armies depend for success upon deliberations conducted over ceremonial wine vessels and sacrificial stands. Thus, under Shun, the appointment of the Chief of the Hundred Officials brought brilliance to the emperor's undertakings; Zhou likewise esteemed the authority [?] of the Minister of War, and its forces were kept in good order. The Duke of Zhou and Lü Wang were united in virtue and achieved the great work of subduing Shang [?]; the Marquis of Quni and the Marquis of Jiang formed a friendship and distinguished themselves by securing the Liu dynasty. These are the foremost concerns of the state and weighty responsibilities of the sovereign's close ministers. Dedicated officials already hold these charges, and subordinate appointments appropriately share their duties. These serve to sustain the work of colleagues united in reverence, rather than merely to provide places for idle officeholders who accompany others at meals.

Moreover, the civil office is called ‘participating in the determination of governmental affairs,’ for its holder shares the chief councilor's authority [?]; and the military council has a vice commissioner, who likewise shares responsibility for responding to changes on the frontiers. Although these old titles were inherited from the Li house of Tang, their deeper purpose actually derives from…

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
藝祖押班知印惟畀二等之階肅揖橫戈不作
三衙之態顧茲重任宜選良材伏念〔臣仲〕
淹〔臣〕弼氣乏老成才非智勇賢科發跡媿
從縻粥之寒畢等擢官誤傳鶴鴈之夢條
陳十事罔救時艱獻納二言未尊
國體志徒切於先憂後樂情每違於五起再
辭從官知耀州焚詔之罪莫追流民撫河
北救荒之政何裨職業每媿其曠瘝年力
已瀆於衰鈍自甘草腐詎意鶯遷冒此高
華轉增危慄茲蓋伏遇
===
○○○○
至誠至聖
允武允文
運撫盈成紹
一祖二宗之緒
命凝中正得四方萬國之心御
經筵而盛暑弗停開天章而日旰罔暇食給
戒無窮之欲思羊存不殺之仁連茹拔茅
punctuated: 藝祖。押班知印，惟畀二等之階；肅揖橫戈，不作三衙之態。顧茲重任，宜選良材。伏念〔臣仲〕淹〔臣〕弼，氣乏老成，才非智勇。賢科發跡，媿從縻粥之寒；畢等擢官，誤傳鶴鴈之夢。條陳十事，罔救時艱；獻納二言，未尊國體。志徒切於先憂後樂，情每違於五起再辭。從官知耀州，焚詔之罪莫追；流民撫河北，救荒之政何裨？職業每媿其曠瘝，年力已瀆於衰鈍。自甘草腐，詎意鶯遷？冒此高華，轉增危慄。茲蓋伏遇○○○○，至誠至聖，允武允文，運撫盈成，紹一祖二宗之緒；命凝中正，得四方萬國之心。御經筵而盛暑弗停，開天章而日旰罔暇。食給戒無窮之欲，思羊存不殺之仁。連茹拔茅，
translation_en:
…the dynastic founder. Presiding over court attendance and holding the seal were entrusted only to officials of the secondary grades [?]; in their solemn salutations and bearing of weapons, they did not adopt the manner of the Three Military Commands. Such weighty responsibilities should indeed be entrusted to worthy men.
We humbly reflect that we, your servants Zhongyan and Bi—Fan Zhongyan and Fu Bi—lack the bearing of seasoned men, and our abilities possess neither wisdom nor courage. We began our careers through the examination for worthy men, ashamed of our humble circumstances and cold gruel [?]; we were promoted to office in ranked order [?], undeservedly fulfilling the dream of cranes and wild geese. Our presentation of ten proposals failed to remedy the difficulties of the times; our submission of two counsels failed to uphold the dignity of the state. Our resolve was earnestly, yet vainly, to worry before others and rejoice after them; our wishes were repeatedly thwarted amid five summonses to rise and two refusals [?]. Appointed from the court attendants to administer Yaozhou, we could not undo the offense of burning the edict; tending the displaced people in Hebei, what benefit did our famine relief measures bring? We are ever ashamed of neglecting our official duties, and our years and strength have already sunk into decrepitude and dullness. Content to decay like grass, how could we have expected to rise like the oriole? Undeservedly receiving this lofty distinction, we feel all the more apprehensive and fearful.
This is because we have humbly encountered Your Majesty [four circle marks in the text], supremely sincere and supremely sagely, truly accomplished in war and in letters. Presiding over an age of fullness and achievement, you continue the legacy of the founding ancestor and the two ancestral emperors. Your mandate rests firmly in centrality and rectitude, winning the hearts of all lands in the four directions. You attend the Classics Colloquium without interruption even in the height of summer; you open the Tianzhang Pavilion and, though the day grows late, allow yourself no respite. In providing food, you guard against limitless desires [?]; mindful of sheep, you preserve the benevolence that refrains from killing [?]. Pulling up the couch grass with its intertwined roots…

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
群賢在位西征北伐五利和戎憂毋釐於
兵民求應切於將相謬以樗朽竝掌樞衡
御墨初須驚
宸恩之旣渥新貂對侍懼輿望之難孚賚鍊致
凶有靦面目循牆引避莫遂衷情臣等敢
不羿翟矢心犬馬圖報和衷密府壯懷共
奮於雲霄正色明時國是敢分於水火敷
文教以贊化試調神鼎之羹講武事而宣
威學弄中軍之鉞庶竭駑鈍少荅鴻私伏願
===
從諫如流
用人惟己勵精圖治憂勤無間於始終居重
馭輕威德常加於中外天地位而萬物育
保壽南山
皇圖固而
國祚綿齊尊北斗臣無任瞻
天仰
聖感戴屏營之至謹奉
表稱
punctuated: 群賢在位，西征北伐，五利和戎，憂毋釐於兵民，求應切於將相。謬以樗朽，竝掌樞衡。御墨初須，驚宸恩之旣渥；新貂對侍，懼輿望之難孚。賚鍊致凶，有靦面目；循牆引避，莫遂衷情。臣等敢不羿翟矢心，犬馬圖報？和衷密府，壯懷共奮於雲霄；正色明時，國是敢分於水火？敷文教以贊化，試調神鼎之羹；講武事而宣威，學弄中軍之鉞。庶竭駑鈍，少荅鴻私。伏願從諫如流，用人惟己，勵精圖治，憂勤無間於始終；居重馭輕，威德常加於中外。天地位而萬物育，保壽南山；皇圖固而國祚綿，齊尊北斗。臣無任瞻天仰聖、感戴屏營之至，謹奉表稱
translation_en:
…Worthy men fill the offices. Campaigns advance westward and northward, and the five advantages bring peace with the Rong [?]. Your concern for soldiers and common people [?] finds an urgent response in your search for generals and chief ministers. Though we are as useless as rotten ailanthus wood, we have mistakenly been entrusted together with the central direction of affairs. At first receiving the imperial writing [?], we were astonished by the abundance of Your Majesty’s favor; newly wearing sable insignia and attending you together, we feared that we could scarcely fulfill public expectations. “Bestowal, refining, bringing calamity” [?]: our faces are filled with shame. Keeping close to the wall, we sought to withdraw, yet could not realize our heartfelt wish.

How could we, your servants, fail to pledge our hearts with “Yi and Di” [?] and seek to repay you with the devotion of dogs and horses? United in purpose within the privy offices, we shall together raise our aspirations to the clouds. Upright in demeanor in this enlightened age, how could we dare divide over national policy like water and fire? We shall spread civil instruction to assist your transforming influence, attempting to season the broth in the sacred cauldron; we shall attend to military affairs to proclaim your might, learning to wield the battle-axe of the central army. We hope to exhaust our meager abilities and repay some small part of your immense personal favor.

We humbly wish that you may accept remonstrance as readily as flowing water and exercise your own judgment in employing men; that you may devote your energies to good government, remaining unceasingly solicitous and diligent from beginning to end; and that, occupying the commanding center and controlling the subordinate parts, you may continually extend your majesty and virtue within and beyond the realm. May Heaven and Earth take their proper places and all things flourish; may your longevity endure like the Southern Mountain. May the imperial enterprise be secure and the dynasty’s allotted years stretch on, its exaltation equal to the Northern Dipper. Your servant, gazing toward Heaven and looking up to the Sage, cannot contain his utmost gratitude, reverence, and trembling awe. I respectfully present this memorial to express…

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
謝以
聞
