第一問
吳崇德
同考試官教諭沈　批〔郊禘大禮非聖人不能作我〕
皇上制禮之精意子能揄揚備悉其亦窺仁孝之旨者矣錄之
考試官教諭劉　批〔際禮樂明備之時子其沐浴膏〕
===
〔澤而有得者故其說詳〕
考試官教授黃　批〔仁孝相關之意揄揚明悉〕
有聖人之德而後可以立大祀之本有聖
人之智而後可以論大祀之制大祀者何
郊社以事帝祇禘嘗以事先祖聖人所以
父天母地尊祖敬宗而隆本始之道也是
故其情深其事大苟非有聖人之德則誠
敬不足以達天人之際而本不立非有聖
人之智則聰明不足以貫人神之分而制
punctuated:
謝以聞。

第叁場
策五道
第一問
吳崇德

同考試官教諭沈　批〔郊禘大禮，非聖人不能作。我〕皇上制禮之精意，子能揄揚備悉，其亦窺仁孝之旨者矣。錄之。

考試官教諭劉　批〔際禮樂明備之時，子其沐浴膏〕〔澤而有得者，故其說詳。〕

考試官教授黃　批〔仁孝相關之意，揄揚明悉。〕

有聖人之德，而後可以立大祀之本；有聖人之智，而後可以論大祀之制。大祀者何？郊社以事帝祇，禘嘗以事先祖，聖人所以父天母地、尊祖敬宗，而隆本始之道也。是故其情深，其事大。苟非有聖人之德，則誠敬不足以達天人之際，而本不立；非有聖人之智，則聰明不足以貫人神之分，而制
translation_en:
…to express thanks and bring this to Your Majesty’s attention.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions
First Question
Wu Chongde

Comment by Associate Examiner Shen, Instructor: “The great rites of the suburban sacrifice and the di ancestral sacrifice can be instituted only by a sage. You have fully and comprehensively elucidated the profound intentions behind Our Emperor’s establishment of ritual. You have surely also gained insight into the meaning of benevolence and filial piety. Select this essay.”

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: “Living at a time when rites and music are clearly established and complete, you have evidently benefited from being bathed in imperial favor; hence the fullness of your exposition.”

Comment by Examiner Huang, Professor: “You have clearly and fully elucidated the interrelationship between benevolence and filial piety.”

Only with the virtue of a sage can one establish the foundation of the great sacrifices; only with the wisdom of a sage can one discuss their regulations. What are the great sacrifices? Through the suburban sacrifice and the sacrifice at the altar of soil, one serves the Lord on High and the spirits of the earth; through the di and chang ancestral sacrifices, one serves one’s forebears. These are the means by which the sage treats Heaven as father and Earth as mother, honors forebears and reveres the ancestral line, and exalts the Way of honoring roots and beginnings. Thus the feelings involved are profound, and the undertaking is momentous. Without the virtue of a sage, one’s sincerity and reverence are insufficient to reach across the boundary between Heaven and humanity, and the foundation cannot be established. Without the wisdom of a sage, one’s discernment is insufficient to comprehend the distinctions between humans and spirits, and the regulations…

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
不通本不立而祀焉者瀆而已制不通而
祀焉者妄而已瀆且妄而大祀之道微矣
是故唯孝子爲能事親唯仁人爲能享帝
仁且孝聖人也是故以情則盡以文則備
以作則聖以述則明夯皇周泱歸太一以
成太隆而禮制備矣是道也求諸在昔學
有成周而我
皇上秩正郊廟之祀直與同符先聖後聖其歸
一揆愚生於此有以仰見
===
國家復古之盛而文武周公之道復見於
今日矣彼漢唐宋世主曲士誕謾不經是惡能
望其萬一哉請爲執事梗槩其說以鳴
皇輿之熙且國之大事祀典爲重祀典之行郊
廟爲大天地者生之本也是故有郊社焉
先祖者類之本也是故有禘嘗焉昔者先
王綱綸天地經緯陰陽悉由斯禮以隆三
本唐虞尚矣夏商以來文獻不足至於成
周經制始備考諸周禮圜丘方澤地各異
punctuated:
不通。本不立而祀焉者，瀆而已；制不通而祀焉者，妄而已。瀆且妄，而大祀之道微矣。是故唯孝子爲能事親，唯仁人爲能享帝。仁且孝，聖人也。是故以情則盡，以文則備，以作則聖，以述則明。夯皇周泱，歸太一以成太隆，而禮制備矣。是道也，求諸在昔，學有成周，而我皇上秩正郊廟之祀，直與同符。先聖後聖，其歸一揆。愚生於此有以仰見國家復古之盛，而文武周公之道復見於今日矣。彼漢唐宋世主曲士，誕謾不經，是惡能望其萬一哉？請爲執事梗槩其說，以鳴皇輿之熙。
且國之大事，祀典爲重；祀典之行，郊廟爲大。天地者，生之本也，是故有郊社焉；先祖者，類之本也，是故有禘嘗焉。昔者先王綱綸天地，經緯陰陽，悉由斯禮以隆三本。唐虞尚矣，夏商以來，文獻不足；至於成周，經制始備。考諸《周禮》，圜丘方澤，地各異
translation_en:
…are not understood. To offer sacrifices without establishing their foundation is merely to profane them; to offer sacrifices without understanding their institutions is merely to act recklessly. Through profanation and recklessness, the Way of the great sacrifices declines. Thus only a filial son can serve his parents, and only a benevolent person can offer sacrifice to the Lord on High. One who is both benevolent and filial is a sage. Thus, in feeling he is wholehearted, in ceremonial forms complete, in creating sagely, and in transmitting discerning. [The wording 夯皇周泱 is unclear.] Returning to the Great One, he achieves the highest exaltation, and the ritual institutions are complete. Seeking this Way in antiquity, we have the perfected Zhou to emulate; and our Emperor, in ordering and rectifying the sacrifices at the suburban altars and ancestral temples, accords directly with its example. Earlier sages and later sages arrive at the same standard. In this, I, an unworthy student, can reverently perceive the magnificence of the dynasty’s restoration of antiquity: the Way of Kings Wen and Wu and the Duke of Zhou appears again today. How could those rulers and narrow-minded scholars of the Han, Tang, and Song, with their extravagant falsehoods and departures from the canonical standards, hope to approach even one ten-thousandth of this achievement? Allow me to outline the argument for you, honored examiners, and thereby proclaim the splendor of the imperial realm.
Among the great affairs of the state, the sacrificial ordinances hold particular weight; in carrying out those ordinances, the sacrifices at the suburban altars and ancestral temples are foremost. Heaven and Earth are the root of life; hence there are the suburban sacrifices to Heaven and the sacrifices at the altars of the soil. Ancestors are the root of human lineage; hence there are the di ancestral sacrifices and the autumn chang sacrifices. In antiquity, the former kings ordered Heaven and Earth and regulated yin and yang, relying entirely on these rites to exalt the three roots. The ages of Tang Yao and Yu Shun are remote indeed, and for the Xia and Shang onward, written records and learned testimony are insufficient. Only with the perfected Zhou did the established institutions become complete. Examining the Rites of Zhou, we find that the Round Mound and the Square Marsh each occupied a different site…

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
所陽象圓而高陰象方而下也冬至夏至
祭以時舉陽氣來復天之始陰氣潛萌地
之始也以至蒼璧黃琮辨其儀也圜鍾函
鍾異其樂也壝而不宇不敢瀆也而郊祀
備矣太廟居中左昭右穆各全其尊親盡
而祧者勢也世室並列一文一武以隆其
報百世不遷者義也既祭大祖又有禘祭
以及始祖而五年一舉既祭親廟又有祫
祭以及毀廟而三年一行酌其疎密也以
===
至羽籥干戈分其簡繁虎蜼犧象辨其降
殺籩豆齊酒量其多寡而廟祀備矣嗟乎
此文武之德而周公之制也文武盛王周
公元聖仁孝深至情文兼備大成集於古
人典則垂於後世事天事親之道無以加
矣周道既衰古禮放失漢襲秦故唐宋相
仍井泉汾陰之祭已非圜丘方澤之制然
猶知有分祭也逮六天之說行而夫婦同
牢矣屋下祭於新莽而褻慢爲甚矣或五
punctuated:
所，陽象圓而高，陰象方而下也。冬至、夏至，祭以時舉，陽氣來復，天之始；陰氣潛萌，地之始也。以至蒼璧黃琮，辨其儀也；圜鍾函鍾，異其樂也；壝而不宇，不敢瀆也。而郊祀備矣。太廟居中，左昭右穆，各全其尊。親盡而祧者，勢也；世室並列，一文一武，以隆其報，百世不遷者，義也。既祭大祖，又有禘祭以及始祖，而五年一舉；既祭親廟，又有祫祭以及毀廟，而三年一行：酌其疎密也。以至羽籥干戈，分其簡繁；虎蜼犧象，辨其降殺；籩豆齊酒，量其多寡。而廟祀備矣。
嗟乎！此文武之德，而周公之制也。文武盛王，周公元聖，仁孝深至，情文兼備，大成集於古人，典則垂於後世，事天事親之道無以加矣。周道既衰，古禮放失，漢襲秦故，唐宋相仍，井泉汾陰之祭，已非圜丘方澤之制，然猶知有分祭也。逮六天之說行，而夫婦同牢矣。屋下祭於新莽，而褻慢爲甚矣。或五
translation_en:
…sites: yang is represented by what is round and high, and yin by what is square and low. At the winter and summer solstices, sacrifices are performed in their proper seasons: the return of yang marks Heaven’s beginning, and the hidden germination of yin marks Earth’s beginning. Azure jade discs and yellow jade tubes distinguish their ceremonial forms; the Huangzhong and Hanzhong pitch standards distinguish their music. Earthen enclosures are provided, but no roofed buildings, for one dares not show irreverence. Thus the suburban sacrifices were fully provided for.
The Grand Ancestral Temple occupied the center, with the zhao temples on the left and the mu temples on the right, each preserving its due dignity. That ancestral tablets were removed to more remote shrines when their kinship connection had run its course followed from necessity. That the permanent ancestral chambers stood side by side, one for King Wen and one for King Wu, magnifying the recompense offered to them, and that their tablets remained unmoved for a hundred generations, followed from righteousness. Besides sacrifices to the grand ancestor, there was the di sacrifice, extending to the first ancestor, held once every five years. Besides sacrifices in the temples of close ancestors, there was the xia collective sacrifice, extending to ancestors whose temples had been dismantled, held once every three years. These intervals reflected a considered balance between frequency and rarity. Feather plumes and flutes, shields and spears distinguished the simpler and more elaborate dances; vessels bearing tiger, long-tailed monkey, ox, and elephant designs marked the gradations of ritual rank; and the quantities of bamboo baskets, stemmed dishes, and sacrificial and ordinary wines were duly measured. Thus the ancestral temple sacrifices were fully provided for.
Ah! These embodied the virtue of Kings Wen and Wu and the institutions established by the Duke of Zhou. Wen and Wu were illustrious kings, and the Duke of Zhou a supreme sage. Their benevolence and filial devotion were profound; inward feeling and outward ceremonial form were both fully present. They brought the achievements of the ancients to completion and transmitted exemplary standards to later ages. Nothing could surpass their way of serving Heaven and one’s parents.
Once the Way of Zhou declined, the ancient rites were dispersed and lost. The Han inherited Qin precedents, and the Tang and Song continued them in succession. The sacrifices at Jingquan [?] and Fenyin already departed from the institutions of the Round Mound and Square Pool, yet people still understood that Heaven and Earth should receive separate sacrifices. When the doctrine of the Six Heavens came into circulation, however, husband and wife shared the same sacrificial victim. Under Wang Mang’s Xin dynasty, sacrifices were performed beneath a roof, and the irreverence became extreme. Sometimes, in five…

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
年而再舉或十年而一郊而沿革靡定矣
惟宋元祐之間蓋嘗議及而蘇軾劉安世
之徒不能協心討論亦終於因陋而已其
何復古之云原廟衣冠之設已非成周宗
廟之舊然猶知有常尊也自明帝創爲同
堂異室之規而昭穆蕩然矣群廟之主合
於祫禘而混亂無別矣或一歲二十五祀
或一次二十八牢而疎數不經矣唯宋元
豐之間蓋嘗議及而陸佃何洵直之徒人
持所見竟無定論亦終於襲故而已又何
復古之云時如有待理無不復我
國家憲天立極百度惟貞而郊廟之禮尤所
嚴重然而丘澤未分昭穆未別
列聖相承誠有俟於
===
今日者矣洪惟我
皇上天縱聰明極建中和欲成
祖宗之德復申成周之制於是始有圜丘方澤
之建夏至冬至之祭以明陰陽之分以□
punctuated:
年而再舉，或十年而一郊，而沿革靡定矣。惟宋元祐之間，蓋嘗議及，而蘇軾、劉安世之徒不能協心討論，亦終於因陋而已，其何復古之云？原廟衣冠之設，已非成周宗廟之舊，然猶知有常尊也。自明帝創爲同堂異室之規，而昭穆蕩然矣。群廟之主合於祫禘，而混亂無別矣。或一歲二十五祀，或一次二十八牢，而疎數不經矣。唯宋元豐之間，蓋嘗議及，而陸佃、何洵直之徒人持所見，竟無定論，亦終於襲故而已，又何復古之云？
時如有待，理無不復。我國家憲天立極，百度惟貞，而郊廟之禮尤所嚴重。然而丘澤未分，昭穆未別，列聖相承，誠有俟於今日者矣。洪惟我皇上，天縱聰明，極建中和，欲成祖宗之德，復申成周之制。於是始有圜丘方澤之建，夏至冬至之祭，以明陰陽之分，以□
translation_en:
…twice in [five] years, or a single suburban sacrifice in ten years: continuity and change followed no settled rule. During the Yuanyou reign period of the Song, the matter was indeed discussed, but Su Shi, Liu Anshi, and others could not deliberate in concert. In the end, they merely perpetuated inadequate practices. How could this be called a restoration of antiquity? The installation of robes and caps in supplementary ancestral temples already departed from the ancestral-temple practices of the fully established Zhou, yet it still showed an understanding that the ancestors should receive enduring veneration. Once Emperor Ming instituted separate chambers within a common hall, however, the zhao and mu arrangement of ancestral generations was swept away. The spirit tablets from the various temples were brought together for the xia and di collective sacrifices, becoming confused and indistinguishable. Sometimes there were twenty-five sacrifices in a single year, or twenty-eight sets of sacrificial animals at a single ceremony: the frequency of observances accorded with no canonical rule. During the Yuanfeng reign period of the Song, the matter was indeed discussed, but Lu Dian, He Xunzhi, and others each clung to their own views and ultimately reached no settled conclusion. In the end, they merely followed established practice. Again, how could this be called a restoration of antiquity?
It was as though the times awaited their moment; there is no principle that cannot be restored. Our dynasty takes Heaven as its model and establishes the supreme standard. Its every institution is correct, and it treats the rites of suburban sacrifice and ancestral worship with particular solemnity. Yet the Mound and the Marsh remained undifferentiated, and the zhao and mu generations remained undistinguished. As our sage sovereigns succeeded one another, there was indeed something awaiting fulfillment today. We reverently reflect that our Emperor, endowed by Heaven with intelligence and discernment, establishes the supreme standard of equilibrium and harmony. Wishing to bring the virtue of his ancestors to fulfillment, he has renewed the institutions of the fully established Zhou. Thus the Circular Mound and Square Marsh were at last constructed, and sacrifices instituted at the summer and winter solstices, to make clear the distinction between yin and yang, and to [illegible] …

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
天帝之尊而屋下合祭之習革矣
昭穆群廟煥然鼎建
獻皇世廟復定徽稱五年之禘配
初祖以
太祖一歲之中肅將享於四時以致孝思以昭
功德而同堂異室之習革矣嗚呼千載不
復之禮復於一朝我
皇上經緯侔神明制作通天地於是見矣伏讀
明詔有曰郊所以祀天廟所以祀先其道一而
已矣未有不相關者也大哉
===
皇言一哉
皇心其自得於仁孝誠敬者深矣哉是以光輝
發越精蘊呈露善繼善述同符於文武周
公而非但禮文之具者也記曰仁人之事
親也如事天事天也如事親其惟我
皇上之謂乎雖然我
皇上之制蓋不止此正
先師之位崇聖教也黜浮屠之學闢異端也覩
punctuated: 天帝之尊，而屋下合祭之習革矣。昭穆群廟，煥然鼎建；獻皇世廟，復定徽稱。五年之禘，配初祖以太祖；一歲之中，肅將享於四時，以致孝思，以昭功德，而同堂異室之習革矣。嗚呼！千載不復之禮，復於一朝。我皇上經緯侔神明，制作通天地，於是見矣。伏讀明詔，有曰：「郊所以祀天，廟所以祀先，其道一而已矣，未有不相關者也。」大哉，皇言！一哉，皇心！其自得於仁孝誠敬者深矣哉！是以光輝發越，精蘊呈露，善繼善述，同符於文武周公，而非但禮文之具者也。《記》曰：「仁人之事親也如事天，事天也如事親。」其惟我皇上之謂乎！雖然，我皇上之制蓋不止此。正先師之位，崇聖教也；黜浮屠之學，闢異端也；覩
translation_en:
…the exalted status of the Lord of Heaven, and the practice of offering joint sacrifices beneath a roof was abolished. The ancestral temples, arranged in the alternating zhao and mu generations, were splendidly established anew; the Temple of the Imperial Line dedicated to Emperor Xian also received a newly determined honorific designation. At the di sacrifice held every five years, Taizu was associated with the primordial ancestor; throughout the year, offerings were solemnly presented in each of the four seasons, to express filial devotion and make manifest the ancestors’ achievements and virtue. Thus the practice of housing them in separate chambers within a common hall was abolished. Ah! Rites that had remained unrestored for a thousand years were restored in a single reign. Here we see that our Emperor’s ordering of affairs matches the divine powers, and that his institutions accord with Heaven and Earth.

Reverently reading the luminous edict, I find these words: “The suburban sacrifices serve to worship Heaven; the ancestral temples serve to worship forebears. The Way underlying them is one and the same; they have never been unrelated.” Great indeed are the imperial words! Undivided indeed is the imperial heart! How profound is his inward understanding of benevolence, filial devotion, sincerity, and reverence! Thus their radiance shines forth and their essential depths become manifest. In ably carrying on his predecessors’ purposes and undertakings, he accords with Kings Wen and Wu and the Duke of Zhou. This is more than merely furnishing the outward forms of ritual. The Record of Rites says: “The benevolent person serves his parents as he serves Heaven, and serves Heaven as he serves his parents.” Surely this speaks of our Emperor!

Yet our Emperor’s institutions extend beyond these matters. He has rectified the status of the First Teacher, thereby honoring the teaching of the sages; he has rejected Buddhist learning, thereby excluding heterodox doctrines; he has beheld…

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
耤田之耕重農事也修親蚕之儀飭
后教也神功睿績照曜寰宇皆前代帝王所不及
者是以天人並應嘉禎畢集螽斯麟趾則百
斯男而億萬載無疆之休端在玆矣愚生㴠
育聖化譬諸渴飲江河豈能測其涯涘姑因
明問而敷陳其大畧耳執事其進教之
第二問
周建邦
同考試官教諭舒　批〔周禮時制予必會通有素不爾何能〕
===
變通久之義明瑩可觀
考試官教諭劉　批〔識隨時變易之義〕
考試官教授黃　批〔通變宜民經濟之學〕
善世之道本其教變通之宜責其實生民
之道以教為本教之術經世之法也風
俗之美善治之成皆由此出古之教人也
以實其取人也亦以實時異勢殊則有變
通之宜法可變而其實不可變也實不變
則法雖變猶不變也待措不同同歸于治
punctuated:
耤田之耕，重農事也；修親蚕之儀，飭后教也。神功睿績，照曜寰宇，皆前代帝王所不及者。是以天人並應，嘉禎畢集。螽斯麟趾，則百斯男，而億萬載無疆之休，端在玆矣。愚生㴠育聖化，譬諸渴飲江河，豈能測其涯涘？姑因明問，而敷陳其大畧耳。執事其進教之。

第二問
周建邦
同考試官教諭舒　批〔周禮時制，予必會通有素，不爾何能〕變通久之義，明瑩可觀。
考試官教諭劉　批〔識隨時變易之義〕
考試官教授黃　批〔通變宜民，經濟之學〕

善世之道，本其教；變通之宜，責其實。生民之道，以教為本。教之術，經世之法也。風俗之美，善治之成，皆由此出。古之教人也以實，其取人也亦以實。時異勢殊，則有變通之宜。法可變，而其實不可變也。實不變，則法雖變，猶不變也。待措不同，同歸于治。
translation_en:
…plowing the imperial ritual field gives weight to agriculture; refining the ceremonial observances for the empress’s personal tending of silkworms puts in order the instruction she imparts. His divine achievements and sagacious accomplishments illuminate the whole realm, surpassing those of the emperors and kings of former ages. Thus Heaven and humankind respond together, and auspicious signs all assemble. As evoked by “Locusts” and “The Qilin’s Hoof,” there will be sons by the hundred: here indeed lies the beginning of boundless blessings for countless ages. Nurtured by the sage’s transforming influence, I, an unworthy student, am like a thirsty man drinking from the great rivers: how could I fathom their limits? In response to your discerning question, I have merely set forth their broad outlines. May you offer me further instruction.

Second Question
Zhou Jianbang
Associate Examiner Shu, Instructor, comments: 〔“Regarding the Rites of Zhou and contemporary institutions, [he?] must long have mastered their interconnections; otherwise, how could he…” [The character 予, ‘I,’ is doubtful here.〕 “The meaning of adaptation and endurance is lucid and worthy of attention.”
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: 〔“He understands the principle of changing in accordance with the times.”〕
Examiner Huang, Professor, comments: 〔“Adapting institutions to benefit the people: learning suited to ordering the state and bringing relief to the world.”〕

The way to improve the world rests on its instruction; appropriate adaptation requires substantive results. The way to sustain the people takes instruction as its foundation. The methods of instruction are the means of ordering the world. Beautiful customs and the achievement of good government all arise from this. In antiquity, instruction concerned substantive attainment, and the selection of men likewise rested on substantive attainment. When times and circumstances differ, appropriate adaptations are required. Institutions may change, but their underlying substance must not change. If that substance remains unchanged, then even when institutions change, it is as though they have not changed. The measures employed [?] differ, yet all lead alike to good order…

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
耳識治體者可以觀矣今夫周之治天下
也内有六鄉之法所置有比長閭胥族師
黨正也外有六遂之法所置有鄰長里宰
鄰長鄙師也大司徒以鄉三物教萬民而
賓興之所謂三物六德六行六藝也鄉大
夫三年大比攷其有六德六行而爲賢通
夫六藝之道而爲能是能遵大司徒之教
而成其材矣於是鄉老及鄉大夫帥胥師
正長之屬合閭族州黨之人行鄉飲之禮
===
用賓客之儀以興舉之書于簡册獻賢能
之書于王王拜受之其重之如此以賢才
之生乃天之所遺以共理天下者國家之
元氣實有在乎此也朱子謂比閭族黨之
法正周公建太平之基本蓋有周自家黨
至於國皆有教之之地民生八歲則入小
學是天下無不教之民既天下之人莫不
從教小人修身君子明道夫故賢才群聚
于朝良善成風於下禮義大行習俗粹美
punctuated:
耳。識治體者可以觀矣。今夫周之治天下也，内有六鄉之法，所置有比長、閭胥、族師、黨正也；外有六遂之法，所置有鄰長、里宰、鄰長、鄙師也。大司徒以鄉三物教萬民而賓興之，所謂三物，六德、六行、六藝也。鄉大夫三年大比，攷其有六德六行而爲賢，通夫六藝之道而爲能，是能遵大司徒之教而成其材矣。於是鄉老及鄉大夫帥胥師正長之屬，合閭族州黨之人，行鄉飲之禮，用賓客之儀以興舉之，書于簡册，獻賢能之書于王，王拜受之。其重之如此，以賢才之生，乃天之所遺以共理天下者，國家之元氣實有在乎此也。
朱子謂比閭族黨之法，正周公建太平之基本。蓋有周自家黨至於國，皆有教之之地。民生八歲則入小學，是天下無不教之民。既天下之人莫不從教，小人修身，君子明道，夫故賢才群聚于朝，良善成風於下，禮義大行，習俗粹美，
translation_en:
…that is all. Those who understand the essentials of governance may discern them here. Now, when the Zhou governed All under Heaven, within the capital region they had the system of six districts (xiang), with Neighborhood Heads (bizhang), Ward Heads (lüxu), Clan Preceptors (zushi), and Community Heads (dangzheng); beyond it they had the system of six townships (sui), with Neighborhood Heads (linzhang), Village Heads (lizai), Neighborhood Heads (linzhang) [? repeated in the transcription], and Section Preceptors (bishi). The Minister of Education (da situ) taught the people through the three categories of district instruction and promoted the worthy with the honors accorded to guests. These three categories were the six virtues, the six forms of conduct, and the six arts. Every three years, the District Grand Masters (xiang dafu) conducted a great assessment: they examined those possessing the six virtues and six forms of conduct and deemed them worthy, and those conversant with the six arts and deemed them capable. These were people who had followed the Minister of Education’s instruction and developed their talents. Thereupon, the District Elders (xiang lao) and District Grand Masters led their subordinate heads, preceptors, and other officers, assembled the people of the wards, clans, precincts, and communities, and performed the district drinking ceremony. They employed the ceremonial honors accorded to guests to recommend and advance these men, recorded their names on tablets, and presented the register of the worthy and capable to the king. The king received it with a bow. Such was the importance attached to them, for men of worth and talent are Heaven’s gift to assist in governing All under Heaven; the vital force of the state truly resides in them.
Master Zhu said that the system of neighborhoods, wards, clans, and communities was precisely the foundation upon which the Duke of Zhou established great peace. Under the Zhou, from households and communities up to the capital, there were places of instruction everywhere. At eight years of age, children entered elementary school; thus, throughout All under Heaven, no one was left untaught. Since everyone followed this instruction, common people cultivated their persons, and gentlemen illuminated the Way. Hence men of worth and talent gathered at court, goodness became customary among the people below, ritual and righteousness widely prevailed, and customs were pure and admirable…

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
刑罰雖設而不犯此有周之大平由教而
致也我
朝稽古定制純用六典天下州縣每百一十
戶為一里十戶為一甲每甲有長
製為木鐸訓詞曰孝順父毋尊敬長上和睦
鄉里教訓子孫各安生理毋作非為
聖謨洋洋
嘉言孔彰教民之道盡之矣夫是詞也使貧而
老者振之以警衆生斯世為斯民是聽是
===
守而不忽焉卽三代直道之民矣又置社
學延師儒以教民閒子弟郡縣設為學校
以教民閒之俊秀三年大比取士以興賢
能夫里甲之制卽周之比閭族黨也社學
郡縣學卽周之小學大學也教之法純用
孔子之道卽周之教德行道藝也然法久
則弊振作維時里甲之設木鐸之詞善矣
有司行之不以其實其視相糾相受之法
何知也今日惟在守令修舉廢墜使里甲
punctuated: 刑罰雖設而不犯，此有周之大平由教而致也。我朝稽古定制，純用六典。天下州縣，每百一十戶為一里，十戶為一甲，每甲有長。製為木鐸訓詞曰：「孝順父毋，尊敬長上，和睦鄉里，教訓子孫，各安生理，毋作非為。」聖謨洋洋，嘉言孔彰，教民之道盡之矣。夫是詞也，使貧而老者振之以警衆。生斯世，為斯民，是聽是守而不忽焉，卽三代直道之民矣。又置社學，延師儒以教民閒子弟；郡縣設為學校，以教民閒之俊秀；三年大比，取士以興賢能。夫里甲之制，卽周之比閭族黨也；社學、郡縣學，卽周之小學、大學也；教之法純用孔子之道，卽周之教德行道藝也。然法久則弊，振作維時。里甲之設、木鐸之詞善矣，有司行之不以其實，其視相糾相受之法何知也？今日惟在守令修舉廢墜，使里甲
translation_en:
…Although punishments were established, no one incurred them. Such was the great peace of the Zhou, achieved through education. Our dynasty examined antiquity to establish its institutions, following entirely the Six Codes. Throughout the subprefectures and counties of the realm, every 110 households constitute a li, and ten households constitute a jia, each with its own head. Admonitions were composed for proclamation with a wooden-clapper bell: “Be filial and obedient to your father and mother [?]; respect your elders and superiors; live harmoniously with your neighbors; instruct your children and grandchildren; each attend peaceably to your livelihood; commit no wrongful acts.” Vast are these sagely counsels, and brilliantly manifest these excellent words: they fully encompass the way of educating the people. Elderly people of limited means are charged with sounding the bell and proclaiming these words to admonish the populace. Those born into this age as its people who heed and observe these words without neglect are indeed people following the upright way of the Three Dynasties.

Community schools were also established, and learned teachers invited to instruct the children of ordinary people. Schools were established in prefectures and counties to educate the outstanding talents among the populace. Every three years, a great examination selects scholars to advance the worthy and capable. The li-jia system corresponds to the Zhou neighborhood groupings of bi, lü, zu, and dang. Community schools and prefectural and county schools correspond to the Zhou elementary and higher schools. Their method of instruction follows entirely the Way of Confucius, corresponding to Zhou instruction in virtue, conduct, the Way, and the arts.

Yet institutions develop defects over time, and their revitalization must be timely. The establishment of the li-jia system and the admonitions proclaimed with the wooden-clapper bell are excellent. But when the responsible officials implement them without giving effect to their substance, what understanding do they show of the methods of mutual correction and mutual reception? What is needed today is simply for prefects and county magistrates to restore what has fallen into disuse, so that the li-jia system…

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
寓保伍之法木鐸有相受之意何患善俗
之不成哉學校之教純用孔子之道善矣
學者有不務實其視德行道藝之教何如
也修之學校如此應之於科舉何所擇哉
科舉之法自唐宋以來未之有改也時也
大儒朱子曰居今之時使孔子復生不免
應舉豈能累孔子斯言也責實之謂也我
朝嘗用建議者以德行經義治事造士行之
既久不能無廢弛之弊今日惟在董學憲
===
臣申明舊章以行學政督責提調師儒恪
循是教以責其實庶乎周官以鄉三物教
民之意則科舉不患不得人使賢者在位
能者在職天下之善治所繇以致矣然此
則任世道者之責也愚何敢與於斯
第三問
何一舉
同考試官教諭坑　批〔仁敬類能言之而統一之旨精一之功漫無定見此作條對詳明蓋其從事於心學者〕
punctuated:
寓保伍之法，木鐸有相受之意，何患善俗之不成哉？學校之教純用孔子之道，善矣。學者有不務實，其視德行道藝之教何如也？修之學校如此，應之於科舉，何所擇哉？科舉之法，自唐宋以來未之有改也，時也。大儒朱子曰：「居今之時，使孔子復生，不免應舉，豈能累孔子？」斯言也，責實之謂也。我朝嘗用建議者，以德行、經義、治事造士，行之既久，不能無廢弛之弊。今日惟在董學憲臣申明舊章，以行學政，督責提調師儒，恪循是教，以責其實。庶乎周官以鄉三物教民之意，則科舉不患不得人，使賢者在位，能者在職，天下之善治所繇以致矣。然此則任世道者之責也，愚何敢與於斯？
第三問
何一舉
同考試官教諭坑，批〔仁敬類能言之，而統一之旨、精一之功，漫無定見。此作條對詳明，蓋其從事於心學者。〕
translation_en:
…embody the system of mutual-security groups, and ensure that proclamations made with the wooden-clapper bell convey the intention of mutual acceptance and assistance. Why then worry that good customs will not be established? That instruction in schools follows exclusively the Way of Confucius is good indeed. Yet some students do not pursue its substance: how does their conduct measure up to instruction in virtue, conduct, the Way, and the arts? If their cultivation in school is of this sort, what choice will there be when they present themselves for the civil-service examinations? The examination system has remained unchanged since the Tang and Song dynasties: such are the circumstances of the age. The great Confucian master Zhu Xi said, “Living in the present age, even if Confucius were reborn, he could not avoid sitting the examinations. How could this compromise Confucius?” These words mean that one must demand substance.

Our dynasty once adopted a proposal to train scholars through virtue and conduct, interpretation of the Classics, and the management of affairs. After this had been practiced for a long time, neglect and laxity inevitably arose. What is needed today is for the surveillance official overseeing education to reaffirm the established regulations in administering education, and to hold the proctors and teachers responsible for faithfully following this instruction and demanding substantive results. This would approach the intention of the Offices of Zhou in teaching the people through the three categories of community instruction. There would then be no need to fear that the examinations would fail to obtain suitable men: the worthy would occupy positions of authority and the capable would hold office. This is how good government throughout the realm would be achieved. Yet this is the responsibility of those charged with the moral order of the age. How could someone as ignorant as I presume to take part in it?

Third Policy Question

He Yiju

Comment by Associate Examiner Keng [?], Instructor: 〔Most can speak of benevolence and reverent attentiveness, yet they have no settled understanding of the principle that unifies them or of the work of refinement and single-mindedness. This essay answers point by point, thoroughly and clearly; its author is evidently one who devotes himself to the learning of the mind.〕

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭呂　批〔仁是本體敬是工夫主敬即是求仁　聖賢之言雖不一旨則無二此策正能及之允式多士〕
考試官教諭劉　批〔精確〕
考試官教授黃　批〔說仁敬明白〕
聖人之道存乎仁聖人之學存乎敬仁也
者天地之德也人之心也萬物之體也全
之者聖人也故曰聖人之道教者不以仁
則非所以爲教學者不以仁則非所以爲
學敬者聖學之功也故曰敬則即是禮無
===
已可克求仁者舍敬其何以哉先儒陸象
山曰仁自夫子發之何也自堯舜禹湯文
武相傳一中也而夫子始以仁教人考之
詩書未嘗言仁之體也至吾夫子贊易乃
發仁之體曰元者善之長也又曰復其見
天地之心乎見於論語教門人皆求仁之
功而孟子曰人皆有不忍人之心又曰惻
隱之心仁也仁之理在我矣孟子沒而聖
人之學不傳至于有宋眞儒輩出道明之
punctuated:
同考試官教諭呂，批〔仁是本體，敬是工夫，主敬即是求仁。聖賢之言雖不一，旨則無二。此策正能及之，允式多士。〕
考試官教諭劉，批〔精確。〕
考試官教授黃，批〔說仁敬明白。〕
聖人之道存乎仁，聖人之學存乎敬。仁也者，天地之德也，人之心也，萬物之體也。全之者聖人也，故曰聖人之道。教者不以仁，則非所以爲教；學者不以仁，則非所以爲學。敬者，聖學之功也。故曰：「敬則即是禮，無已可克。」求仁者舍敬，其何以哉？先儒陸象山曰：「仁自夫子發之。」何也？自堯舜禹湯文武相傳，一中也，而夫子始以仁教人。考之《詩》《書》，未嘗言仁之體也。至吾夫子贊《易》，乃發仁之體，曰：「元者，善之長也。」又曰：「復，其見天地之心乎！」見於《論語》，教門人皆求仁之功。而孟子曰：「人皆有不忍人之心。」又曰：「惻隱之心，仁也。」仁之理在我矣。孟子沒而聖人之學不傳，至于有宋，眞儒輩出，道明之
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Lü, Instructor, comments: 〔Humaneness is the fundamental substance; reverence is the practical work. Maintaining reverence is precisely seeking humaneness. Though the words of the sages and worthies differ, their purport is one. This policy essay addresses precisely this point and can indeed serve as a model for the many candidates.〕
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: 〔Precise and sound.〕
Examiner Huang, Professor, comments: 〔Explains humaneness and reverence clearly.〕
The Way of the sages resides in humaneness; the learning of the sages resides in reverence. Humaneness is the virtue of Heaven and Earth, the heart of human beings, and the substance of the myriad things. Those who realize it fully are sages; hence it is called the Way of the sages. Teaching that does not proceed through humaneness is not true teaching; learning that does not proceed through humaneness is not true learning. Reverence is the practical work of sagely learning. Thus it is said: “Reverence is itself ritual propriety; there is no self left to overcome [?].” If those seeking humaneness abandon reverence, by what means can they proceed?
The earlier Confucian scholar Lu Xiangshan said: “Humaneness was first brought to light by the Master.” Why is this? What Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu transmitted to one another was the single principle of the Mean; it was the Master who first taught people through humaneness. If we examine the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents, they never discuss the substance of humaneness. Only when our Master composed his commentaries on the Book of Changes did he reveal its substance, saying: “The primal is the chief of all goodness.” He also said: “In Return, do we not see the heart of Heaven and Earth!” As recorded in the Analects, his instruction to his disciples concerned throughout the practical work of seeking humaneness. Mencius said: “Everyone has a heart that cannot bear the suffering of others.” He also said: “The heart of compassion is humaneness.” The principle of humaneness thus resides within us.
After Mencius died, the learning of the sages ceased to be transmitted. With the advent of the Song, true Confucian scholars appeared in succession, and the illumination of the Way…

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
會也程明道曰仁者與物同體義禮知信
皆仁也言仁爲全德也又曰萬物之生意
最可觀此元者善之長也言萬物一仁也
伊川曰偏言則一事專言則包四者言四
端皆仁也又曰仁者天下之公善之本也
言萬善皆仁也至若横渠張子之言禮儀
三百威儀三千無一物而非仁也蓋言仁
體事而無不在也紫陽朱子之言天地生
生之理這箇動意未嘗止息蓋言仁爲天
===
地生生之理也分而言之固有不同合而
觀之則皆發明仁之理者無不盡也學者
求之於心可以得之矣求仁之功莫要於
敬也詩書所載列聖之功皆敬也吾夫子
亦曰修已以敬豈有異乎孟子曰勿忘勿
助敬之旨也周子以無欲爲學蓋無欲則
一不謂之敬乎明道以敬而不自得者爲
心生乃示人曰容貌必端言語必正者非
是道獨善其身要人道如何只是天理合
punctuated:
會也。程明道曰：「仁者與物同體，義禮知信皆仁也。」言仁爲全德也。又曰：「萬物之生意最可觀，此元者善之長也。」言萬物一仁也。伊川曰：「偏言則一事，專言則包四者。」言四端皆仁也。又曰：「仁者天下之公，善之本也。」言萬善皆仁也。至若横渠張子之言「禮儀三百，威儀三千，無一物而非仁也」，蓋言仁體事而無不在也。紫陽朱子之言「天地生生之理，這箇動意未嘗止息」，蓋言仁爲天地生生之理也。分而言之，固有不同；合而觀之，則皆發明仁之理者，無不盡也。學者求之於心，可以得之矣。

求仁之功，莫要於敬也。詩書所載列聖之功，皆敬也。吾夫子亦曰：「修已以敬。」豈有異乎？孟子曰：「勿忘勿助。」敬之旨也。周子以無欲爲學，蓋無欲則一，不謂之敬乎？明道以敬而不自得者爲心生，乃示人曰：「容貌必端，言語必正者，非是道獨善其身，要人道如何，只是天理合
translation_en:
…a time when the Way became clear. Cheng Mingdao said: “The benevolent person forms one body with all things; righteousness, ritual propriety, wisdom, and trustworthiness are all benevolence.” This means that benevolence is virtue in its entirety. He also said: “The vital impulse of all things is most worthy of contemplation. This is what is meant by ‘The originating is the chief of all goodness.’” This means that one benevolence pervades all things. Yichuan said: “Spoken of as one aspect, it is a single matter; spoken of comprehensively, it embraces the four.” This means that the four beginnings are all benevolence. He also said: “Benevolence is the impartiality of all under Heaven and the foundation of goodness.” This means that all forms of goodness are benevolence. As for Master Zhang of Hengqu’s statement, “The three hundred rules of ritual and the three thousand rules of deportment contain nothing that is not benevolence,” it means that benevolence embodies itself in affairs and is present everywhere. Master Zhu of Ziyang’s statement, “The principle by which Heaven and Earth continually generate life—this impulse to activity never ceases,” means that benevolence is the principle by which Heaven and Earth continually generate life. Considered separately, these statements certainly differ; viewed together, they all elucidate the principle of benevolence, leaving nothing unexplained. Students can attain it by seeking it within their own hearts.

In the work of seeking benevolence, nothing is more essential than reverent attentiveness. The efforts of the succession of sages recorded in the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents all consisted in reverent attentiveness. Our Master likewise said: “Cultivate oneself through reverent attentiveness.” How could there be any difference? Mengzi said: “Neither forget it nor help it grow.” This expresses the purport of reverent attentiveness. Master Zhou made freedom from desires the basis of learning. For freedom from desires brings unity; should this not be called reverent attentiveness? Mingdao regarded reverent attentiveness without inward fulfillment as a sign that the heart was still unpracticed. He therefore instructed people, saying: “One’s appearance must be dignified and one’s speech correct. This is not a matter of perfecting oneself alone and wanting others to say something of one [?]; it is simply that the principle of Heaven requires…”

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
如此本無私意只是箇循理而已以循理
爲敬諸儒之所未及也或問敬伊川曰主
一之謂敬問一曰無適之謂一蓋一者天
理也易曰天下之動貞夫一者也至於朱
子以畏爲敬書曰兢兢業業其義彰矣若
謂惻隱之心仁之端也於此求之則不差
矣此南軒之論灼見端緒其於諸儒之見
蓋相符焉此其所以爲孔門之學也夫道
一也吾夫子於易曰百姓日用而不知而
===
於論語曰未有小人而仁者也於此默識
可以知仁矣又曰仁遠乎哉我欲仁斯仁
至矣此則直指求仁之必得學者豈可不
從事於心學乎愚也章句末學未之有得
也姑述所聞以對執事其進而教之幸甚
第四問
曾士文
同考試官教諭胡　批〔論相一策正欲觀學者自期何如塲中作者類能品第但不知相業之本子獨有見於此其志可知而識〕
punctuated:
如此，本無私意，只是箇循理而已。以循理爲敬，諸儒之所未及也。或問敬，伊川曰：「主一之謂敬。」問一，曰：「無適之謂一。」蓋一者，天理也。《易》曰：「天下之動，貞夫一者也。」至於朱子，以畏爲敬，《書》曰：「兢兢業業。」其義彰矣。若謂「惻隱之心，仁之端也」，於此求之，則不差矣。此南軒之論，灼見端緒，其於諸儒之見，蓋相符焉。此其所以爲孔門之學也。夫道一也。吾夫子於《易》曰：「百姓日用而不知。」而於《論語》曰：「未有小人而仁者也。」於此默識，可以知仁矣。又曰：「仁遠乎哉？我欲仁，斯仁至矣。」此則直指求仁之必得。學者豈可不從事於心學乎？愚也，章句末學，未之有得也。姑述所聞，以對執事，其進而教之，幸甚。
第四問
曾士文
同考試官教諭胡　批〔論相一策，正欲觀學者自期何如。塲中作者類能品第，但不知相業之本。子獨有見於此，其志可知，而識〕
translation_en:
…thus; there is originally no selfish intent, only adherence to principle. To define reverent attentiveness as adherence to principle goes beyond what the other Confucian scholars had attained. Someone asked Yichuan about reverent attentiveness. He replied, “Concentrating on the one is called reverent attentiveness.” Asked about the one, he replied, “Not straying elsewhere is called oneness.” This one is the principle of Heaven. The Book of Changes says, “The movements of all under Heaven find their constancy in the one.” As for Master Zhu, he defined reverent attentiveness in terms of awe. The Book of Documents says, “Fearful and vigilant”; its meaning is thereby made clear. As for the saying, “The heart of compassion is the beginning of benevolence,” if one seeks benevolence here, one will not go astray. This argument of Nanxuan clearly perceives its beginnings and accords with the views of the other Confucian scholars. This is why it constitutes the learning of Confucius’s school.
The Way is one. In the Book of Changes, our Master says, “The common people use it daily without knowing it.” Yet in the Analects he says, “There has never been a petty man who was benevolent.” By silently apprehending this, one can understand benevolence. He also says, “Is benevolence far away? If I desire benevolence, benevolence is here.” This directly indicates that seeking benevolence will assuredly attain it. How could students fail to devote themselves to the learning of the mind? I, in my ignorance, am merely a student of textual minutiae and have not attained it. I have provisionally set down what I have heard in reply to you, sir. I would count it a great good fortune if you would further instruct me.
Fourth Question
Zeng Shiwen
Comment by Associate Examiner Hu, Instructor: 〔This policy question on chief ministers was intended precisely to reveal what students aspire to. Most candidates in the examination hall can rank and evaluate them, but do not understand the foundation of a chief minister’s achievements. You alone have insight into this. Your aspirations can thus be known, and your discernment…〕

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
之才曷各氣超特之識亦可具見得士如此奚翅場屋光耶
考試官教諭劉　批〔論相道無餘蘊其亦先□□□□〕
考試官教授黃　批〔品藻務求復□□□□□□〕
論古人之相業惟其才求古人之相業惟
其誠天下非才弗理非誠弗動必才與至
誠合一斯周天下之治苟非至誠雖有功
業亦出於事爲之末其何以稱輔弼哉由
是推之則古人之相業可以論其世矣先
儒上蔡謝子曰學必以聖人爲至志在天
===
下必以宰相事業自期降此寧足道乎斯
言也其聖賢志在天下國家乎顧愚何足
以知之嘗聞前古有股肱耳目之托有麯
糱鹽梅之喻是皆君臣相遇其道大行無
俟於論矣姑以後世言之史稱高祖創業
蕭曹爲冠漢宣中興丙魏有聲史綱謂相
假許史以爲重進之不以正謂丙非魏可
並也入可不謹厥始乎史稱房玄齡善謀
杜如晦善斷姚崇善應變以成天下之務
punctuated:
之才曷各氣，超特之識，亦可具見。得士如此，奚翅場屋光耶？
考試官教諭劉，批〔論相道無餘蘊，其亦先□□□□〕
考試官教授黃，批〔品藻務求復□□□□□□〕
論古人之相業，惟其才；求古人之相業，惟其誠。天下非才弗理，非誠弗動。必才與至誠合一，斯周天下之治。苟非至誠，雖有功業，亦出於事爲之末，其何以稱輔弼哉？由是推之，則古人之相業可以論其世矣。先儒上蔡謝子曰：「學必以聖人爲至，志在天下，必以宰相事業自期。降此，寧足道乎？」斯言也，其聖賢志在天下國家乎？顧愚何足以知之？嘗聞前古有股肱耳目之托，有麯糱鹽梅之喻，是皆君臣相遇，其道大行，無俟於論矣。姑以後世言之，史稱高祖創業，蕭曹爲冠；漢宣中興，丙魏有聲。史綱謂相假許史以爲重，進之不以正，謂丙非魏可並也。入可不謹厥始乎？史稱房玄齡善謀，杜如晦善斷，姚崇善應變，以成天下之務。
translation_en:
…his talent [the following wording is garbled: ?] and exceptional insight can also be fully discerned. To obtain a scholar like this brings distinction far beyond the examination hall!

Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: 〔The discussion leaves nothing unexplored concerning the way of the chief minister. He too first … [four illegible characters; meaning uncertain].〕

Examiner Huang, Professor, comments: 〔In appraising them, he strives to recover … [six illegible characters; meaning uncertain].〕

When discussing the achievements of ancient chief ministers, consider their ability; when seeking the source of those achievements, consider their sincerity. Without ability, the realm cannot be ordered; without sincerity, it cannot be moved. Only when ability and utmost sincerity unite can the governance of the realm be made complete. Without utmost sincerity, even meritorious achievements remain merely the incidental results of practical activity. How could this qualify as assisting the sovereign? Reasoning from this, we may discuss the achievements of ancient chief ministers in relation to their times.

The earlier Confucian master Xie of Shangcai said: “In learning, one must take sagehood as the ultimate goal. If one’s aspirations embrace the realm, one must set oneself the standard of a chief minister’s accomplishments. Would anything less even be worth speaking of?” Do not these words express the sages’ and worthies’ concern for the realm and the state? Yet how could someone as ignorant as I adequately understand them?

I have heard that in antiquity rulers entrusted their ministers with serving as their limbs, ears, and eyes, and likened them to ferment and yeast, salt and plums. In all these cases, ruler and minister found their proper counterparts, and their Way prevailed widely; there is no need to discuss them further. Let us speak provisionally of later ages. The histories state that when Gaozu founded his dynasty, Xiao and Cao stood foremost; during the restoration under Emperor Xuan of Han, Bing and Wei enjoyed renown. The Outline of History says that the chief minister borrowed the influence of the Xu and Shi families to enhance his standing, and that his advancement did not follow the proper course. It holds that Bing could not be placed on a par with Wei. Can one fail to be cautious at the outset of entering office [?]? The histories state that Fang Xuanling excelled at planning, Du Ruhui at making decisions, and Yao Chong at responding to changing circumstances so as to accomplish the affairs of the realm…

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
宋璟善守文以持天下之正胡氏謂姚之
善於迎合宋之剛正非姚所可並也人可
不慎厥終乎當大宋之有天下也西戎方
熾之時韓范當其任協謀經畧元昊稱臣
契丹求地之日富弼當其任再聘于燕邊
方以寧乃若歐陽子以行道濟時爲心以
犯顏敢諫爲忠韓魏公言于朝曰歐陽修
今之韓愈也則以文擒功矣仁宗時韓琦
范仲淹富弼並用忠誠一心以成輔相之
===
功英宗時韓琦復相歐陽修爲參政治平
之治最號得人功烈之偉忠誠之著也宋
李沆柄用時中外有上利害一切報罷四
方水旱盜賊不孝惡逆之事奏聞不諱漢
魏相當事嘗以爲古今異宜方今務在奉
行故事或有四方異聞逆賊風雨災變輒
奏言之此劉元城所以稱其最得宰相大
體也若裴晉公忠誠自立將相全材勲高
中夏聲播外夷王沂公之儼然不動正色
punctuated:
宋璟善守文，以持天下之正。胡氏謂姚之善於迎合，宋之剛正，非姚所可並也。人可不慎厥終乎？當大宋之有天下也，西戎方熾之時，韓、范當其任，協謀經畧，元昊稱臣；契丹求地之日，富弼當其任，再聘于燕，邊方以寧。乃若歐陽子，以行道濟時爲心，以犯顏敢諫爲忠。韓魏公言于朝曰：「歐陽修，今之韓愈也。」則以文擒功矣。仁宗時，韓琦、范仲淹、富弼並用，忠誠一心，以成輔相之功；英宗時，韓琦復相，歐陽修爲參政，治平之治，最號得人。功烈之偉，忠誠之著也。
宋李沆柄用時，中外有上利害，一切報罷；四方水旱、盜賊、不孝惡逆之事，奏聞不諱。漢魏相當事，嘗以爲古今異宜，方今務在奉行故事；或有四方異聞、逆賊、風雨災變，輒奏言之。此劉元城所以稱其最得宰相大體也。若裴晉公忠誠自立，將相全材，勲高中夏，聲播外夷；王沂公之儼然不動，正色
translation_en:
…Song Jing excelled at upholding established institutions, thereby maintaining rectitude throughout the realm. Master Hu said that Yao was adept at accommodating others’ wishes, whereas Song’s firmness and uprightness were beyond Yao’s equal. Can one fail to take care over how one ends? When the great Song ruled the realm, at the height of the western Rong’s power, Han Qi and Fan Zhongyan undertook responsibility, jointly planning their strategy until Yuanhao acknowledged himself a subject. When the Qidan demanded territory, Fu Bi undertook responsibility, twice going as envoy to Yan, and the frontier was thereby pacified. As for Master Ouyang, he set his heart on putting the Way into practice and aiding his age, and regarded braving imperial displeasure and daring to remonstrate as loyalty. Han, Duke of Wei, said at court: “Ouyang Xiu is the Han Yu of our day.” Thus he achieved merit through writing [?]. Under Renzong, Han Qi, Fan Zhongyan, and Fu Bi were employed together; loyal and sincere, they worked with one purpose to accomplish the work of assisting the sovereign. Under Yingzong, Han Qi again became chief councilor, and Ouyang Xiu became assistant administrator. The government of the Zhiping era was especially praised for securing the right men. The greatness of their achievements manifested their loyalty and sincerity.
When Li Hang held power under the Song, proposals concerning benefits and harms submitted from within and outside the capital were all rejected. Yet he reported without concealment floods, droughts, banditry, and acts of unfilial conduct and heinous rebellion throughout the realm. When Wei Xiang held office under the Han, he maintained that ancient and present circumstances called for different measures, and that the pressing task was to carry out established precedents. Whenever there were unusual reports from the regions, rebels, or disastrous disturbances of wind and rain, he invariably reported them to the throne. This is why Liu Yuancheng praised him as having the best grasp of the essential responsibilities of a chief councilor. As for Pei, Duke of Jin, he established himself through loyalty and sincerity, possessing the full talents of both general and chief councilor; his achievements were exalted throughout the central realm, and his reputation spread among foreign peoples. Wang, Duke of Yi, remained dignified and unshaken, with a solemn countenance…

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
立朝進用人才必先望實此韓魏公於近
時宰相有取也其他安可盡數耶元豐八
年司馬君實入朝萬人遮道呼曰公無歸
洛留相天子活百姓既相力改新法以澤
天下當時遼人戒曰中國相司馬矣慎無
生事開邊隙相之係天下之重如此司馬
之相業可知矣韓魏公才偏規模小之論
殆亦責備之意與或者以公之罷役法爲
固執然公之心急於救民必欲復祖宗之
===
舊也程子稱之曰誠貫天地行通神明是
矣夫諸子之相業如此審其時究其心則
其功烈庸有取焉孟子曰人不足與適也
政不足間也惟大人爲能格君心之非君
仁莫不仁君義莫不義君正莫不正一正
君而國定矣此萬世之相道也志在天下
者可以知所從事矣執事勿以爲謬謬
第五問
王詢
punctuated:
立朝，進用人才必先望實，此韓魏公於近時宰相有取也。其他安可盡數耶？元豐八年，司馬君實入朝，萬人遮道呼曰：「公無歸洛！留相天子，活百姓！」既相，力改新法，以澤天下。當時遼人戒曰：「中國相司馬矣，慎無生事，開邊隙！」相之係天下之重如此，司馬之相業可知矣。韓魏公才偏規模小之論，殆亦責備之意與？或者以公之罷役法爲固執，然公之心急於救民，必欲復祖宗之舊也。程子稱之曰：「誠貫天地，行通神明。」是矣。夫諸子之相業如此，審其時，究其心，則其功烈庸有取焉。孟子曰：「人不足與適也，政不足間也，惟大人爲能格君心之非。君仁，莫不仁；君義，莫不義；君正，莫不正。一正君而國定矣。」此萬世之相道也。志在天下者，可以知所從事矣。執事勿以爲謬謬。

第五問
王詢
translation_en:
…in his conduct at court, and in advancing talented men he always gave priority to reputation and actual ability: these were qualities that Han, Duke of Wei, esteemed among the chief councilors of recent times. How could all the other examples be enumerated?

In the eighth year of Yuanfeng [1085], Sima Junshi came to court. Ten thousand people blocked the road and cried: “My lord, do not return to Luoyang! Remain as chief councilor to the Son of Heaven and save the people!” Once appointed chief councilor, he worked strenuously to change the New Policies and thereby benefit all under Heaven. At the time, the people of Liao warned one another: “The Central Kingdom has made Sima chief councilor. Take care not to provoke trouble and cause a breach on the frontier!” Such is the weight of a chief councilor’s bearing upon all under Heaven; from this we can understand Sima’s achievements in that office. As for the judgment concerning Han, Duke of Wei, that his talents were limited and his scope narrow [?], was this perhaps also an expression of the desire to demand perfection? Some considered Sima obstinate for abolishing the service law. Yet his heart was set upon urgently rescuing the people, and he was determined to restore the old institutions of the imperial ancestors. Master Cheng praised him, saying: “His sincerity pervaded Heaven and Earth; his conduct reached the spirits.” This was indeed so.

Such were these men’s achievements as chief councilors. If we examine their times and investigate their intentions, we will find merit to esteem in their accomplishments. Mencius said: “Individual men are not worth reproaching, nor particular measures worth criticizing. Only a great man can correct what is wrong in the ruler’s heart. If the ruler is benevolent, none will fail to be benevolent; if the ruler is righteous, none will fail to be righteous; if the ruler is upright, none will fail to be upright. Once the ruler is set right, the state is settled.” This is the way of the chief councilor for all ages. Those whose ambitions embrace all under Heaven can thus know where to direct their efforts. May you, honored sir, not regard these words as mistaken. [The final word is repeated in the transcription.]

Fifth Question
Wang Xun

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
同考試官訓導鄭　批〔籌邊之策非素蘊經濟者不能言乎能援引精當且於鎮兵民兵二事區處甚悉豈書生而知將略者耶〕
考試官教諭劉　批〔究心時務不忘邊慮故能參酌古略以濟變用録以表子用世之學〕
考試官教授黄　批〔論議英發足見胸中甲兵〕
有將兵之道有用兵之宜夫將兵之道無
常焉惟其人而已用兵之宜無他焉惟其
時而已得人以制其機因時以立其法鑒
之於既往審之於將然使慮無不周備無
===
不飭則於安攘之策思過半矣長治久安
之道不有在於是哉方今海内又安國家
閒暇若無所事於兵也執事發策及此豈
非以西蜀有邊陲之患而思所以豫防之
歟愚雖不敏謹掇拾以對夫天生五材誰
能去兵此天理人事之不可無者不然則
箕子之敘疇周公之告君何必以兵師爲
言耶蓋天下雖安忘戰則危古昔盛時未
甞以兵爲諱吾獨慨夫古之兵異乎今之
punctuated:
同考試官訓導鄭批〔籌邊之策，非素蘊經濟者不能言乎？能援引精當，且於鎮兵、民兵二事區處甚悉，豈書生而知將略者耶？〕
考試官教諭劉批〔究心時務，不忘邊慮，故能參酌古略，以濟變用。録以表子用世之學。〕
考試官教授黄批〔論議英發，足見胸中甲兵。〕
有將兵之道，有用兵之宜。夫將兵之道無常焉，惟其人而已；用兵之宜無他焉，惟其時而已。得人以制其機，因時以立其法，鑒之於既往，審之於將然，使慮無不周，備無不飭，則於安攘之策思過半矣。長治久安之道，不有在於是哉？方今海内又安，國家閒暇，若無所事於兵也。執事發策及此，豈非以西蜀有邊陲之患，而思所以豫防之歟？愚雖不敏，謹掇拾以對。夫天生五材，誰能去兵？此天理人事之不可無者。不然，則箕子之敘疇、周公之告君，何必以兵師爲言耶？蓋天下雖安，忘戰則危。古昔盛時，未甞以兵爲諱。吾獨慨夫古之兵異乎今之
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Zheng, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔Could anyone without a longstanding grounding in statecraft speak of strategies for frontier defense? His citations are apt and precise, and his arrangements concerning both garrison troops and militia are particularly thorough. Can this be a scholar who also understands a general’s strategy?〕
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: 〔He applies himself to contemporary affairs and keeps frontier concerns in mind; thus he can weigh ancient strategies and adapt them to changing circumstances. Selected to commend your learning suited to public service.〕
Examiner Huang, Professor, comments: 〔His arguments are spirited and outstanding, amply revealing the armies arrayed within his breast.〕
There is a way to command troops, and there are appropriate circumstances for employing them. The way to command troops has no fixed form: it depends solely on the person. The appropriate employment of troops depends on nothing other than the circumstances of the time. Obtain the right person to control critical opportunities, establish methods suited to the times, take lessons from the past, and carefully assess what is to come. If no consideration is neglected and no preparation left unattended, one will have thought through more than half the strategy for securing peace within and repelling threats from without. Does not the way to lasting order and enduring peace lie here?
At present, all within the seas is again at peace, and the state enjoys repose, as though it had no need to concern itself with military affairs. Your policy question addresses this subject: is it not because western Shu faces troubles along its borders, and you are considering how to forestall them? Though I am slow-witted, I respectfully gather what I can to offer a reply.
Heaven produced the five materials: who can dispense with weapons? They are indispensable to the principles of Heaven and the affairs of humankind. Otherwise, when Jizi set forth the categories of the Great Plan and the Duke of Zhou admonished his ruler, why would they have needed to speak of troops and armies? For even when the realm is at peace, forgetting warfare brings danger. In the flourishing ages of antiquity, military matters were never treated as taboo. What I particularly lament is that the troops of antiquity differed from those of today…

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
兵也已何者聖人作易以坎下坤上爲師
蓋水不離地兵不離民故古者以農爲兵
以利爲將有事則驅之而戰軍師伍兩之
法嚴無事則歸之于田比閭族黨之制密
伏至險於大順藏不測於至静三代以上
未之或改也然必不得已而後用之除殘
去暴保邦衛民如伊尹鳴條之役周公東
山之征此則王者之師能以正衆而非夫
人之所能及也後世此義不講井田廢而
===
兵民分將吏判而兵制壞用兵之宜惟存
乎將耳然勢無常形法難定用善乎岳武
穆之言曰陣而後戰兵法之常運用之妙
存乎一心此眞得將兵之要也蓋善奕者
不視譜善醫者不泥方通其變而已矣矧
兵凶戰危事無大於此者其可不知變而
顧拘於法乎以練兵言之經曰威克厥愛
允濟愛克厥威允罔功兵若貴於嚴也殊
不知寬嚴無定用貴得其中爾是故郭子
punctuated: 兵也已。何者？聖人作易，以坎下坤上爲師。蓋水不離地，兵不離民，故古者以農爲兵，以利爲將。有事則驅之而戰，軍師伍兩之法嚴；無事則歸之于田，比閭族黨之制密。伏至險於大順，藏不測於至静，三代以上未之或改也。然必不得已而後用之，除殘去暴，保邦衛民，如伊尹鳴條之役、周公東山之征，此則王者之師，能以正衆，而非夫人之所能及也。後世此義不講，井田廢而兵民分，將吏判而兵制壞，用兵之宜惟存乎將耳。然勢無常形，法難定用。善乎岳武穆之言曰：「陣而後戰，兵法之常；運用之妙，存乎一心。」此眞得將兵之要也。蓋善奕者不視譜，善醫者不泥方，通其變而已矣。矧兵凶戰危，事無大於此者，其可不知變而顧拘於法乎？以練兵言之，經曰：「威克厥愛，允濟；愛克厥威，允罔功。」兵若貴於嚴也。殊不知寬嚴無定用，貴得其中爾。是故郭子
translation_en:
…the armies of today. Why is this? When the sage composed the Book of Changes, he placed Kan below and Kun above to form the hexagram Shi, “The Army.” Water does not depart from the earth, nor soldiers from the people. Thus, in antiquity, farmers served as soldiers, and “profit” supplied the commanders [?]. When affairs required it, they were led into battle, and the regulations governing armies, divisions, squads of five, and units of twenty-five were strict. When there was no fighting, they returned to the fields, where the system of residential groupings—bi, lü, zu, and dang—was closely organized. Utmost danger lay concealed within utmost compliance, and unfathomable power was stored within perfect stillness. Throughout the Three Dynasties and earlier, this system was never altered. Yet troops were employed only when there was no alternative: to eliminate the cruel, remove the violent, protect the state, and defend the people. Such were Yi Yin’s campaign at Mingtiao and the Duke of Zhou’s expedition to Dongshan. These were the armies of true kings, capable of setting the multitude right—something beyond the reach of ordinary men.

In later ages this principle was no longer studied. With the abolition of the well-field system, soldiers and civilians became separate; with the separation of commanders and civil officials, military institutions fell into ruin. The proper employment of troops then depended solely upon the commander. Yet circumstances have no constant configuration, and methods cannot have a fixed application. Well did Yue Wumu say: “To draw up formations before fighting is the regular rule of warfare; the subtlety of their application rests in the mind alone.” This truly grasps the essentials of commanding troops. A skilled player of weiqi does not consult a manual, and a skilled physician does not cling to prescriptions: they simply adapt to changing circumstances. How much more is this so in warfare, with its ill fortune and danger! No matter is more consequential. Can one fail to understand adaptation and instead remain bound by rules?

Speaking of training troops, the Classic says: “When authority prevails over affection, success is assured; when affection prevails over authority, there will assuredly be no achievement.” It would seem that strictness is what matters in military affairs. Yet this overlooks the fact that neither leniency nor strictness has a fixed application: what matters is attaining the proper balance. Thus Guo Zi…

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
儀治軍以寛而士卒歸心以挫吐番之衆
李光弼治軍以嚴而旌旗動色以制思明
之强事異而功同者何也蓋結以恩義則
寛非失之縱肅其號令則嚴非失之苛此
軍士所以樂子儀之寛而不忍犯憚光弼
之嚴而不敢犯也兵烏得而不練哉以選
兵言之傳曰財匱於兵衆力分於將多兵
若宜於省也殊不知多寡無定數貴得其
精爾是故蕭俛段文昌嘗省兵於唐矣乃
===
致軍士爲盜而貽禍國家文彥博龐籍嘗
省兵於宋矣乃致軍士精强而用蘇邊儲
事同而功異者何也蓋仁宗之時公私困
竭正宜省兵以息民也選精壯而退老弱
邊儲安得而不蘇穆宗之時兩河略定正
宜養兵以善後也限逃亡而落軍籍盜賊
安得而不生此文彥博龐籍之所爲固非
施昌言李昭亮之可及而蕭俛段文昌之
所爲秖足以召朱克融王庭湊之亂也夫
punctuated: 儀治軍以寛，而士卒歸心，以挫吐番之衆；李光弼治軍以嚴，而旌旗動色，以制思明之强。事異而功同者，何也？蓋結以恩義，則寛非失之縱；肅其號令，則嚴非失之苛。此軍士所以樂子儀之寛而不忍犯，憚光弼之嚴而不敢犯也。兵烏得而不練哉？以選兵言之，傳曰：「財匱於兵衆，力分於將多。」兵若宜於省也，殊不知多寡無定數，貴得其精爾。是故蕭俛、段文昌嘗省兵於唐矣，乃致軍士爲盜，而貽禍國家；文彥博、龐籍嘗省兵於宋矣，乃致軍士精强，而用蘇邊儲。事同而功異者，何也？蓋仁宗之時，公私困竭，正宜省兵以息民也。選精壯而退老弱，邊儲安得而不蘇？穆宗之時，兩河略定，正宜養兵以善後也。限逃亡而落軍籍，盜賊安得而不生？此文彥博、龐籍之所爲，固非施昌言、李昭亮之可及，而蕭俛、段文昌之所爲，秖足以召朱克融、王庭湊之亂也。夫
translation_en:
…Guo Ziyi governed his army with leniency, winning the soldiers’ allegiance and thereby defeating the forces of Tubo. Li Guangbi governed his army with strictness, lending even its banners an imposing appearance and thereby checking Shi Siming’s strength. Why did different measures achieve the same success? When men are bound together through kindness and righteousness, leniency does not lapse into indulgence; when commands are enforced with discipline, strictness does not lapse into harshness. This is why the soldiers welcomed Ziyi’s leniency and could not bear to violate his orders, while they dreaded Guangbi’s strictness and dared not violate his orders. How could troops thus governed fail to be well trained?

As for selecting troops, a transmitted text says: “Resources are exhausted by numerous soldiers; strength is divided by numerous commanders.” It would seem that troops ought to be reduced. Yet this overlooks the fact that there is no fixed number, large or small: what matters is securing the best men. Thus Xiao Mian and Duan Wenchang once reduced troop numbers under the Tang, only to drive soldiers into banditry and bring calamity upon the state. Wen Yanbo and Pang Ji once reduced troop numbers under the Song, with the result that the soldiers became picked and powerful, and frontier supplies were consequently replenished. Why did the same measure produce different results?

In Renzong’s time, public and private resources were strained and exhausted: it was precisely the right time to reduce troops and give the people respite. By selecting the vigorous and able and discharging the old and weak, how could frontier supplies fail to recover? In Muzong’s time, the Lianghe region had only just been largely pacified: it was precisely the right time to maintain troops so as to secure the aftermath. By setting a time limit for deserters [?] and striking them from the military rolls, how could banditry fail to arise? What Wen Yanbo and Pang Ji accomplished was certainly beyond the reach of Shi Changyan and Li Zhaoliang, whereas what Xiao Mian and Duan Wenchang did served only to bring on the rebellions of Zhu Kerong and Wang Tingcou. Now…

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
豈可以槩論哉是則臨機應變因時制宜
信皆存乎將之一心而非常法之所能拘
也雖然法不外乎正奇兵不外乎攻守蓋
攻討之兵用於暫鎮守之兵用於久方今
西蜀邊陲威茂松潘尤爲要害戎夷出沒
無歲無之用鎮守之兵爲久安之策誠不
可以不豫也稽之於古陸宣公言之備矣
彼誠見夫當時散徵士卒分戍邊陲更代
往來以爲守備不量性習不辨土宜邀其
===
所不能強其所不欲求廣其數而不考其
用將致其力而不察其情可以爲羽衛之
儀而無益於備邊之實也故欲罷更番之
制置鎮守之兵類其部伍安其室家給以
牛種務獎營田既息踐更徵發之煩且無
幸灾苟免之弊寇至則人自爲戰時至則
家自力農出則足兵居則足食與夫倏來
忽往者不可同等而論矣是雖一時之言
要之古今屯戍防邊利害無出於此茲欲
punctuated: 豈可以槩論哉？是則臨機應變，因時制宜，信皆存乎將之一心，而非常法之所能拘也。雖然，法不外乎正奇，兵不外乎攻守。蓋攻討之兵用於暫，鎮守之兵用於久。方今西蜀邊陲，威、茂、松潘尤爲要害，戎夷出沒，無歲無之。用鎮守之兵爲久安之策，誠不可以不豫也。稽之於古，陸宣公言之備矣。彼誠見夫當時散徵士卒，分戍邊陲，更代往來，以爲守備，不量性習，不辨土宜，邀其所不能，強其所不欲，求廣其數而不考其用，將致其力而不察其情，可以爲羽衛之儀，而無益於備邊之實也。故欲罷更番之制，置鎮守之兵，類其部伍，安其室家，給以牛種，務獎營田。既息踐更徵發之煩，且無幸灾苟免之弊。寇至則人自爲戰，時至則家自力農，出則足兵，居則足食，與夫倏來忽往者不可同等而論矣。是雖一時之言，要之古今屯戍防邊，利害無出於此。茲欲
translation_en:
…How could these cases be judged indiscriminately? Thus, responding to changing circumstances as they arise and adopting measures suited to the times truly depend entirely upon the commander's judgment; fixed rules cannot constrain them. Nevertheless, methods do not extend beyond orthodox and unorthodox operations, nor military activity beyond attack and defense. Troops used for offensive campaigns serve a temporary purpose; troops stationed in garrisons serve a lasting one. Today, on the frontier of western Shu, Wei, Mao, and Songpan are especially vital strategic points. Not a year passes without incursions by the Rong and Yi. We must indeed prepare in advance to employ permanent garrison troops as a means of securing lasting peace.

Looking to the past, we find that Lu Xuangong (Lu Zhi) discussed this fully. He clearly perceived that, in his day, soldiers were recruited from scattered places and assigned to separate frontier garrisons, coming and going in successive rotations to provide defense. No consideration was given to their dispositions and accustomed ways, nor were local conditions distinguished. They were required to do what they could not and compelled to do what they did not wish to do. Numbers were increased without examining their usefulness, and their exertions were demanded without considering their circumstances. Such troops could furnish the ceremonial display of imperial guards, but contributed nothing to the actual defense of the frontier.

He therefore wished to abolish the system of rotating service and establish permanent garrison troops, organize them into units, settle their families, provide them with oxen and seed, and make a concerted effort to encourage cultivation. This would both end the burdens of rotational service and conscription and eliminate the abuses of welcoming calamity as an opportunity to evade duty. When invaders arrived, each man would fight on his own initiative; when the farming season arrived, each household would devote its efforts to cultivation. On deployment there would be sufficient troops; at home there would be sufficient food. Such men could not be placed on the same footing as those who arrived and departed in haste.

Although these words addressed the circumstances of one particular time, in essence the benefits and drawbacks of garrisoning and defending the frontier, past and present, do not extend beyond what they describe. Now, wishing to…

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
舉而行之莫若分衞所之精軍爲戍守之
久計授以屯田繼以糧餉齊其器械脩其
樓櫓而又嚴其科索之禁節其工役之勞
使之定其志而樂其居期以力衰而後代
則敵情地勢無不周知充國金城之勝李
牧鴈門之威可以復見於今矣又何外夷
之足患哉雖然外固當重也而内亦不可
以或輕宋儒范祖禹謂後世郡縣古之諸
侯也委之以土地人民而不與兵是以匹
===
夫而守一州也烏伸偁討淮蔡之後而以
三州之兵付之刺史者得非有見於河朔
之拒命由於鎭將之專擅也歟今日郡縣
民兵之設似亦其策之遺意也但今天下
之民疲於差占戍守之害亦已甚矣兹欲
釐而正之莫若於常役之中選驍勇之士
籍其名數定其年貌禁其差占免其戍守
而又教之以坐作進退之法親上死長之
義使之安其鄉而習其業期以力衰而後
punctuated:
舉而行之，莫若分衞所之精軍，爲戍守之久計，授以屯田，繼以糧餉，齊其器械，脩其樓櫓，而又嚴其科索之禁，節其工役之勞，使之定其志而樂其居，期以力衰而後代，則敵情地勢無不周知。充國金城之勝，李牧鴈門之威，可以復見於今矣，又何外夷之足患哉！

雖然，外固當重也，而内亦不可以或輕。宋儒范祖禹謂：「後世郡縣，古之諸侯也。委之以土地人民而不與兵，是以匹夫而守一州也。」烏伸偁討淮蔡之後，而以三州之兵付之刺史者，得非有見於河朔之拒命，由於鎭將之專擅也歟？今日郡縣民兵之設，似亦其策之遺意也。但今天下之民，疲於差占、戍守之害，亦已甚矣。兹欲釐而正之，莫若於常役之中選驍勇之士，籍其名數，定其年貌，禁其差占，免其戍守，而又教之以坐作進退之法、親上死長之義，使之安其鄉而習其業，期以力衰而後
translation_en:
…to put this into practice, nothing would be better than to assign selected troops from the guards and battalions to a long-term plan for garrison defense. Give them military farmland, follow this with grain and pay, put their weapons and equipment in order, and repair their watchtowers and defensive structures. Strictly enforce prohibitions against exactions and reduce the burden of construction labor, so that their minds are settled and they take pleasure in their homes, with replacement to come only when their strength declines. They would then become thoroughly familiar with the enemy’s circumstances and the terrain. Chongguo’s victory at Jincheng and Li Mu’s might at Yanmen could be seen again today. What cause would there then be to fear the foreign peoples beyond our borders?

Nevertheless, although external defense certainly deserves attention, internal affairs must never be treated lightly. The Song Confucian scholar Fan Zuyu said: “The prefectures and counties of later ages are the feudal lords of antiquity. To entrust them with land and people but give them no troops is to have an ordinary man defend an entire prefecture.” After campaigning against Huai and Cai, Wu Shencheng [?] entrusted the troops of three prefectures to their prefects. Was this not because he recognized that Heshuo’s defiance of imperial commands arose from the unchecked power of its garrison commanders? Today’s establishment of militias in the prefectures and counties likewise seems to preserve something of the intent of that policy. Yet the people throughout the realm have already suffered grievously from being requisitioned for service and appropriated for private use, and from garrison duties. To rectify these abuses, nothing would be better than to select brave and vigorous men from among those liable for regular service, register their names and numbers, ascertain their ages and physical descriptions, forbid their requisition or appropriation for other service, and exempt them from garrison duties. Teach them the methods of sitting and rising, advancing and retreating, and the duty of cherishing their superiors and dying for their commanders. Let them live securely in their home communities and practice their occupations, with the stipulated time coming only after their strength has declined…

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
代則有勇知方無不恭命黃帝丘乘之法
周官井牧之制可以復見於今矣又何內
變之足憂哉夫如是則有采薇天保之風
而無尾大中乾之弊不獨可行於西蜀一
隅推之天下皆可也雖然天下無常治之
法貴乎有常治之人故得一良將則無不
可用之軍得一良吏則無不可用之民選
將任官其機實係於部使其本又在於
朝廷也執事倘不以愚言爲迂願轉聞于
上
punctuated: 代，則有勇知方，無不恭命。黃帝丘乘之法、周官井牧之制，可以復見於今矣，又何內變之足憂哉？夫如是，則有《采薇》《天保》之風，而無尾大中乾之弊。不獨可行於西蜀一隅，推之天下皆可也。雖然，天下無常治之法，貴乎有常治之人。故得一良將，則無不可用之軍；得一良吏，則無不可用之民。選將任官，其機實係於部使，其本又在於朝廷也。執事倘不以愚言爲迂，願轉聞于上。
translation_en:
…be replaced; then they will possess courage and understand their proper duties, and all will respectfully obey commands. The Yellow Emperor’s system of chariot levies by territorial units (qiu), and the system of well-fields and pastoral allotments in the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan), may thus be seen again today. What internal disturbances would then be worth fearing? In this way, there would be the spirit of “Gathering Ferns” (Caiwei) and “Heaven Protects” (Tianbao), without the defects of an overgrown periphery and an exhausted center. This could be implemented not only in the single region of western Shu, but throughout the realm.

Nevertheless, there is no method that invariably secures order in the realm; what matters is having people who consistently govern well. Thus, with one good general, no troops are unusable; with one good official, no people are unusable. The crucial responsibility for selecting generals and appointing officials lies with the regional commissioners, while its ultimate foundation rests with the imperial court. If you, sir, do not consider my humble words impractical, I ask that you convey them to His Majesty.

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
四川鄉試録後序
我
朝純用孔子之道以敎天下以
成就人才爲大務三年大比
明試以言以求眞才試之言
所以考其行也丁酉四川鄉
試〔邦〕〔釆〕與考校之任我
===
皇上以敬一作人四方風動維蜀
之士其文焯矣文之焯者行
之稽也古者才德一而仕以
爲人後世才德二而仕以爲
己蓋知仁義禮天德也古今
人心之所同也知則能周萬
物仁則能愛義則能正禮則
punctuated:
四川鄉試録後序

我朝純用孔子之道以敎天下，以成就人才爲大務。三年大比，明試以言，以求眞才。試之言，所以考其行也。丁酉四川鄉試，〔邦〕〔釆〕與考校之任。我皇上以敬一作人，四方風動。維蜀之士，其文焯矣。文之焯者，行之稽也。古者才德一，而仕以爲人；後世才德二，而仕以爲己。蓋知仁義禮，天德也，古今人心之所同也。知則能周萬物，仁則能愛，義則能正，禮則
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Sichuan Provincial Examination

Our dynasty teaches all under Heaven exclusively through the Way of Confucius and makes the cultivation of talent its chief concern. Every three years, the great examination is held: candidates are tested discerningly through their words, to seek true talent. Testing their words is a means of examining their conduct. In the dingyou year [1537], I, Bangcai 〔邦〕〔釆〕, shared responsibility for examining and assessing candidates in the Sichuan Provincial Examination. Our emperor cultivates men through reverent single-mindedness, and all quarters respond to his influence. As for the scholars of Shu [Sichuan], their compositions are indeed brilliant. The brilliance of their compositions provides evidence by which to assess their conduct. In antiquity, talent and virtue were one, and men entered office for the sake of others; in later ages, talent and virtue became divided, and men entered office for their own sake. Wisdom, benevolence, righteousness, and ritual propriety are virtues endowed by Heaven, common to human hearts in antiquity and today. Through wisdom one can comprehend the myriad things; through benevolence one can love; through righteousness one can rectify; through ritual propriety…

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
能理才者其德之用乎維彼
才難本末具舉降此則舉其
大者遺其細盡其小者惛於
大乃若曲謹小廉非德也周
羅便捷非才也是故器使者
用人者之責也任重道遠者
自立之志也仕所以推行其
===
道必天德在我而時出之當
行而行於已不與斯可以決
天下之大疑處天下之大事
矣故曰艮其背不獲其身行
其庭不見其人雖然宇宙內
事皆吾分內事事不一也豈
無至要以一萬事之不一者
punctuated: 能理。才者，其德之用乎？維彼才難，本末具舉；降此，則舉其大者，遺其細；盡其小者，惛於大。乃若曲謹小廉，非德也；周羅便捷，非才也。是故器使者，用人者之責也；任重道遠者，自立之志也。仕所以推行其道，必天德在我，而時出之，當行而行，於已不與，斯可以決天下之大疑，處天下之大事矣。故曰：「艮其背，不獲其身；行其庭，不見其人。」雖然，宇宙內事，皆吾分內事。事不一也，豈無至要以一萬事之不一者
translation_en: …can bring order. Is talent not the working of one’s virtue? Truly, such talent is rare: it encompasses both root and branch. Below this level, some grasp the greater matters but overlook the finer points; others exhaust their efforts on small matters but remain confused about the great ones. Scrupulousness over trifles and petty incorruptibility are not virtue; encompassing cleverness and quick facility [?] are not talent. Thus, employing people according to their capacities is the responsibility of those who appoint them; taking up a heavy burden on a long journey expresses the resolve of those who establish themselves. Holding office is the means of putting one’s Way into practice. One must possess Heaven-given virtue within oneself and manifest it as circumstances require, acting when action is called for, without involving one’s private self [?]. Only then can one resolve the world’s great uncertainties and manage its great affairs. Hence the saying: “Keeping his back still, he does not apprehend his own body; walking in his courtyard, he does not see its people.” Nevertheless, all affairs within the universe fall within the scope of my own responsibility. Affairs are diverse: could there be no supremely essential principle by which to unify the diversity of the myriad affairs…

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
乎研幾者任重道遠之要哉
吾夫子曰幾者動之微而朱
子謂精粗隱顯一時穿透此
聖學心傳之的也爾多士實
從事於斯而致審焉則必動
以天而爲
上爲德爲下爲民之道皆由此出
===
終身用之有不能盡者矣夫
然則上不負
天子下不負所學而〔邦 采〕等以人
報
國之心庶乎可以少慰矣乎乃
於賢能之書也敬敘於后以
端其志而示之要焉
punctuated: 乎？研幾者，任重道遠之要哉！吾夫子曰：「幾者，動之微。」而朱子謂「精粗隱顯，一時穿透」，此聖學心傳之的也。爾多士實從事於斯而致審焉，則必動以天，而爲上爲德、爲下爲民之道，皆由此出，終身用之，有不能盡者矣夫！然則上不負天子，下不負所學，而〔邦 采〕等以人報國之心，庶乎可以少慰矣乎！乃於賢能之書也，敬敘於后，以端其志而示之要焉。
translation_en:
…? Discerning the first stirrings is indeed the essential means of bearing a heavy responsibility over a long journey! Our Master said, “The first stirrings are the subtle beginnings of movement.” Master Zhu spoke of “penetrating the refined and the coarse, the hidden and the manifest, all at once.” This is the true aim of the transmission from mind to mind of the sages’ learning. If you scholars truly devote yourselves to this and examine it with utmost care, your actions will assuredly accord with Heaven. From this will emerge all the ways of acting for those above and for virtue, and for those below and for the people [?]. Even a lifetime of application will not exhaust them!

Then you will neither fail the Son of Heaven above nor betray what you have learned. And the hope that we, Bangcai and the others, cherish—to repay the state by supplying worthy men—may perhaps find some small consolation! Thus I respectfully append this preface to the record of the worthy and capable, to set their aspirations straight and show them what is essential.

title: 嘉靖十六年四川鄉試錄
text:
福建建寧府壽寧縣儒學教
諭劉〔邦采〕謹序
punctuated: 福建建寧府壽寧縣儒學教諭劉〔邦采〕謹序。
